Their platform offers real-time vehicle tracking, driver behavior analytics, smart dash cameras, field service management, and compliance tools, helping companies improve safety, efficiency, and accountability while reducing operational costs.

providers.name: Aatmunn
providers.description: Aatmunn (formerly Guardhat, founded 2014 in Detroit and headquartered in Livonia, Michigan) is an industrial safety and asset intelligence platform for frontline and deskless workers. Its SPANR / Industrial Internet of People (IIoP) platform unifies workers, workplaces, and assets into one real-time system, connecting devices from any manufacturer and layering AI-driven insights for predictive hazard detection, emergency response, inspections, and compliance. Products include Inspections, Lone Worker Safety, Human Condition Monitoring, Gas Detection, Control Access Zoning, and Asset Tracking, serving 250+ companies across high-risk industries such as oil & gas, chemicals, mining & infrastructure, manufacturing, utilities, and warehousing & logistics. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and is maintained by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; Aatmunn publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Amazfit
providers.description: Zepp Health, operating under the Amazfit brand, develops wearable devices and health-focused applications that empower individuals to monitor and improve their well‑being. Their product lineup includes smartwatches, fitness trackers, and a companion mobile app offering features such as heart‑rate monitoring, sleep analysis, activity tracking, and personalized health insights. Zepp Health emphasizes seamless integration of hardware and software to deliver an engaging user experience that inspires joy and promotes a healthier lifestyle.

providers.name: Energy Robotics
providers.description: Energy Robotics GmbH, now trading as Korial, is a Darmstadt, Germany enterprise AI platform (spun out of TU Darmstadt robotics research) for fully autonomous industrial operations. It is hardware-agnostic, unifying mixed-vendor robots, legged and tracked ground robots, drones, fixed cameras, and field sensors into a single governed AI operating layer that turns live telemetry into verified insight and orchestrated action across oil & gas, chemicals, power & utilities, and critical infrastructure. The platform spans four modules: Kore (the AI core with LLM, agentic workflows, embedded AI skills, and fleet/device supervision), Connect (an integration backbone exposing bidirectional governed APIs into ERP, EAM, SCADA, historians and ICS/OT systems), Recreate (digital twins and mission simulation), and Sustain (support, onboarding, and managed mission execution). Korial reports 1,000,000+ autonomous inspections, 100+ global deployments, and named customers including Shell, bp, Repsol, Petrobras, Pluspetrol, Chevron, E.ON, Evonik, BASF, and Merck. Rebranded from Energy Robotics GmbH on 4 May 2026.

providers.name: Infinitum
providers.description: Infinitum (formerly Infinitum Electric) is an Austin, Texas motor manufacturer, founded in 2016 by Ben Schuler, that builds the Aircore EC+ family of air-core printed-circuit-board (PCB) stator electric motors along with integrated fan and pump systems, Active Front End (AFE) drives, power generation packages and off-road traction motors for data centers, commercial and industrial buildings, water and wastewater treatment, agriculture and mobility. Its software surface is operator tooling rather than a developer platform: the I-con motor control application for commissioning, monitoring and diagnostics, a browser-based Motor Selection Tool (MST) and Fan Selection Tool (FST), an IoT kit for telemetry, and BACnet, Modbus and analog/digital field integration on the motor itself. Infinitum does document an HTTP API for the selection tools - fan selection, motor selection and fan chart endpoints - but the reference is served behind an account sign-in and the company states that detailed API documentation and advanced integration require a signed NDA and a commercial agreement, so no public contract is reachable.

providers.name: openHAB
providers.description: openHAB is an open-source, vendor‑agnostic home automation platform that enables users to integrate a wide range of smart devices and technologies into a unified system. It offers a flexible architecture, extensive documentation, and a vibrant community supporting installation, configuration, and automation across Linux, Windows, macOS, and embedded hardware.

providers.name: Airwave
providers.description: Airwave (Indianapolis, founded 2022) is a field intelligence platform for industrial and field-service technicians: ANSI Z87+ smart safety glasses with a built-in camera, microphone and speakers record the job, and the Airwave software turns the footage into inspection reports, job hazard analyses, customer summaries and searchable job notes, with an AI assistant ("Blue") answering questions from uploaded manuals, parts lists and team knowledge. The pricing page lists API integrations (ERP, CRM, CMMS) and an Airwave Glasses SDK only in the custom-priced Video Intelligence tier behind a sales conversation; no public developer documentation, API reference or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Deeploi
providers.description: Deeploi (deeploi GmbH) is a Berlin-based all-in-one IT management (ITSM) platform for mid-sized businesses and startups, primarily across the DACH region. It centralizes employee onboarding and offboarding, device and inventory management, software and license/account administration, cybersecurity and compliance policies, and unlimited expert IT support in a single dashboard priced per active employee. Deeploi operates an Information Security Management System aligned with ISO/IEC 27001 and is GDPR compliant, publishing its posture through a Kertos-powered Trust Center. The company is backed by Atomico. Deeploi does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance)
providers.description: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance) is a Chicago-based commercial trucking insurance company delivering modern, data-driven coverage for small and mid-size fleet operators. Its flagship HDVI Shift product uses integrated telematics and safety data to dynamically price premiums, rewarding safe driving with monthly discounts of up to 20 percent, and its Fleet Portal gives fleets tools to improve safety, reduce risk, maintain compliance, and lower costs. HDVI was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it operates a customer-facing Fleet Portal and telematics/ELD/dash-cam partner integrations rather than an open developer program. This profile captures the company's real public identity, its published llms.txt, its SOC 2 Type 2 compliance posture, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Highway9
providers.description: Highway 9 Networks is a Silicon Valley company delivering AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service through its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform. The platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), a distributed 5G core and edge AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device/workload groupings (Mobile Zones) to give enterprises deterministic, ultra-reliable private mobile networks and in-building cellular coverage. It targets manufacturing and warehousing (autonomous robots, drones, logistics), higher education (AI labs and research), and energy (predictive maintenance, remote operations). The Mobile Center Streaming APIs let partners integrate configuration, device management, monitoring, analytics, and operational workflows with the platform. Founded by an ex-VMware team behind NSX/SDN, hybrid cloud, and the Telco 5G/Edge cloud platform.

providers.name: Hive Power
providers.description: Hive Power SA is a Swiss software company (Manno, Ticino) building FLEXO, a Flexibility Orchestrator that connects distributed energy assets — electric vehicles, stationary batteries, solar systems, and smart appliances — to electricity markets and grid services. FLEXO pairs an AI optimization engine (weather, price, and behavior forecasting) with a REST API mid-layer and end-user/admin interfaces to deliver smart charging (V1G/V2G/V2X), virtual power plant (VPP) aggregation, battery monetization, energy-community management, and local optimization. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating EVs, chargers, batteries, and solar/EMS via IoT platforms and manufacturer APIs (Enode, ABB, Huawei, LG, SMA, Easee, ChargePoint) and protocols such as MODBUS, MQTT, and OCPP. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: By Miles
providers.description: By Miles is a London-based insurtech that pioneered pay-by-mile motor insurance in the United Kingdom, founded in 2016 for low-mileage drivers who cover under roughly 7,000 miles a year. Its single line of business is UK private motor (personal lines property and casualty), priced as a fixed annual premium covering the parked car plus a per-mile charge for the distance actually driven. Mileage is measured either by the OBD-II "Miles Tracker" telematics dongle or, on its "connect" trackerless policies, by pulling odometer data directly from the manufacturer's connected-car platform after the driver links a Tesla, Ford or Mercedes-Benz account. By Miles was acquired by Direct Line Group in April 2023 and, following Aviva's acquisition of Direct Line Group, has been wound down — it stopped quoting new business and, from 6 January 2026, stopped offering renewal quotes to existing customers. Its API posture is that of a pure API CONSUMER, not a producer: it was the first UK insurtech directly authorised by the FCA as an AISP/PISP to consume Open Banking APIs (January 2020), and it consumes OEM connected-car APIs for mileage, but it publishes no public self-serve developer portal, no reference documentation, no OpenAPI, no Postman collection and no webhook catalogue. The only integration surface is a partnerships email address and a private AWS API Gateway host serving its own mobile app, so this record is a partner-gated stub by design.

providers.name: HyBird
providers.description: HyBird is an industrial software company behind Clarity, a modular Industrial Operating System built on a self-updating, photorealistic living digital twin. Clarity unifies 3D twin and document management, engineering and management of change, P&ID management, intelligent (preventive, predictive, reactive) maintenance, EHS, robotic inspection with AI defect detection, structural integrity, asset performance monitoring, and an AR-guided connected workforce for heavy industries such as oil & gas, cement and building materials, energy, terminals, and nuclear. It integrates with EAM/CMMS platforms including SAP PM, S/4HANA, Microsoft Dynamics, and IBM Maximo. HyBird is a Techstars-backed company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Synop
providers.description: Synop is a software platform for commercial electric vehicle fleet charging and energy management, describing itself as "the operating system for commercial EV fleets." Its hardware- and software-agnostic platform integrates vehicles, chargers, and the grid across the U.S. and Europe, spanning charge management (remote charger control, real-time alerts, EVSE interoperability across 100+ charging station models), energy management (AI-based load and time-of-use optimization, curtailment, demand response, and vehicle-to-grid events), vehicle management (state-of-charge and efficiency via telematics), payment management (billing, driver reimbursement, and transaction reporting), utility management, and SynopLink edge connectivity for site-level operations. Synop cites 500+ MWh under management across 800+ commercial depots. Its API integrations surface live time-of-use rate data and export reimbursement data to accounting and expense systems, though the developer documentation is a password-gated ReadMe admin guide rather than a public developer portal.

providers.name: Autofleet
providers.description: Autofleet is a fleet and mobility optimization platform founded in 2018 in Tel Aviv by Kobi Eisenberg and Dor Shay, and since 2024 an independently operated, wholly owned subsidiary of Element Fleet Management Corp. (TSX: EFN). Its AI-driven software plans, dispatches, routes and simulates vehicle-based operations across postal and parcel delivery, last-mile logistics, rental and car sharing, corporate motor pools, microtransit, NEMT and school transport, taxi and rideshare, field service, and autonomous mobility, in more than 20 countries. The platform is sold as an integration hub — Autofleet markets a public API and webhooks for connecting telematics, GPS, keyless access, maintenance, booking, dispatch, CRM and ERP systems — and adds Nova, a fleet-specific generative AI layer for natural-language operational questions. The API gateway is live at api.autofleet.io, but the developer reference at docs.autofleet.io is a password-protected ReadMe hub, so no machine-readable contract is publicly retrievable.

providers.name: Cardiosense
providers.description: Cardiosense, Inc. is a Chicago-based medical technology company developing AI-powered, noninvasive cardiac hemodynamic monitoring for heart failure care. Its CardioTag device is a wearable chest biosensor that captures seismocardiographic (SCG), electrocardiographic (ECG) and photoplethysmographic (PPG) signals, and its PCWP Analysis Software is a standalone AI software-as-a-medical-device that estimates Pulmonary Capillary Wedge Pressure from those signals without right heart catheterization or an implantable sensor. Both are authorized by the FDA as Class II medical devices, and the company received an FDA De Novo classification. Cardiosense publishes no developer program, SDK or API specification; its only machine-readable surfaces are an authored llms.txt, an extended AI-context document, an explicit AI-crawler allowance in robots.txt, and an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol server on its own host.

providers.name: Owletcare
providers.description: Owlet (Owletcare) is a baby-monitoring technology company that builds connected-nursery hardware and companion apps for parents. Its flagship Dream Sock is marketed as an FDA-cleared smart baby monitor that tracks a sleeping infant's pulse rate, oxygen levels, movement and sleep patterns, alongside the Dream Sight HD video monitor and the combined Dream Duo system. Products pair a wearable/camera with the Owlet Dream mobile app for real-time wellness insights and notifications. The consumer storefront at owletcare.com runs on Shopify; sign-in is handled by Shopify's Customer Account API (OIDC/OAuth), and Owlet does not currently publish a first-party developer API program. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from Owlet's public web surface.

providers.name: RealWear
providers.description: RealWear builds rugged, hands-free head-mounted and assisted-reality wearable computers (the Navigator series and HMT-1) for frontline and industrial workers in energy, manufacturing, field service, and utilities. Its Android-based devices are operated entirely by voice through the on-device WearHF service, which turns any Android app's touch controls into voice commands and can be tuned with WearML voice directives placed in UI metadata — so there is no separate SDK to install. RealWear now also ships Ari, a voice-first AI assistant (Ari OS and the Ari Cloud dashboard) with Microsoft connectors (Teams, Outlook email and calendar, contacts, Copilot), skills, and cross-session memory. Developers extend the platform with native Android, Unity, React Native, Cordova, Xamarin, and HTML apps plus custom Ari skills. This profile was surfaced as a Foundry Group portfolio company and enriched from RealWear's public developer surface.

providers.name: Brava Home
providers.description: Brava Home, Inc. is a Redwood City, California consumer-hardware company that makes the Brava smart countertop oven — a connected cooking appliance that uses its patented Pure Light infrared-lamp technology to sear, bake, air-fry, dehydrate, toast, reheat, and slow-cook, controlled through the Brava Home mobile app and a guided recipe platform. Brava sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at shop.brava.com. Brava does not publish a public developer/device API; its machine-facing surface is agentic commerce — the storefront exposes a Shopify-native Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) profile at /.well-known/ucp and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint so shopping agents can search the catalog, build carts, and drive buyer-approved checkout. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a cowboy-ventures portfolio lead, this profile has been enriched from Brava's real public surface.

providers.name: Heex Technologies
providers.description: Heex Technologies builds the Smart-Data Platform, an event-based data management solution for autonomous systems, robotics, and ADAS/AD vehicles. Instead of moving raw big data off fleets, Heex lets engineering teams define Smart Events with pre-set triggers so software agents capture only the most relevant, context-rich data ("Smart-Data") directly at the edge or in the cloud. The platform spans a Heex Agent/SDK deployed on robots and vehicles (Ubuntu x86_64/ARM, ROS/ROS2), a Heex CLI for operating the SDK and Heex Cloud, and a web platform for triggers, events, recordings, and fleet monitoring. It is used across AMRs, industrial robots, smart mobility, and off-road autonomy, with customers and partners including NVIDIA, Siemens, RATP, Vinci, Stanley Robotics, Apex.AI and Helm.AI. Backed by Techstars, Google for Startups, and AWS Activate.

providers.name: HumanFirst
providers.description: HumanFirst is a digital health measurement company whose Atlas platform helps clinical research and life-sciences teams evaluate, select, and operationalize sensor-based digital health technologies — wearables, connected devices, and digital biomarkers — for clinical trials and real-world evidence. Atlas curates a knowledge network of digital measures, connected devices, and the published evidence behind them so sponsors and CROs can choose fit-for-purpose measures. HumanFirst is now part of ICON plc and integrated into ICON's Digital Health Technologies (DHT) capabilities. The Atlas platform is delivered as an authenticated web application at app.gohumanfirst.com; the company does not currently publish a public developer API. This profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Medigate
providers.description: Medigate was a healthcare IoT / connected-medical-device cybersecurity company (headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, backed by Partech and others) that built the first security platform dedicated to healthcare IoT — device discovery, risk assessment, and clinically-aware network segmentation for hospitals. Claroty completed its acquisition of Medigate on 2022-01-10 and folded the product into "Claroty xDome for Healthcare"; the standalone brand is retired and medigate.io now redirects to claroty.com. A residual customer-facing REST API remains live at api.medigate.io (with a password-gated interactive reference at api.medigate.io/docs) that integrations use to pull device inventory, device groups, and device risk scores.

providers.name: Microsoft Surface
providers.description: Microsoft Surface is a line of touchscreen-based personal computers and accessories designed and developed by Microsoft. Surface provides enterprise management APIs through UEFI configuration and Intune integration for managing Surface devices at scale.

providers.name: NimaSensor
providers.description: NIMA (originally 6SensorLabs, founded by MIT alumni Shireen Yates and Scott Sundvor) makes a portable, consumer-use gluten detection sensor for people living with celiac disease and gluten sensitivity. A pea-sized food sample is loaded into a single-use capsule, inserted into the handheld NIMA Sensor, and returns a clear result in about three minutes, detecting gluten down to 10 ppm. The product relaunched in 2025-2026 with investment from RA Capital Management, pairing a next-generation sensor with newly engineered test capsules and the NIMA Now app. NIMA is a consumer hardware and e-commerce company (storefront hosted on Shopify), not a developer-API provider - it exposes no first-party public developer API. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Alif Semiconductor
providers.description: Alif Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Pleasanton, California with engineering operations in Grenoble, France. It designs secure, AI/ML-enabled 32-bit microcontrollers and fusion processors for edge computing, built around Arm Cortex-M55 cores and dedicated Arm Ethos-U55 Neural Processing Units. Its Ensemble (E1C, E1, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8) and Balletto (B1) product families target battery-powered edge AI and generative-AI workloads, pairing hardware AI acceleration with autonomous aiPM power management and a multilayered hardware Root of Trust security subsystem. Alif ships an embedded developer surface rather than a public web API: a Zephyr-based SDK, CMSIS Device Family Packs, VS Code project templates, the Conductor configuration tool, evaluation kits, datasheets, and reference manuals published across its support hub and GitHub organization. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and Mayfield.

providers.name: Tulip Interfaces
providers.description: Tulip is a manufacturing operations platform that enables frontline operations teams to build apps, connect machines and devices, and analyze production data without code. The Tulip REST API provides programmatic access to apps, tables, connectors, stations, automations, and analytics, supporting integration with ERP, MES, and industrial equipment on the shop floor.

providers.name: Proxy
providers.description: Proxy (Y Combinator, Summer 2016) was a San Francisco digital-identity startup founded by Denis Mars and Simon Ratner that built a mobile and wearable digital wallet for payments, identity, and authentication, later expanding into biometric identity verification and vaccine-credential verification. The company was acquired by OURA in 2023; the proxy.com domain no longer resolves to an active product and there is no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record.

providers.name: SeekOps
providers.description: SeekOps Inc. is an Austin, Texas emissions-measurement company that detects and quantifies methane and carbon dioxide from industrial facilities using drone-mounted laser spectroscopy. Its SeekIR sensor suite applies tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) originally developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to search for methane on Mars, hardened for terrestrial energy operations. SeekOps sells measurement as a service — Leak Detection and Quantification (LDAQ) surveys flown over upstream and midstream oil and gas sites, offshore platforms, landfills, biogas digesters and renewable natural gas facilities — and delivers the results through two software surfaces: Celsius, a cloud analytics and reconciliation-reporting dashboard, and FASTR, a real-time telemetry view. Founded in 2017, the company has surveyed facilities across six continents and is backed by Equinor Ventures and OGCI Climate Investments. Its software is customer-only: both Celsius and FASTR sit behind authentication and SeekOps publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Uptake
providers.description: Uptake Technologies is a Chicago-based industrial AI and predictive-maintenance software company founded in 2014 by Eric Lefkofsky and Brad Keywell. Its SaaS platform ingests telematics, sensor, fluid-analysis and work-order data from heavy commercial fleets and industrial assets, then applies machine-learning failure models — backed by an Asset Strategy Library of roughly 800 equipment types and tens of thousands of failure modes acquired with Asset Performance Technologies in 2018 — to predict component failure before it happens. Products include Uptake Fleet and Radar (predictive maintenance alerts), Compass (work-order data cleansing), Fusion (operational-technology data to cloud) and Scout (rules-based alerting), delivered through the fleet.uptake.com web application, a Geotab Marketplace add-in, and a customer-provisioned REST API gateway at api.uptake.com. Bosch announced its acquisition of Uptake in March 2026.

providers.name: Glowforge
providers.description: Glowforge is a Seattle-based consumer hardware company that makes desktop 3D laser printers (Glowforge Pro, Plus, Aura, and Spark) which cut and engrave materials such as wood, acrylic, leather, fabric, and paper. The machines are cloud-connected: designs are prepared in the browser-based Glowforge App (app.glowforge.com) and sent to the printer over the internet, with camera-based material placement, autofocus, and an online design catalog and marketplace. Glowforge does not publish a public developer API; its developer-facing footprint is limited to open-source GPL firmware and kernel components on GitHub (published for license compliance) and a public system status page.

providers.name: Guardhat
providers.description: Guardhat (now operating as Aatmunn) is an industrial safety and asset intelligence platform serving more than 250 companies across oil & gas, utilities, logistics and warehousing, chemicals, mining, infrastructure, and manufacturing. Its SPANR platform is a unified intelligence layer that collects data from connected safety devices and wearables, normalizes it into a single source of truth, applies business logic, and surfaces insights through a suite of applications for digital safety inspections, lone worker safety, gas detection, human condition monitoring, control access zoning, and asset tracking. Originally known for connected hard hats and wearable safety technology, the company rebranded from Guardhat to Aatmunn. Guardhat is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. This profile has been enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or OpenAPI surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Yellowfin
providers.description: Yellowfin provides an embedded analytics and business intelligence platform that enables organizations to create interactive dashboards, reports, and data stories. Its public REST API lets developers integrate content, manage users, and embed analytics into their own applications, supporting a range of data visualisation and storytelling capabilities.

providers.name: Automox
providers.description: Automox is a cloud-native IT operations and endpoint management platform that automates patching, configuration, and software deployment across Windows, macOS, and Linux devices from a single console. The Automox API is a REST API that gives developers programmatic access to organizations, zones, devices, groups, policies, packages, worklets, commands, events, reports, and users for building integrations and automating endpoint management workflows, authenticated with API keys.

providers.name: ChinaCache (EdgeNext)
providers.description: ChinaCache International Holdings was one of China's earliest and largest content delivery network (CDN) operators, founded in 1998 and formerly listed on NASDAQ. Its international CDN, edge computing, and cloud security business now operates under the EdgeNext brand at edgenext.com, delivering content acceleration, DDoS/WAF security, and edge compute across a network of 1500+ global points of presence and 90+ Tbps of capacity, with a strong footprint in China and other emerging markets. The company runs a customer console at home.console.edgenext.com with OpenID Connect (Keycloak) single sign-on and a REST API host at api.edgenext.com, documented in its online Document Center, for managing CDN domains, cache purge/prefetch, security policies, and edge configuration. The original chinacache.com domain now resolves to the EdgeNext web properties.

providers.name: Ecorobotix
providers.description: Ecorobotix SA is a Swiss agricultural technology company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Yverdon-les-Bains, Switzerland, building AI-driven ultra-high-precision (UHP) crop-care equipment. Its flagship ARA smart sprayer combines Plant-by-Plant AI detection with UHP-Spray-Technology to scan a field, classify crops versus weeds in under 250 milliseconds, and place treatment on a roughly six-by-six centimetre target, cutting herbicide and plant-protection input volumes by up to 95 percent compared with broadcast spraying. The product family spans the ARA620 and ARA595 UHP sprayers for row and vegetable crops, the ALBA UHP sprayer for turf, and a library of crop-specific algorithms for broccoli, carrots, onions and chicory. More than 1,000 ARA units have been deployed across Europe, the United Kingdom, North America, South America and Australia/New Zealand. Machine telemetry, treatment maps and fleet data are delivered to customers through the Ecorobotix cloud portal, which is backed by an authenticated REST API; that API is not offered as a public developer program.

providers.name: SCADA
providers.description: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) is an industrial control system architecture used to monitor and control industrial processes, infrastructure, and facility-based equipment. It is widely used in manufacturing, energy, water treatment, oil and gas, transportation, and other critical infrastructure sectors to collect real-time data from remote sensors and control equipment. Modern SCADA systems increasingly expose REST APIs, OPC-UA endpoints, and MQTT brokers for integration with enterprise systems, cloud platforms, and AI/ML workloads.

providers.name: EarlyFrame
providers.description: EarlyFrame provides a stateful edge webhook orchestration platform with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. It intercepts raw webhook payloads, transforms them into structured JSON, de‑duplicates, applies conditional routing, and fans out to Discord, Slack, Telegram and custom APIs. The service offers tiered plans, including a free sandbox, and supports AI‑agent integration via JSON‑RPC MCP.

providers.name: Seeed Studio
providers.description: Seeed Studio is a global IoT hardware enabler offering a wide range of open‑source hardware, development boards, sensors, and modules. Founded in 2010, it supports makers, startups, and enterprises with products like the Wio Terminal, Grove system, and reComputer series, plus a comprehensive wiki, community forums, and developer resources. The company emphasizes rapid prototyping, open‑source collaboration, and end‑to‑end solutions from hardware to cloud services.

providers.name: SkyFoundry
providers.description: SkyFoundry, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Glen Allen, Virginia, develops SkySpark, an analytics and informatics platform that connects, stores, analyzes, and visualizes data from smart devices, automation and control systems, meters, and sensors to "find what matters" in large equipment and facility datasets. SkySpark automatically detects issues, patterns, deviations, faults, and cost-reduction opportunities across intelligent buildings, industrial, agriculture, energy, government, and healthcare facilities, and has been applied to over 15,000 buildings spanning more than a billion square feet. SkySpark is a native Project Haystack server: external applications integrate through the Haystack HTTP REST API (ops such as read, hisRead, hisWrite, pointWrite, watchSub/watchPoll, eval, commit, and nav) with Zinc, JSON, Trio, and CSV data formats, and authenticate using the Haystack SCRAM (SHA-256) handshake with bearer authTokens. The company sells through a network of 140+ OEM, systems-integrator, and value-added-distributor channel partners rather than a self-service public SaaS.

providers.name: gjalla-io
providers.description: Gjalla.io is a technology company focused on providing innovative solutions in the IoT and data analytics space. Founded to bridge the gap between complex data streams and actionable insights, Gjalla.io offers a suite of APIs that enable developers to integrate real-time device telemetry, analytics dashboards, and automated reporting into their applications. The platform emphasizes scalability, security, and ease of integration, supporting a wide range of industries including smart manufacturing, environmental monitoring, and logistics. With a commitment to open standards and developer-friendly documentation, Gjalla.io aims to empower businesses to harness the power of connected devices and data-driven decision making.

providers.name: NTT
providers.description: NTT (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation) is a Tokyo-headquartered global technology and telecommunications group with roughly 340,000 employees and a 150-year history of innovation. The group operates through five business divisions — Consulting & IT Services, Mobile Solutions, Smart Tech, Consumer & Business, and Research & Development — and is anchored by major subsidiaries including NTT DOCOMO (Japan's largest mobile carrier), NTT Communications / NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS (enterprise cloud, network, and platform services), NTT DATA Group (global IT services and systems integration), NTT Ltd. (managed services), and NTT Research. NTT exposes a substantial developer surface through the NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS Developer Portal at developer.ntt.com, which catalogs enterprise APIs across Network (Arcstar Universal One, Flexible InterConnect, Global M2M), Cloud (Smart Data Platform, Enterprise Cloud 2.0), Voice, App (Safety Confirmation, Text & Language Analysis, Speech Recognition), Management (asset visibility, vulnerability), and Core (Authorization, Billing, API Log, Business Process, Service Order, Pay-per-use, Price, Organization, Personal Profile) categories. The group also publishes IoT APIs (Things Cloud) and a docomo Developer support portal at dev.smt.docomo.ne.jp. NTT's primary open source presence is the nttcom GitHub organization, which ships the Enterprise Cloud Python and Go SDKs (eclsdk / eclcloud), the eclcli command-line tool, Terraform providers for Enterprise Cloud 2.0 (terraform-provider- ecl) and Flexible InterConnect (terraform-provider-fic), the ksot network-IaC framework, the pola stateful PCE / PCEP library, the fluvia eBPF/XDP IPFIX exporter, and threatconnectome for SBOM-driven vulnerability management. NTT DATA additionally maintains regional GitHub orgs (NTTDATA, NTTDATA-EMEA, NTTDATA-DACH, NTTDATAInnovation, launchbynttdata, nttdata-oss) covering testing automation, Kubernetes plugins, and LLM observability tooling. NTT also drives the IOWN (Innovative Optical and Wireless Network) initiative, photonics and optical-quantum research, and responsible AI development across its R&D arm.

providers.name: ObjectBox
providers.description: ObjectBox is a high-performance, low-footprint, offline-first on-device database with built-in data synchronization and on-device vector search, designed for mobile, IoT, embedded, and edge computing applications. It is delivered as native language bindings (Java, Kotlin, C/C++, Go, Swift, Flutter/Dart, and Python) rather than a hosted REST API, giving apps ACID-compliant local persistence that works reliably offline and is described as up to 10x faster than SQLite. ObjectBox was the first on-device vector database on the market, targeting Edge AI use cases such as semantic search, recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation, and offers optional bi-directional Data Sync between devices and the cloud, including a direct connector to MongoDB. Founded in Germany and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Ohmconnect
providers.description: OhmConnect is a residential demand-response and virtual power plant company that turns household electricity flexibility into grid capacity. It alerts customers during "OhmHours" — windows when grid power is most expensive or carbon-intensive — and pays them cash, gift cards, and prizes for reducing or automating down their usage, then aggregates those reductions and sells them into wholesale energy markets. It serves California utility customers (PG&E, SCE, and SDG&E) and operates as a competitive retail electricity provider in Texas through OhmConnect Energy. OhmConnect runs a login-gated developer portal (developer.ohmconnect.com) secured with AWS Cognito OAuth2, but publishes no public API specification.

providers.name: Silicon Labs
providers.description: Silicon Labs (Silabs) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Austin, Texas that designs silicon, software, and solutions for a more connected, IoT world. Its portfolio includes wireless connectivity SoCs and modules for Bluetooth, Bluetooth Mesh, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, and proprietary sub-GHz protocols, along with 32-bit microcontrollers, sensors, and timing devices. Developers build on Silicon Labs hardware using the Simplicity Studio IDE, the Simplicity SDK (formerly Gecko SDK), the docs.silabs.com developer documentation, and the Silicon Labs Community. Silicon Labs is a hardware and embedded-software provider rather than a web-API vendor: its public developer surface is embedded C/C++ SDKs, tools, and reference examples on GitHub (github.com/SiliconLabs), not a hosted REST API — so this profile carries identity, developer-portal, and security signals rather than API specifications.

providers.name: August
providers.description: August (August Home) makes Wi-Fi smart locks, keypads, doorbell cameras, and the August Connect bridge for keyless, app-controlled home entry. Founded in San Francisco and originally backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Uncork Capital, August was acquired by Assa Abloy and its product line is now unified with Yale Home; the two brands share the August mobile app. August does not publish a public device-control API for consumers — third-party integrations rely on community-reverse-engineered endpoints or aggregators such as Seam, and Yale/August partners use the developer.august.com portal. Its august.com storefront (hosted on Shopify) does, however, expose an agent-native commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp and a hosted shopping MCP server at /api/ucp/mcp for buy-for-me agents, alongside Shopify customer-account OpenID Connect discovery.

providers.name: Belden
providers.description: Belden Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets networking, connectivity, and cable products and solutions for industrial automation, smart buildings, and broadcast markets. The company delivers end-to-end signal transmission solutions for mission-critical applications, including industrial Ethernet infrastructure, cybersecurity, and IIoT connectivity. Belden's Hirschmann brand is a leading provider of industrial network switches and management software with CLI, SNMP, and REST API interfaces for network device management.

providers.name: OpenWrt
providers.description: OpenWrt is an open-source project that provides a fully writable filesystem for embedded devices, primarily routers. It offers a Linux-based operating system with a package manager, allowing users to customize firmware, add features, and improve performance. The community maintains extensive documentation, guides, and a developer portal, supporting a wide range of hardware platforms. OpenWrt’s mission is to empower users with flexible, secure, and up-to-date networking solutions.

providers.name: OT Fabric
providers.description: OT Fabric (otfabric.io) builds open-source, MIT-licensed, pure-Go protocol libraries, command-line tools and Dockerized interoperability test suites for industrial operational technology (OT): Modbus, OPC UA, BACnet/IP, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850, Siemens S7, OpenADR, OCPP, DNP3, IEEE 2030.5, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, CANopen on CAN bus and KNX, plus SunSpec Modbus and IEC 61850 information models and Sparkplug B over MQTT. Its stated goal is 'unified data for industrial operations': breaking down OT data silos so industrial data is easy to discover, access and use across systems, sites and teams. It publishes libraries and CLIs rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Parsyl
providers.description: Parsyl Inc. is a Denver, Colorado based technology-enabled cargo insurance company for perishable and temperature-sensitive supply chains, with an office in London and underwriting capacity placed at Lloyd's of London. It pairs IoT temperature and condition sensors with a data platform that turns shipment telemetry into risk insight, and sells that insight back as connected marine cargo insurance products — ColdCover cargo insurance, stock throughput, excess stock, legal liability, a small-business program, and the cargo market's first parametric spoilage policy. Customers include food, seafood, pharmaceutical, vaccine and semiconductor shippers, plus global health programs such as Africa CDC and PFSCM. Parsyl runs a Data Partner Program that ingests telemetry from third-party monitoring vendors (Berlinger, Copeland, Roambee, Sensitech, Tive) and offers custom API integration so customers can pull their own systems' data into the Parsyl Platform. The API surface is real but is documented only to authenticated customers at docs.parsyl.com; no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, MCP server or agent card is published publicly.

providers.name: Nova Labs
providers.description: Nova Labs, Inc. is the company behind the Helium Network, a decentralized wireless network that replaces traditional carrier infrastructure with community-hosted Hotspots and is coordinated on the Solana blockchain and incentivized with the HNT token. Helium operates two networks: a global LoRaWAN network for low-power IoT devices and a cellular/Wi-Fi offload network for mobile connectivity (Helium Mobile). Nova Labs open-sources the network's protocol surface as gRPC/Protobuf service definitions (the helium/proto config, router, and proof-of-coverage services) and publishes a set of first-party client libraries, a command-line tool, and Rust crates for cryptography and protobuf types. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from Nova Labs' public developer surface; much of the legacy Helium IoT REST API tooling is archived following the network's migration to Solana.

providers.name: OpenDTU
providers.description: OpenDTU provides open-source firmware for solar inverters, enabling local monitoring and control without reliance on cloud services. The project supports ESP32-based hardware, offers a web UI, MQTT integration, and a documented Web API for retrieving inverter data, configuring settings, and managing devices. It targets DIY solar enthusiasts and small installations seeking transparent, self-hosted energy monitoring solutions.

providers.name: ServiceMax
providers.description: ServiceMax is asset-centric field service management (FSM) software that helps equipment manufacturers and service organizations maximize equipment uptime, optimize technician productivity, and streamline service delivery. Its cloud platform, built natively on the Salesforce platform (ServiceMax Core and Asset 360), spans work order and workflow management, scheduling and dispatch (Service Board), preventive and predictive maintenance, contract and entitlement management, parts and inventory, offline-capable mobile tools (ServiceMax Go), real-time technician collaboration (Zinc), and customer self-service (Engage). Founded in 2007 and acquired by PTC in 2023, ServiceMax integrates with PTC's IoT and PLM portfolio (ThingWorx, Windchill) and exposes its data and workflows through the underlying Salesforce API surface rather than a standalone public developer API.

providers.name: General Motors
providers.description: You can reach customers in their cars using GMs powerful, in-vehicle platform. Our tools can provide access to close to 200 data points, allowing you to monitor vehicle data in real-time to deliver the content that matters, when it matters. Create an account now to start developing amazing in-vehicle experiences for your customers.

providers.name: Terex
providers.description: Terex Corporation is a global manufacturer of aerial work platforms and materials processing equipment. Terex provides digital telematics solutions through its MyTerex platform and Connect by Terex for remote diagnostics, fleet management, and predictive maintenance of construction and industrial equipment.

providers.name: Bevel
providers.description: Bevel is a consumer digital-health application, built by Finerpoint, Inc., that acts as an AI-powered "connected health coach." It consolidates and interprets health data from wearables (Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin, Amazfit) and lab providers (Labcorp, Quest, LifeLabs) into a single view, scoring daily strain, sleep, recovery, stress/energy, nutrition, cycle, biological age and strength training. Its "Bevel Intelligence" layer delivers conversational, research-backed guidance, personalized workout plans and daily check-ins. Bevel is a mobile-first consumer product with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, roadmap and legal surface. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: RemoteLock
providers.description: RemoteLock provides a cloud-based smart access control platform that enables property owners and managers to control doors, locks, and credentials across multifamily, vacation rentals, and commercial properties. Their API allows developers to integrate lock management, schedule access, and receive real-time events via webhooks, supporting a wide range of hardware and software integrations.

providers.name: Sensel
providers.description: Sensel is a Sunnyvale, California touch-input company founded in 2013 by Ilya Rosenberg and Aaron Zarraga, building high-resolution force-sensing hardware — the Morph pressure-sensitive input device and the force-sensing touchpad technology shipped in laptops such as Lenovo's ThinkPad X1 Titanium Yoga. Its developer surface is not a web API: the Sensel API is an open-source, MIT-licensed C library (LibSensel) that talks to Sensel devices over USB/serial, published at github.com/sensel/sensel-api with C, C#, Python, Arduino, Processing, Max and Pure Data bindings and documented at guide.sensel.com. Sensel's intellectual property, physical assets and trademarks were acquired by Cirque Corporation (an Alps Alpine company), and sensel.com now 301-redirects to cirque.com/sensel.

providers.name: Uhnder
providers.description: Uhnder is an Austin, Texas fabless semiconductor company founded in 2015 that designs the S80 and S81 77 GHz 4D digital imaging Radar-on-Chip (RoC) for automotive ADAS and automated mobility. Its Digital Code Modulation (DCM) approach on a 28nm RF CMOS process replaces analog FMCW radar with a software-defined sensor, and each RoC ships with an ASPICE-qualified Software Development Kit carrying ready-to-integrate software APIs, on-chip user algorithm support and system tools for Tier-1 and OEM radar stacks. Uhnder is a chip supplier rather than a web-API provider: the SDK and its APIs are embedded interfaces delivered under a commercial customer relationship, and the company publishes no public developer portal, documentation host or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Zip Security
providers.description: Zip Security is a cloud-based security, IT, and compliance platform that automates identity management, device management (MDM for macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android), and endpoint threat detection for small and mid-sized businesses. It unifies tools such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, and CrowdStrike behind a single dashboard, deploying frameworks, policies, and controls that are continuously enforced to help teams reach SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, CMMC, and PCI readiness, often within two weeks. Zip Security is backed by General Catalyst. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Armadaai
providers.description: Armada.ai provides edge computing solutions with hardware and software platforms such as Leviathan, Galleon, Atlas, Bridge, and Marketplace. The company builds ruggedized mobile data centers and GPU‑as‑a‑service offerings for industries including oil & gas, defense, public sector, manufacturing, mining, and telecommunications. Their products enable scalable AI workloads at the edge, combining high‑performance compute with remote monitoring and management.

providers.name: Electric
providers.description: Electric (Electric AI) is an IT and security management platform for small and medium-sized businesses, consolidating device management, application and SaaS management, security posture monitoring with automatic remediation, and employee onboarding/offboarding into a single platform that requires no in-house IT skills and syncs with HR systems. Founded in New York and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Electric bundles partner tooling (JumpCloud MDM/SSO, Keeper, ThreatDown, Harmony Email, Perimeter81 VPN, Drata) behind an AI-powered IT Hub, help desk, and hardware procurement service. It is not a developer-API company: there is no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company and enriched from Electric's public web surface.

providers.name: Rush Enterprises
providers.description: Rush Enterprises is the largest network of commercial vehicle dealerships in North America, operating Rush Truck Centers with more than 200 locations across the United States. The company offers new and used commercial vehicles, all-makes parts, vehicle technology solutions, collision repair, alternative fuel systems, vehicle and equipment leasing, and financial services. Rush Enterprises provides fleet technology through RushCare, including Service Connect (integrated with OEMs like Peterbilt, International, Hino, and Cummins), Parts Connect, and telematics solutions powered by Geotab.

providers.name: MQTT
providers.description: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is an OASIS-standard, lightweight publish/subscribe messaging transport protocol designed for constrained devices and low-bandwidth, high-latency, or unreliable networks, making it the de-facto messaging protocol for IoT and machine-to-machine (M2M) communication. MQTT is a protocol specification rather than a hosted API: clients connect over TCP/TLS (typically port 1883 or 8883) or WebSocket (8080/8081) to an MQTT broker (such as Mosquitto, HiveMQ, EMQX, or AWS IoT Core) and exchange CONNECT, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE, and other control packets defined by the standard. The current standard is MQTT Version 5.0 (OASIS Standard, 7 March 2019); MQTT 3.1.1 remains widely deployed.

providers.name: AO Smith
providers.description: A. O. Smith Corporation (NYSE: AOS) is a global manufacturer of residential and commercial water heaters, boilers, water treatment and air purification products, headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Its connected-product line runs on the iCOMM platform, which lets homeowners and plumbing professionals monitor and control compatible water heaters — temperature, vacation mode, leak and maintenance alerts, energy-use history — from a mobile app. A. O. Smith operates no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK or MCP server, and the iCOMM backend is an undocumented GraphQL endpoint reachable only by the mobile apps and by community clients that reverse-engineered it.

providers.name: CoolerX
providers.description: CoolerX — formerly Cooler Screens — is an in-store retail media and merchandising technology company that turns cooler doors, endcaps, checkout coolers and pharmacy fixtures into IoT-connected digital screens. The platform pairs an AI "Intent Engine" for contextual targeting and conversion-funnel optimization with a Dynamic Content Engine for creative optimization, alongside campaign management, real-time measurement, and a data integration hub for product, price, promotion and context data. It is deployed with retailers including Kroger, Walgreens, Giant Eagle's GetGo, Chevron and Western Union, and is built on Microsoft Azure with NVIDIA, BOE, LG, Samsung and Foxconn as hardware and infrastructure partners. CoolerX sells to retailers and brands through a demo and sales motion; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: SMSEagle
providers.description: SMSEagle provides reliable SMS and MMS alerting solutions for critical environments. Their hardware gateways support single to eight-modem configurations, offering high‑availability, failover, and integration features such as email‑to‑SMS, webhooks, LDAP, MQTT, and multi‑factor authentication. Targeted at industries like IT, healthcare, and automation, SMSEagle enables automated message flows, escalation, and real‑time notifications via a web‑based GUI and API.

providers.name: Ambiq Micro
providers.description: Ambiq Micro is a semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions for battery-powered and endpoint-AI devices. Its proprietary Subthreshold Power Optimized Technology (SPOT) platform lets its Apollo family of Arm Cortex-M microcontrollers and Artasie real-time clocks run at extremely low energy, powering wearables, hearables, healthcare, smart-home, industrial and gaming devices. Ambiq's developer surface is an embedded C/C++ toolchain - the AmbiqSuite SDK and the open-source neuralSPOT AI SDK/Toolkit - plus a set of first-party Python AI toolkits (heartKIT, sleepKIT, physioKIT, neuralspotx) published on PyPI and GitHub (AmbiqAI, AmbiqMicro). This is not a web/REST API provider; it is profiled here for its open-source developer and AI SDK footprint.

providers.name: KITRO
providers.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

providers.name: AMPAworks
providers.description: AMPAworks builds AI-powered smart-shelf inventory management for healthcare and defense supply chains. Its platform pairs computer-vision cameras and rolling kiosks that image inventory to auto-count stock in real time with software that tracks supplies 24/7, automates reordering, and gives teams live visibility to prevent stock-outs. The company reports outcomes such as $15M in cost reduction, 25,000 hours saved on hand counting, and 72% fewer stock-outs across more than 28 healthcare and operational organizations. Backed by 500 Global, AMPAworks operates from offices in Santa Monica CA, Buffalo NY, Hackensack NJ, and Ann Arbor MI.

providers.name: Blackberry
providers.description: BlackBerry Limited is a Canadian intelligent security software and services company headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, and listed on the NYSE and TSX as BB. Once known for its smartphones, BlackBerry today builds embedded and cybersecurity software for enterprises and governments. Its portfolio spans QNX (a real-time operating system for automotive and embedded/IoT systems), Cylance AI-driven endpoint protection, BlackBerry UEM (Unified Endpoint Management), BlackBerry AtHoc critical event management and mass notification, BlackBerry SecuSUITE secure voice and messaging, BlackBerry Workspaces secure file sharing, and the BlackBerry Dynamics secure mobility platform. Developers integrate with these products through REST APIs and SDKs, including the BlackBerry UEM Web Services REST API, the BlackBerry AtHoc API (v2, REST with OpenID Connect / OAuth 2 auth), and the BlackBerry Dynamics SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline from BlackBerry's public developer surface.

providers.name: DigiLens
providers.description: DigiLens Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California company that designs and manufactures holographic waveguide optics and augmented reality display systems for extended reality (XR). Its Crystal Waveguides are produced with a proprietary photopolymer material set, inkjet printing and a holographic contact-copy process rather than etching, and are supplied to partners including Samsung, Corning, Panasonic, Sony, Continental, Mitsubishi Chemical and Goertek for smartglasses, automotive head-up displays, smart helmets and avionics head-up guidance. DigiLens also ships ARGO, a standalone, rugged enterprise AR headset running DigiOS — an Android-based operating system with voice UI, gaze and scroll-wheel interaction, projector control and Microsoft Intune MDM certification. Developers build for ARGO in Unity or Android Studio on top of the DigiOS SDK and Qualcomm Snapdragon Spaces, with samples published in the digilens-ar GitHub organization and documentation on the DigiLens developer portal. DigiLens has raised a Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above $500M.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: AMMP
providers.description: AMMP (AMMP OS) is a distributed energy monitoring and operations platform for operators of commercial and industrial (C&I) solar and battery-storage portfolios. It unifies visibility across multi-vendor fleets, pulling data directly from more than 30 manufacturer cloud platforms and its own AMMP Edge data logger, and layers on monitoring, alerting, stakeholder reporting, commercial (SLA/cost) tracking, and customizable dashboards. AMMP OS monitors over 10,000 sites across 35+ countries and emphasizes vendor independence and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified security. Surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and enriched by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Metrobloks
providers.description: Metrobloks, LLC develops and operates multi-tenant colocation data centers in underserved metropolitan markets, positioning capacity at the metro edge so that AI inference, IoT, gaming, streaming, telecom and financial workloads run closer to the users and devices that generate them. Founded by Ernest Popescu (CEO), Scott Couzens (COO), Ryan Shea (SVP Real Estate) and Alejandro Maldonado (CMO), the company came out of stealth in June 2024 with an oversubscribed $5.2M seed round led by Current Equity Partners with participation from Serena Capital, and has since announced a Eurazeo commitment of up to EUR 100 million for European expansion, a financing round led by the Canopy Generations Fund, a Kansas City joint venture with Lincoln Property Company, and a partnership with Soluna. Sites are announced or under development in Miami FL, Phoenix AZ, Detroit MI, Kansas City MO, Indianapolis IN and McAllen TX in North America, plus Paris in Europe. The product is physical: modular standardized halls, scalable power, air and hybrid liquid cooling with near-zero water consumption, and carrier-neutral interconnection including a self-perform cross-connect option. Metrobloks sells infrastructure, not software. It publishes no API, no developer portal, no customer self-service platform and no machine-readable specification of any kind; its only published compliance claim is a SOC 2 and SOC 3 assertion on its ESG page.

providers.name: Time.now
providers.description: Time.now provides a simple, free World Time API delivering current date and time information for any timezone. The service returns JSON data with fields such as datetime, timezone, utc_offset, and day_of_week, enabling developers to integrate accurate time data into applications without managing their own time zone databases. The API is publicly accessible, supports CORS, and offers endpoints like /api/timezone/{area}/{location} for worldwide coverage.

providers.name: WABCO Holdings
providers.description: WABCO Holdings was a leading global supplier of technologies and services that improve the safety, efficiency, and connectivity of commercial vehicles. The company developed advanced braking, stability, suspension, and transmission automation systems. WABCO was acquired by ZF Friedrichshafen in 2020 and now operates as ZF's Commercial Vehicle Control Systems division, continuing to serve OEMs, fleets, and aftermarket customers worldwide with integrated telematics, fleet management, and vehicle safety technologies.

providers.name: Ariadnemaps
providers.description: Ariadnemaps provides a privacy‑first people counting platform that uses hybrid fusion of phone‑signal sensing and time‑of‑flight depth sensors to deliver sub‑meter accuracy without cameras or personal data. The solution offers real‑time occupancy monitoring, queue management, and visitor flow analytics for venues such as retail stores, airports, and smart cities, complying with GDPR and EU AI Act requirements.

providers.name: Evidation Health
providers.description: Evidation Health is a San Mateo, California digital health company, founded in 2012, that measures health in everyday life and runs permissioned real-world data research at scale. Its consumer app and platform — Achievement — rewards members for connecting wearables, apps and health records, and its enterprise Research & Engagement Platform gives life-sciences, payer, government and non-profit customers eConsent and onboarding, ePRO and survey capture, passive and active device monitoring, program analytics, and participant education. Evidation combines data from sources including Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Dexcom and EHR/claims records (via a partnership with 1upHealth's FHIR-based Patient Connect, and with HealthVerity), and has enabled 175+ virtual real-world studies and 70+ peer-reviewed publications. Evidation publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces are the member app backend and enterprise data deliveries, neither of which is publicly documented.

providers.name: Insta360
providers.description: Insta360 (Arashi Vision Co., Ltd) is a consumer and professional imaging company best known for its 360-degree and action cameras (the X, GO, ACE, Link, and Pro/Titan lines). For developers, Insta360 runs a first-party developer program through its Insta360Develop GitHub organization and a VitePress developer-documentation site. Cameras expose on-device HTTP control APIs: consumer models implement Google's Open Spherical Camera (OSC) API over the camera Wi-Fi AP, and the Pro/Titan line adds a JSON-over-HTTP command API (ProCameraApi) for capture, live streaming, and file access. Native SDKs wrap this surface for C++ (camera control and media stitching/editing), Android, and iOS so third-party apps can connect to, configure, capture from, and post-process footage from Insta360 hardware.

providers.name: Squadle
providers.description: Squadle is a food safety and operational compliance platform for multi-unit restaurant and foodservice operations. It combines IoT remote temperature monitoring (its Remote Temperature System) with digital food-safety checklists, shift management, and patented ZeroTouch technology that automates temperature logging and triggers corrective actions. The platform reports 3.3B+ completed tasks and 100M+ temperatures measured. Squadle was acquired by Crunchtime and now operates as part of the Crunchtime Operations Execution platform; the squadle.com domain redirects to crunchtime.com/squadle. No public API or developer platform is currently published.

providers.name: Whirlpool
providers.description: Whirlpool Corporation is the world's only major U.S.-based manufacturer of kitchen and laundry appliances, with approximately $16 billion in annual net sales and 41,000 employees globally. Its brand portfolio includes Whirlpool, KitchenAid, JennAir, Maytag, Amana, Brastemp, Consul, and InSinkErator. Whirlpool offers connected smart appliances integrating with Amazon Alexa, Amazon Dash Replenishment, Google Assistant, and Matter for smart home automation, and provides a cloud-connected appliance API used by the Whirlpool mobile app and third-party integrations.

providers.name: Bosch
providers.description: Bosch is a German multinational engineering and technology company producing automotive components, industrial technology, consumer goods, and energy and building technology. Bosch operates the Bosch IoT Suite, an open IoT platform offering device management, software rollouts, edge services, and IoT data analytics, along with open source contributions to Eclipse Foundation IoT projects.

providers.name: Verizon Connect
providers.description: Verizon Connect is the fleet management, telematics, and GPS vehicle tracking business of Verizon (it grew out of Verizon's acquisitions of Fleetmatics and Telogis). Its Reveal platform exposes a documented suite of REST APIs and webhooks - the Reveal Integration Services / Fleetmatics Integration Manager (FIM) APIs - covering vehicles, drivers, GPS positions and history, trips (segments), driver status and safety, hours-of-service logbooks, geofences (places), groups, work orders, non-powered asset tracking, fleet inspections, and dash-cam video events. The API is not openly self-service - access is gated to Reveal customers and their approved integration partners, who request Integration Manager and Reveal REST credentials through the Reveal marketplace before they can call the documented endpoints.

providers.name: Fort
providers.description: Fort is a Y Combinator (W26) hardware startup building a screenless wearable that automatically tracks strength training for people who care about longevity. Founded by three former Tesla engineers, the device uses heart rate and motion sensing to detect gym sessions, workout classes, sleep, and recovery without requiring the wearer to manually log reps, sets, or exercises, then delivers actionable feedback on how lifestyle factors affect strength progress. Fort is styled as jewelry rather than performance gear, ships in three finishes with 7+ day battery life, and pairs with Fort Foundations, an expert-led training program built around core movement patterns. The product is currently available for pre-order and has no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public web and commercial presence.

providers.name: Fueloyal
providers.description: Fueloyal is an automotive IoT and connected-vehicle platform company that builds proprietary IoT gateway hardware and software for fleet management, fuel management, predictive maintenance, dual dash cameras, EV services, and OEM connected-vehicle solutions. Its products help fleets and vehicle manufacturers monitor, connect, and service vehicles, with an OEM connected-platform and marketplace for delivering connected-vehicle services and mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Fueloyal was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sunflower Labs
providers.description: Sunflower Labs is an innovative technology company focused on developing advanced AI-driven solutions for agricultural optimization. Founded with the mission to empower farmers through data-driven insights, Sunflower Labs offers a suite of APIs that provide real-time environmental monitoring, crop health analytics, and predictive yield modeling. Backed by leading venture capital firms including Sequoia Capital, the company leverages cutting‑edge machine learning and IoT sensor integration to deliver actionable recommendations that improve sustainability, increase productivity, and reduce resource waste across the agricultural sector. Their platform integrates seamlessly with existing farm management systems, offering developers robust documentation, SDKs, and support to build custom applications that drive the future of smart farming.

providers.name: Lucis
providers.description: Lucis is a Paris-based, AI-powered preventative health platform (Y Combinator P25; backed by General Catalyst) that helps members understand their biology through comprehensive lab testing and personalised coaching. Members receive two annual lab assessments (blood, urine, and saliva) at 450+ partner labs across Europe, producing 110+ data points across 11 body systems — metabolic, cardiovascular, hormonal, nervous, and more — which an AI engine turns into personalised action plans spanning nutrition, supplementation, sleep, activity, and mental health. The platform ingests wearable data (Garmin, Withings, Oura, Strava; Apple Watch and Whoop coming soon) for ongoing monitoring. Lucis is a consumer health product; as of this profile it exposes a member web/mobile application and a compliance portal but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Numina
providers.description: Numina is a New York City-based urban street-intelligence company (founded 2014, backed by 500 Global and SOSV) whose privacy-first, edge-processing computer-vision sensors measure how people, bicycles, and vehicles move through the public right-of-way. Its "Know Your Streets" platform turns anonymous, aggregated activity into multimodal mobility data for urban planners, municipal departments of transportation, and facilities managers, and exposes that data through the Numina Graph GraphQL API and a developer sandbox. (This profile was seeded as a 500 Global portfolio stub under the placeholder label "CTY"; its Website pointer and 500 Global backing identify it as Numina / numina.co.)

providers.name: Ampere Computing
providers.description: Ampere Computing is a Santa Clara, California semiconductor company founded in 2018 by Renee James and now part of the SoftBank Group. It designs Arm-based Cloud Native Processors — the Ampere Altra and Altra Max families (up to 128 cores) and the flagship AmpereOne family (up to 192 single-threaded cores) — for cloud, AI inference and edge deployments. Alongside the silicon it ships a software stack: Ampere Optimized AI frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX Runtime, llama.cpp, Ollama) distributed as first-party container images, tuned GCC/glibc/binutils builds, performance and porting tooling, and an arm64 developer community. Ampere publishes no public developer API — its developer program is a hardware, tooling and porting program rather than an API program.

providers.name: Farmbot Monitoring Solutions
providers.description: Farmbot Monitoring Solutions, founded in Sydney in 2014, is a leading Australian AgTech company providing water level monitoring and sensor solutions for farms. Their experienced team understands farmers' daily challenges and delivers user‑friendly products that reduce costs, boost productivity, and streamline farm management.

providers.name: Upciti
providers.description: Upciti is a French smart-city company that equips cities with intelligent computer-vision sensors and the Upciti OS platform, turning streets into clear, anonymous data for informed municipal decisions across parking, mobility, energy, water, gas, lighting, temperature, weather, air quality, pollen, illegal dumping, and noise. Sensors process video 100% locally with no image storage (GDPR-native, DTPR-supporting), and the platform advertises an open API for connecting GIS, BI, and business tools with no proprietary lock-in. Product documentation is customer-gated.

providers.name: Vodafone
providers.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aperiatechnologies
providers.description: Aperiatechnologies (operating as Aperia) provides automatic tire inflation solutions for commercial truck fleets. Their Halo platform monitors and maintains optimal tire pressure, reducing roadside breakdowns, safety violations, and fuel costs. The company combines IoT sensors, cloud analytics, and real‑time alerts to improve fleet safety and efficiency across North America.

providers.name: Cradlewise
providers.description: Cradlewise offers an all‑in‑one smart bassinet and crib that converts from a newborn bassinet to a toddler crib for up to 24 months. It includes a built‑in baby monitor, sound machine, and sleep‑tracking features, aiming to simplify nighttime care for parents. The product integrates IoT sensors and a companion app to provide real‑time insights and soothing sounds, positioning Cradlewise at the intersection of baby care and smart home technology.

providers.name: FlexGen Power Systems
providers.description: FlexGen Power Systems is a Durham, North Carolina energy storage technology company founded in 2009 that designs, integrates and operates grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) and the software that runs them. Its flagship product is HybridOS, a hardware-agnostic energy management system (EMS) for multi-source, multi-site battery and solar portfolios, alongside HybridOS Control BMS (a US-built battery management system), a solar power plant controller (PPC), EMS retrofit, activation and lifecycle services, and data-center power solutions. FlexGen has been named a BloombergNEF Tier 1 energy storage company, acquired Clean Energy Services (CES) and the assets of Powin, and states that HybridOS exposes automated APIs and historian data API access to customers. No public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published; the HybridOS API surface is reached only through customer deployments and the login-gated FlexGen customer portal.

providers.name: Hitachi Construction Machinery
providers.description: Hitachi Construction Machinery provides operational data about machines and equipment on construction sites through the Telematics API, which complies with the ISO 15143-3 (AEMP 2.0) standard. The API enables higher efficiency, productivity, and safety while reducing life cycle costs. API access, data elements and supported regions are arranged through Hitachi dealers; no public API reference or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Fleet Complete
