Its 360-degree Workplace Intelligence Platform, T-Pulse, combines proprietary IoT sensors, drones, robotics and machine vision with industrial AI to deliver automated inspections, predictive maintenance, gas and oil leak detection, structural health monitoring, and real-time workplace safety, operations and security monitoring for enterprises such as Shell, Vedanta, Adani Group and Hindustan Zinc. Backed by Accel and Elevation Capital. The company does not publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Metromile
providers.description: Metromile is a pay-per-mile auto insurance platform powered by telematics and data science. Customers attach the Pulse OBD device to their vehicle to track mileage; premiums consist of a base monthly rate plus a per-mile charge, rewarding low-mileage drivers with significant savings. Beyond consumer insurance, Metromile Enterprise offers a cloud-based REST API platform for property and casualty insurers covering touchless claims automation, accident reconstruction (Replay), fraud detection (Detect), digital FNOL reporting (Report), and back-office workflow automation (Streamline). Metromile was acquired by Lemonade in July 2022.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: Cactos
providers.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.

providers.name: ESPHome
providers.description: ESPHome is an open-source platform that simplifies building custom smart home devices using ESP8266/ESP32 microcontrollers. It provides a visual device builder, YAML configuration files, and seamless integration with Home Assistant, allowing users to create sensors, switches, lights, and more without extensive coding. The platform offers extensive component libraries, OTA updates, and local control, emphasizing privacy and flexibility for hobbyists and developers alike.

providers.name: Euler Motors
providers.description: Euler Motors is an Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer headquartered in New Delhi, building battery-electric cargo and light commercial vehicles for last-mile logistics — the HiLoad and Turbo electric three-wheelers and the Storm EV four-wheeler light commercial vehicle range. Alongside the vehicles the company operates Euler Shepherd, a connected-vehicle telematics platform delivered as two end-user products: Shepherd Lite (a mobile app for real-time vehicle location, battery state of charge, range, charging status and alerts) and Shepherd Enterprise (a browser-based fleet console with trip, utilization and operations reporting). Euler Motors publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog or partner integration documentation on any host it controls. The Shepherd web console is a single-page application whose backend answers anonymous requests with 403, so the telematics data surface is reachable only to vehicle owners inside the product. The company does publish an llms.txt at its web root, directing AI crawlers to its product, service-network and blog pages.

providers.name: Hatch
providers.description: Hatch offers a variety of smart sleep devices to help you sleep better night after night. Create healthy sleeping habits for the whole family with Hatch. Their flagship Hatch Sleep Clock is a sleep tracker designed to get you to sleep without relying on scores, offering customizable light and sound routines.

providers.name: LARQ
providers.description: LARQ is a direct-to-consumer water technology company that designs self-cleaning and filtering drinkware and home water products. Its flagship Bottle PureVis uses UV-C light to neutralize up to 99.9999% of harmful, odor-causing bacteria in the bottle and on the water surface, and the range extends to filtered bottles, filtered pitchers, an under-sink water filter, and the cuva beverage flavor line. The company positions itself around sustainable hydration — reducing single-use plastic bottle consumption — and funds environmental nonprofits from a portion of each purchase. LARQ is a consumer hardware and e-commerce business: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Nanoleaf
providers.description: Nanoleaf designs and manufactures smart lighting products, including LED light panels, light strips, and interactive lighting systems for homes and commercial spaces. Their platform integrates with major smart home ecosystems, offering AI‑powered experiences, wellness features, and developer APIs for controlling lighting, retrieving device status, and building custom integrations.

providers.name: ROMTech
providers.description: ROMTech (ROM Technologies, Inc.) is a privately held medical technology company headquartered in Brookfield, Connecticut that builds connected orthopedic rehabilitation technology. Its flagship product, the PortableConnect Adaptive Telemed Technology, is a prescription, clinician-delivered home rehabilitation device for patients recovering from total knee replacement, total hip replacement, joint manipulation and ACL repair. Adaptive pedal technology adjusts automatically to a patient's current range of motion across four therapy modes (passive, active-assisted, active and resistance); the AccuAngle Bluetooth wearable measures knee flexion and extension during each session; and the PortableConnect App runs a prescribed protocol of three to five daily sessions over a typical four-to-eight-week plan. Session data — range of motion, adherence and key health metrics — streams to a Clinician Portal where the prescribing surgeon reviews real-time reports and adjusts the protocol remotely, with in-app telemedicine for face-to-face follow-ups. The technology began as the ROM3 Rehab device. ROMTech was named to Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies list for 2025 and to the LexisNexis Top 100 Global Innovators for 2026, and sells to clinicians, health systems and the Department of Veterans Affairs. ROMTech runs no public developer program: it publishes no OpenAPI, SDK, webhook catalog or developer documentation, and the Clinician Portal at portal.romtech.com is a closed single-page application backed by a private, undocumented API at middleware.romtech.com/api.

providers.name: Roofline
providers.description: Roofline (RooflineAI GmbH, Köln, Germany) is a 2024 RWTH Aachen University spin-off building a retargetable AI compiler stack for edge deployment. Its three products are an SDK that compiles models ahead of time from any framework — the product page shows a single Python call, attic.compile(model, (input,)) — a lightweight C runtime with Python bindings that executes the compiled model and orchestrates heterogeneous SoCs, and a Performance Dashboard fed by a roofbench command-line tool running nightly benchmarks across hundreds of models for latency, throughput and memory footprint. The stack is built on open-source MLIR and IREE with proprietary hardware-specific optimization on top, and targets NPUs, MCUs and heterogeneous SoCs with quantization (INT8, blocked, symmetric, asymmetric, dynamic), dynamic shapes for on-device LLMs and mixture-of-experts support. Published work includes NXP eIQ Neutron NPU LLM enablement, Vulkan 1.3 and Arm SVE support in IREE, and day-0 support for Liquid AI LFM2. Roofline is a strategic partner of the Edge AI Foundation and raised a seed round from Serena and First Momentum Ventures. It sells compiler licenses to hardware vendors and embedded software teams: there is no developer program, no public API, no documentation host and no registry-published package. Every product page ends at a Contact Sales form, and the only machine-readable document Roofline publishes anywhere is an llms.txt on its marketing site.

providers.name: Biofourmis
providers.description: Biofourmis is a health technology company founded in 2015, with offices in Boston, Singapore and India, that partners with health systems, hospitals, payers and life science companies to deliver care in the home. Its platform combines medical-grade device connectivity, FDA-cleared algorithms and digital biomarkers, a patient mobile app and clinician dashboard, and 70+ dynamic care pathways to support Hospital at Home, Timely Discharge, SNF at Home and Remote Patient Monitoring programs. Biofourmis merged with CopilotIQ in October 2024 to form an end-to-end platform for AI-driven in-home care; ActiGraph acquired the Biofourmis life science business in January 2025. The company markets EMR integration and device-agnostic connectivity to enterprise healthcare customers, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: ECOVACS Robotics
providers.description: ECOVACS Robotics is a global home service robotics company founded in 1998 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, that designs, manufactures, and sells AI-powered autonomous cleaning devices for consumer and commercial use. Its product families include DEEBOT robotic vacuum and mopping robots, WINBOT window-cleaning robots, GOAT robotic lawn mowers, ULTRAMARINE pool-cleaning robots, and the DEEBOT PRO commercial line, all managed through the ECOVACS HOME mobile app. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; as of this enrichment pass ECOVACS publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface — this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: FordPass / Ford Pro
providers.description: FordPass is Ford Motor Company's consumer connected-vehicle mobile app and service platform for Ford and Lincoln owners, exposing remote start/stop, remote lock/unlock, vehicle status (fuel/charge, tire pressure, oil life, odometer, location), Vehicle Health alerts, BlueCruise hands-free driving, Wi-Fi hotspot, Phone As A Key, scheduled service, and roadside assistance via the embedded FordPass Connect 4G LTE modem. Ford Pro is Ford's commercial fleet brand spanning Ford Pro Telematics, Ford Pro Intelligence, Ford Pro E-Telematics for EVs, Ford Pro Charging, Ford Pro FinSimple, and dealer/upfit services. The Ford Developer Marketplace (developer.ford.com) hosts Ford's partner-facing API program — FordConnect Query API for consumer-vehicle data and remote command access (with vehicle-owner consent via FordPass account OAuth), plus a Ford Pro REST API surface for fleets including Vehicle Status, Vehicle Historical Status, Vehicle Metadata, Vehicle Efficiency (fuel/energy/idle), Driver Behavior, Trip Reports, and Vehicle Health. Ford Pro Telematics is integrated with Geotab, Fleetio, Samsara, Motive, Verizon Connect, and other fleet platforms, and Smartcar offers a consumer OAuth bridge to Ford vehicles using FordPass Connect credentials. Access to Ford APIs is gated behind a partner application and credentials issued through the Ford Developer Portal; Ford has periodically restricted individual-developer access. No public OpenAPI specification is published outside the partner portal, so this profile documents the Ford developer surface as an index without a generated machine-readable contract.

providers.name: MapmyIndia Mappls (C.E. Info Systems Ltd.)
providers.description: MapmyIndia Mappls (C.E. Info Systems Ltd.) provides comprehensive mapping, location intelligence, and IoT solutions across India. Their platform offers APIs for maps, geocoding, routing, traffic, and advanced services like 4D maps, drone services, and AI-driven analytics. Serving enterprises, developers, and government agencies, MapmyIndia enables integration of real‑world spatial data into applications, supporting navigation, asset tracking, and location‑based services.

providers.name: NanoLumens
providers.description: NanoLumens is an American designer and manufacturer of direct-view LED (dvLED) displays and video walls, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and founded in 2006 by Rick Cope. It builds fixed and flexible indoor and outdoor displays in custom sizes, shapes and curvatures across the Engage Pro, Engage, NXT, Nixel, NanoPanel 55, Captivate, Performance, CLRVision, CLRVU and NanoBanner product lines, together with Aurora video processing and the NanoSuite display-management software. Its displays are deployed in retail, casinos, higher education, sports and arenas, control rooms, hospitality, themed entertainment, government, corporate and transportation environments. The software side of the business — the AWARE platform and NanoSuite, powered by the ISAAC ecosystem — markets a JSON REST API and webhook-based alerting for remote diagnostics, content scheduling and display-fleet monitoring, but that API is delivered to display owners through an authenticated tenant and has no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Sensorum Health
providers.description: Sensorum Health is a healthcare technology company that provides home-based, fully passive sensor technology and integrated clinical services to identify and triage the earliest signs of health decline in older adults living with chronic conditions. The platform monitors patients 24/7 in their own homes without requiring wearables, smartphones, or WiFi, then coordinates clinical interventions when concerning health patterns emerge — with the goal of preventing avoidable hospital admissions. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). Added to the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record; no public API, specification, or developer program has been published as of this profile.

providers.name: Synapsor
providers.description: Synapsor (legal entity Ottai Technology (Wuxi) Co. Ltd.) is a Chinese medical-device company based in Wuxi, Jiangsu that develops AI-powered, medical-grade smart wearable devices. Its flagship product is the Ottai continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system - a waterproof, calibration-free wearable sensor paired with a mobile app and AI assistant for 24/7 glucose tracking and diabetes management, sold in China and internationally via ottai.com. Investors include Qiming Venture Partners, Huatai Zijin Investment, Wuxi Industry Development Group, YuanBio Venture Capital, and Shunwei Capital. Synapsor publishes no public developer API, portal, or machine-readable API specifications as of July 2026.

providers.name: Vaisala
providers.description: Vaisala is a global leader in measurement instruments and intelligence, providing weather, climate and industrial solutions. With over 1 million sensors manufactured annually and a presence in 150+ countries, Vaisala delivers reliable data for climate action, aviation, energy and many other sectors, supporting customers worldwide with innovative technologies and services.

providers.name: Wakefit
providers.description: Wakefit Innovations Limited (wakefit.co) is an Indian direct-to-consumer home and sleep-solutions company founded in 2016 in Bengaluru, selling memory-foam and orthopaedic mattresses, beds, sofas, wardrobes, bedding, decor and the Wakefit Zense connected-sleep line (Regul8 mattress temperature controller and Track8 contactless sleep tracker) through its own e-commerce storefront, an offline retail network and Indian marketplaces. Wakefit operates as a retailer rather than a platform: it publishes no public developer program, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its storefront back end at api.wakefit.co is a private, login-gated internal dashboard. This profile records the company identity and the public pages it does serve.

providers.name: Zero Motorcycles
providers.description: Zero Motorcycles is an American manufacturer of electric motorcycles and powertrains, founded in 2006 in Santa Cruz, California. It designs and builds street, dual-sport and off-road electric motorcycles across its S, DS, FX and X lines — including the SR/S, SR/F, DSR/X, FXE and XE — around a proprietary Z-Force electric powertrain and aircraft-grade aluminum frame. Its bikes run the Cypher operating system, which pairs with the Zero Motorcycles NextGen mobile app over Bluetooth and cellular telematics for ride data, remote diagnostics, over-the-air updates and performance customization, and with the Cypher Store, where owners purchase software upgrades that unlock additional power, top speed and features. Zero sells internationally through a dealer network and serves retail, fleet and authority/first-responder segments. Its connected-vehicle platform is consumer-facing only: Zero publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Boldr
providers.description: Boldr is a Techstars-backed consumer hardware company building energy-saving smart home climate control devices. Its two products are Kelvin, a smart infrared heater, and Klima, a smart thermostat controller for mini-split air conditioners that also monitors appliance health so units last longer with fewer issues. Both devices are managed through the Boldr mobile app, which lets homeowners control climate settings remotely and track energy usage to lower utility bills. Boldr also runs Boldr Pro, a program for HVAC contractors. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted online store at shopboldr.com and does not currently publish a first-party developer API; its only public machine-readable surface is the Shopify Customer Account OIDC discovery served at the storefront host.

providers.name: Crosser - IoT Edge Streaming Analytics
providers.description: Crosser provides an IoT edge streaming analytics platform that enables real-time data processing and insights at the device level. By integrating edge computing with powerful analytics, Crosser helps manufacturers, logistics providers, and other industrial operators to monitor, analyze, and act on sensor data instantly, reducing latency and bandwidth costs while improving operational efficiency and decision-making.

providers.name: Ensemble Scientific (ESCI)
providers.description: Ensemble Scientific combines real-time sensors, forecasting, and autonomous irrigation systems for efficient water management. Based in British Columbia, they provide smart irrigation control for modern farms, offering hardware and a cloud platform to monitor, optimize, and automate watering across zones, reducing water use and improving yields for crops such as berries, strawberries, and other field produce.

providers.name: Ai Fabrik
providers.description: AI Fabrik is an infrastructure company building an edge inference delivery network for high-performance AI tokens. Incubated within Gruve and led by founder Tarun Raisoni alongside Swati Deshpande and Tanuj Mohan, the company has deconstructed the traditional data center model and rebuilt every layer for real-time AI, delivering distributed inference close to users and cloud providers with sub-20ms latency, cost efficiency, and built-in compliance. AI Fabrik is deploying five initial production sites with 6,000+ B300 GPUs launching in 2026, backed by Mayfield, Xora (Temasek), Acclimate Ventures, and Cisco Investments.

providers.name: Axiom Space
providers.description: Axiom Space, Inc. is a privately funded American space infrastructure developer headquartered in Houston, Texas, founded in 2016 by Kam Ghaffarian and former NASA International Space Station Program Manager Michael Suffredini. The company is building Axiom Station, the world's first commercial space station and planned successor to the ISS, and has flown private astronaut missions to the ISS (Ax-1 through Ax-4). Axiom Space also develops the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit for NASA's return to the lunar surface, and sells human spaceflight, microgravity research, in-space manufacturing, and Orbital Data Center services (in-orbit cloud compute, with the ODC T1 node built alongside Kepler Communications and Skyloom Global). As of this enrichment pass Axiom Space publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract — every offering is transacted through direct enterprise, agency, and government engagement, and its only public code presence is a two-repository GitHub organization holding forks of NASA simulation software (Trick and GUNNS).

providers.name: Botrista
providers.description: Botrista, Inc. is a San Francisco based beverage-automation company founded in 2017 that builds the DrinkBot robotic beverage dispenser and the CloudBar cloud platform behind it. The DrinkBot automates craft beverages — infused teas, flavored lemonades, iced coffees and mocktails — dispensing a drink in roughly twenty seconds from a touchscreen order, and every unit is internet connected so it pulls recipes, reports consumption, tracks ingredient levels and pushes maintenance alerts back to Botrista. CloudBar is the operator-facing web application used by restaurant, campus dining, convenience and theme-park operators to manage recipes, inventory replenishment and sales/menu performance analytics across a fleet of machines, alongside a separate Botrista Data Portal. Botrista sells beverage automation as a service rather than as a developer platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract, and POS integrations are handled case-by-case through its commercial team.

providers.name: Cognosos
providers.description: Cognosos provides AI‑powered real‑time location intelligence and asset tracking solutions for healthcare, automotive, and logistics industries. Their cloud‑based platform combines GPS, Bluetooth, and proprietary machine‑learning models to deliver high‑accuracy visibility of assets both indoors and outdoors, helping customers reduce costs, improve safety, and streamline operations.

providers.name: Defined Networking
providers.description: Defined Networking provides Managed Nebula, a managed overlay network that creates direct, encrypted connections between hosts without requiring VPN gateways or open inbound ports. The service supports remote access, drop‑in encryption, multi‑cloud deployment, and IoT/fleet telematics, enabling teams to securely connect laptops, servers, cloud instances, and mobile devices across NAT and firewalls.

providers.name: KubeEdge
providers.description: KubeEdge is a CNCF graduated project that extends Kubernetes to edge computing. It provides infrastructure support for networking, application deployment, and metadata synchronization between cloud and edge. KubeEdge enables containerized application orchestration at the edge with offline autonomy, ensuring edge nodes continue functioning when disconnected from the cloud.

providers.name: OpenYurt
providers.description: OpenYurt is a CNCF incubating project that extends Kubernetes for edge and cloud-edge collaboration scenarios. It provides node autonomy for edge nodes to continue operating during cloud-edge network disconnections, seamless node conversion between cloud and edge modes, and unified management of edge resources through NodePool and YurtAppSet abstractions.

providers.name: Tovala
providers.description: Tovala is a Chicago-based food-technology company that pairs a fresh meal delivery service with its proprietary smart countertop ovens. Weekly rotating, chef-crafted meals ship with QR codes that the Tovala Smart Oven (5-in-1) and Smart Oven Pro (6-in-1 with steam) scan to cook automatically, eliminating shopping, prepping, and cleanup. The company also offers GLP-1 balanced and high-protein menus, flexible meal plans, and a consumer mobile app backed by its api.tovala.com platform. Tovala is a Y Combinator portfolio company.

providers.name: Blaize
providers.description: Blaize (NASDAQ: BZAI) is an edge AI company headquartered in El Dorado Hills, California that builds a programmable inference platform uniting silicon and software. Its Graph Streaming Processor (GSP) powers the Pathfinder and Xplorer accelerator families — SoM, M.2, EDSFF and PCIe form factors plus the DST developer station and Blaize Inference Server — and its software layer pairs the Picasso SDK (C++, Python, OpenVX, with TensorFlow/PyTorch/ONNX import via NetDeploy) with AI Studio, a code-free environment spanning the full edge AI DataOps/DevOps/MLOps lifecycle. In April 2026 Blaize announced a planned Blaize AI Services platform that packages multimodal inference, business logic and orchestration as modular application-level APIs across vision, video, document, speech and moderation workloads. The developer surface — SDK downloads, repositories and reference material — is served from a self-hosted GitLab at software.blaize.com and requires an account, so no public machine-readable API contract is published.

providers.name: Deako
providers.description: Deako is a whole-home smart lighting company that designs modular smart switches, dimmers, plugs, and simple switches (motion, timer, nightlight, and fan controls) for residential new construction and retrofit. Its Deako Intelligence platform layers adaptive lighting, follow-me sound, intercom, and parent-care features on top of the hardware, and the devices integrate with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Control4, Clare, and the Matter smart-home standard. Deako sells directly and through a network of homebuilders, electricians, and integrators. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile tracks the company's public web, support, blog, legal, and smart-home integration surface, awaiting any future developer program.

providers.name: Moleaer
providers.description: Moleaer Inc. is a Hawthorne, California nanobubble technology company that designs and manufactures nanobubble generators — Clear, Bloom, Lotus, Neo, Nexus, Trinity, Freya, Indalo, Titan and XTB, plus the NanoShield service — used to raise dissolved oxygen, act as a chemical-free oxidant, and control algae and biofilm in aquaculture, horticulture and irrigation water, lakes and ponds, wastewater treatment, food and beverage, car washes, mining, and oil and gas. Its only digital surface is a customer-only remote monitoring service, launched in 2020 with industrial IoT provider AMI Global, that reports equipment status and water-quality readings (DO, pH, ORP, temperature, conductivity) into a login-gated portal at www.monitoring-moleaer.com. Moleaer publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification; equipment-level integration is offered through industrial control protocols (SCADA/Modbus/EtherNet-IP) on the generators themselves, not through a web API.

providers.name: Sioma
providers.description: SIOMA is a Colombian precision-agriculture (agtech) software platform for tropical crops such as oil palm, banana, and cacao. It helps plantations monitor field labor, track harvest and weighing (pesaje) operations with GPS, and make data-driven decisions to raise productivity. The product combines a mobile field-management app, GPS-based labor tracking, smart weighing hardware (Nukak, Sigma, Jaco, and Bascula-G scales), and Siomi, an AI assistant for agriculture. SIOMA is delivered as a customer web and mobile application and is backed by 500 Global. No public API or developer program is currently published.

providers.name: 4D Bios
providers.description: 4D Bios Co., Ltd. (四维生态, Hangzhou, China) is an ag-tech manufacturer of smart vertical-farming systems, founded in 2018 by Dr. Gary Hua. It designs and builds fully enclosed, digitally controlled plant factories — 3D, nursery, strawberry, leafy-greens and specialty lines — alongside containerized grow systems, indoor grow boxes, full-control planting equipment and LED horticultural lighting. The hardware is operated from the company's own software layer: the 4D Cloud Platform, the 4D CUBE MS management console and 4D BOX, which combine IoT telemetry, environmental and HVAC control, nutrient-solution circulation and big-data analytics for year-round continuous production. 4D Bios markets a "4D Bios Open Platform API" for customers who have already purchased its products and want to build their own software or hardware against the platform, and invites third-party platform service providers to develop applications on the Open Platform. That API has no public developer portal, reference, or machine-readable contract; the Open Platform and IoT consoles are login-gated single-page applications.

providers.name: CDNetworks
providers.description: CDNetworks is a global content delivery network (CDN) and cloud services provider that delivers high‑performance, secure, and reliable web content, video, and applications to end‑users worldwide. Founded in 2000, the company operates an extensive edge network spanning over 200 points of presence across the Americas, Europe, Asia‑Pacific, and the Middle East. CDNetworks offers solutions for web acceleration, DDoS protection, web application firewall, and edge computing, helping enterprises improve latency, availability, and security for their digital assets. Their platform supports a range of industries, including media, e‑commerce, gaming, and SaaS, and integrates with major cloud providers to provide hybrid delivery models.

providers.name: iBasis
providers.description: iBasis is a global communications solutions provider serving mobile operators, MVNOs, over-the-top players, and IoT device companies worldwide. Its portfolio spans international and managed voice, 5G data roaming and roaming hub/breakout, A2P and RCS messaging monetization, and IoT connectivity built on eSIM technology, the Simfony connectivity-management platform, MVNO-as-a-Service, and fixed wireless access. iBasis also offers signaling and fraud security (FraudLock iQ360, Security iQ360, Signaling Vulnerability Scanner) and business intelligence for carriers. Customer and partner operations run through the eCare portal behind single sign-on; iBasis does not currently publish a public developer program, OpenAPI specifications, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and enriched from the public iBasis web presence and live domain probes.

providers.name: Justos
providers.description: Justos is a Brazilian digital auto insurance insurtech founded in 2020 and headquartered in Barueri, São Paulo. Operating as a managing general agent (MGA), Justos uses smartphone-collected driving data (telematics) to reward safe drivers with lower, usage-based pricing — advertised as up to 30% cheaper than traditional plans — plus weekly bonuses and perks like gas vouchers, maintenance, and ride credits. Its products are distributed digitally through a consumer mobile app and a broker (corretor) portal, with claims tracked in-app and 24/7 support. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Kaszek, SoftBank Latin America and GGV; its auto insurance is underwritten by Companhia Excelsior de Seguros (SUSEP code 05690). No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: Kotcha
providers.description: Kotcha is a consumer running-coaching mobile application operated by PACEUP SAS, a French company based in Paris, and co-founded with marathon world-record holder Eliud Kipchoge and the NN Running Team. The app generates personalized, adaptive training plans for 5K, 10K, half-marathon and marathon distances, delivered through a conversational AI coach that adapts to completed workouts, and it imports activity and health data from Strava, Garmin Connect, Apple, Coros and Huawei wearables. Kotcha raised EUR 3.5M in October 2025 in a round led by Racine2, operated by Serena and makesense. Kotcha is a consumer subscription product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its terms of service explicitly prohibit automated access to the service. This profile records that absence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Sonatus
providers.description: Sonatus, Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California automotive software company, founded in 2018, that builds cloud-to-edge vehicle AI software for software-defined vehicles (SDVs). Its Fastlane platform pairs in-vehicle Fastlane Edge software with Fastlane Collector for dynamic, policy-driven vehicle data collection, Fastlane Insight for cloud-side analysis, and Fastlane Copilot for quick-start integration, alongside the Sonatus Automator vehicle-automation product. Sonatus states its technology is deployed in more than eight million vehicles worldwide, and it is backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Kia, LG, Marvell, NEC, Foxconn and Translink Capital. Sonatus sells to vehicle OEMs and tier-one suppliers rather than to individual developers: it markets an SDK comprising Sonatus Automator, APIs and documentation, but that developer surface is delivered to contracted OEM customers and is not published on any public developer portal.

providers.name: AssetWatch
providers.description: AssetWatch provides advanced asset condition monitoring and predictive maintenance solutions for industrial plants. Their platform combines vibration analysis, oil analysis, AI-driven insights, and human expertise to help organizations reduce unplanned downtime, improve reliability, and optimize maintenance strategies across various industries such as chemicals, food & beverage, metals, mining, and more.

providers.name: Atombergtechnology
providers.description: Atomberg is an Indian smart home appliance brand offering energy‑efficient ceiling fans, mixer grinders, water purifiers, juicers and smart locks. Founded with a focus on cutting‑edge technology and design, the company emphasizes low power consumption, durability and modern aesthetics for contemporary homes. Their product line integrates IoT features and aims to provide sustainable solutions for everyday living, serving customers across India and expanding globally.

providers.name: Customer Analytics
providers.description: Customer Analytics (CA) is a data, analytics and AI consultancy headquartered in Middleton, Wisconsin with a delivery centre in Guindy, Chennai, India. The firm delivers AI/ML and data analytics, data engineering, business intelligence and reporting, business solutions design and software development, platform implementation and software management (Microsoft Dynamics 365, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce), and quality assurance. Alongside these services it packages six productised offerings — DataWorks 360, BI Xpert 360, AI Assist 360, Retail AI Insights 360, PBILens 360 and Smart IoT Data Track 360 — and publishes case studies across healthcare, manufacturing, retail/B2B, education, agriculture, clinical research, warehouse operations, the art industry and government. Customer Analytics is a professional services company: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Freedom Robotics
providers.description: Freedom Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics infrastructure company founded in 2017 that builds mission-critical software to help robotics companies build, operate, support, and scale heterogeneous robot fleets. Its cloud platform — sometimes referred to as Mission Control — provides device and fleet management, remote teleoperation (Pilot), live data streaming, smart alerts and notifications, fleet maps and heatmaps, deployment and service management, remote development, and analytics across cobots, industrial robots, AMRs, drones, and custom hardware. The platform is robot- and OS-agnostic, installs on a device in seconds via a single-line Freedom Agent installer, and integrates with ROS, ROS 2, Python, microcontrollers, Protobuf, Docker, and the cloud offerings of AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Freedom exposes a public REST API at api.freedomrobotics.ai covering accounts, devices, alerts, statistics, uploads, tokens, users, user groups, and zones, plus a Python SDK (freedomrobotics.link) with Link, MicroLink, message, log, image, and command-callback primitives for programmatic control and telemetry of large numbers of robots. The company has raised approximately $17M in venture funding and operates on a per-robot subscription model (publicly cited at roughly $300 per robot per month) with custom enterprise plans negotiated through sales.

providers.name: Signify (Philips Hue, WiZ)
providers.description: Signify, formerly Philips Lighting, is a global leader in lighting solutions, offering professional, consumer, and IoT-enabled products such as Philips Hue and WiZ. The company provides smart lighting, LED technology, and digital services across residential, commercial, and industrial markets, focusing on sustainability and innovative lighting experiences.

providers.name: Aptimiz
providers.description: Aptimiz provides digital solutions for agricultural time‑tracking and farm management, offering connected devices and software to monitor labor, equipment, traceability, and crop activities. Their platform helps growers optimize operations, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve decision‑making through real‑time data.

providers.name: Epic CleanTec
providers.description: Epic Cleantec is a San Francisco based water technology company that designs, builds and operates onsite water reuse systems for buildings. Its OneWater and OneWater Rain systems collect, treat and recycle a building's greywater, blackwater, rainwater and condensate onsite — recovering up to 95% of wastewater for non-potable uses such as toilet flushing, irrigation, cooling towers and laundry — alongside wastewater heat recovery and a soil amendment product line. The technology grew out of work on the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation Reinvent the Toilet Challenge and is deployed in multifamily, commercial office, hospitality, stadium, data center, higher education and community-scale developments across North America. Systems ship with PLC/SCADA control and a cloud-connected Eco-Insights reporting dashboard for remote monitoring, alarms and utility savings reporting, but Epic Cleantec publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; the data surface is delivered to building owners and operators as a hosted dashboard rather than as a public API.

providers.name: Evigence Sensors
providers.description: Evigence Sensors is a freshness-management technology company for the food industry, combining low-cost physical sensors with data analytics to monitor food quality in real time from production to consumption at the individual item level. Its time-temperature indicator technology powers both digital (QR-scan) and visual freshness indicators applied to retail units, serving food brands, retailers, foodservice operators, cold-chain logistics providers, and consumers across the supply chain. Evigence holds 27 granted patents and its indicators meet WHO time/temperature monitoring standards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Evigence publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its verified public company properties only.

providers.name: FiberSense
providers.description: FiberSense is a distributed fiber optic sensing (DFOS / distributed acoustic sensing) company that turns existing and purpose-built fiber optic cables into dense arrays of vibration and acoustic sensors for real-time detection, localization and classification of objects and events across critical infrastructure. Its AI/ML algorithms filter noise and false alarms in dense urban, marine and underground environments, delivered as a subscription-based sensing platform rather than a public developer API. Product lines include DigitalAsset (critical infrastructure asset protection), DigitalCity (urban infrastructure and utility monitoring), DigitalMarine (subsea and marine cable route monitoring) and DigitalLeak (pipeline leak detection). Backed by Prosus Ventures; customer support runs through an Atlassian service desk portal.

providers.name: Forterra
providers.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.

providers.name: Freight Farms
providers.description: Freight Farms is a Boston-based vertical farming company that builds the Greenery container farm, a commercial-scale, modular, hydroponic farm assembled inside a shipping container so growers can produce hyper-local produce 365 days a year in any climate. Its Farmhand software platform provides remote farm control, farm data analytics and insights, crop planning, and pre-set growing recipes, backed by certified training, onboarding, logistics, and technical support. The company reports 800+ farms across 50 U.S. states and 3 territories and 2,100+ farmers in 42 countries. Freight Farms currently publishes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI surface; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, brand, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe while a programmatic surface is monitored for.

providers.name: Fuchsia
providers.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Haber
providers.description: Haber (Elixa Technologies Private Limited), headquartered in Pune, India with a US presence in Chicago, is an industrial AI company delivering AI-led automation for smart manufacturing across heavy industries including pulp, paper, packaging and tissue, metals and mining, food and beverages, oil and gas, and water/utility institutions. Its product suite spans eLIXA, an IIoT-powered process intelligence platform; Mt. Fuji for historical data storage, visualizations, digital twins and predictive interventions; Kaiznn, an optimization engine for trim-loss reduction, inventory and production scheduling; plus Kensei and FiMorph. The platform emphasizes real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and enterprise-grade security (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jiobit
providers.description: Jiobit is a real-time GPS tracking device company owned by Life360, based in San Mateo, California. Its lightweight (18g) wearable tracker is designed for kids, pets, seniors, and adults, combining LPWA CatM1 cellular, GPS, WiFi, and BLE for location accuracy of 1-50 feet, up to 30 days of battery life, geofence and SOS/911 emergency alerts, and tamper-proof, government-level encryption. Jiobit is a consumer hardware and mobile-app product sold direct-to-consumer with a monthly connectivity subscription; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: K4Connect
providers.description: K4Connect is a Morrisville, North Carolina technology company serving the senior living industry, backed by Sierra Ventures. Its patented FusionOS integration and data platform provides two-way ("One-to-Many") interoperability that shares the who, what and when of a community between every integrated system, connecting 50+ leading applications, devices and services. On top of FusionOS sits K4Community, an enterprise engagement suite of interconnected modules: Team Hub for staff, the Plus App for residents, Voice (Amazon Alexa), K4TV infotainment, Digital Signage, and smart-home Resident Check-In. K4Connect operates a partner-led integration model rather than a public self-serve developer API; integrations are built and coordinated through FusionOS.

providers.name: Moj.io
providers.description: Mojio (moj.io) is a connected-car and connected-mobility platform that collects, processes, and monetizes vehicle telematics data at scale for mobile network operators, automotive OEMs, insurers, and fleet/field-service businesses. Its "Mobility Studio" platform exposes REST endpoints for vehicle data, a PUSH API for real-time insights, mobile SDKs, and a vehicle simulator, alongside a white-label consumer app (Motion) and a services ecosystem (Alexa, Google Maps, Bosch, and others). Mojio has processed 15+ billion miles of driving data. As of this pass the API and SDK surface is partner-gated — there is no public developer portal, published OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API documentation. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Neuron Mobility
providers.description: Neuron Mobility is a rental e-scooter and e-bike operator and micromobility technology developer running shared micromobility fleets in cities across Australia, the United Kingdom, and Canada. The company designs its own vehicles (including the N3 e-scooter), safety systems such as its patented Helmet Lock and ScootSafe rider training program, and the backend fleet-management, IoT, and geofencing technology that powers its rider apps and city operations. Backed by 500 Global, Neuron was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no first-party developer API, GBFS data feed, or well-known discovery surface on its own domain; this profile captures its public web, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Remedee Labs
providers.description: Remedee Labs is a French medical device company founded in 2016 in Grenoble that develops millimeter-wave neuromodulation solutions for chronic pain management. Its flagship product is the Remedee wrist bracelet, which stimulates nerve endings to trigger endorphin release, paired with the myRemedee companion app and human coaching. The company markets two subscription solutions, FibroRem for fibromyalgia and NoviRem for osteoarthritis pain. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network; the product is consumer-facing and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Siren
providers.description: Siren is a digital health company that makes temperature-monitoring smart socks to prevent diabetic foot ulcers. The seamless, machine-washable socks require no charging or smartphone; embedded sensors continuously track foot temperature to detect the early inflammation that precedes an ulcer, and licensed nurses review the data and alert the patient's healthcare provider. Siren pairs the hardware with a remote patient monitoring service billed through providers and payers, and operates as a HIPAA-regulated healthcare business rather than a developer platform. It is backed by 500 Global and DCM Ventures. As surveyed for the API Evangelist network, Siren publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Sleep Number
providers.description: Sleep Number Corporation (NASDAQ: SNBR) designs, manufactures, and retails smart adjustable-firmness beds and sleep-wellness products, sold through an omnichannel US retail model. Its Sleep Number 360 smart beds run the proprietary SleepIQ operating system, which captures biometric sleep data each night and returns actionable insights to improve sleep health. Sleep Number does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; the SleepIQ platform is a closed, undocumented backend consumed only by the first-party mobile and web apps. The community has reverse-engineered unofficial SleepIQ client libraries (Python, Go, PHP), but these are not first-party and are not endorsed by Sleep Number. This profile was surfaced as a legacy portfolio lead of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Stel
providers.description: Stel Life provides cellular-connected remote patient monitoring (RPM) infrastructure for healthcare. Its cellular-enabled vitals hubs and connected medical devices — blood pressure monitors, pulse oximeters, glucometers, thermometers, and scales — let patients transmit vital-sign readings to electronic health record (EHR) systems without WiFi, broadband, a smartphone, or app setup, targeting elderly, low-income, rural, and low-tech-literacy populations. Health systems and digital health organizations use Stel across the care continuum, from wellness and chronic-care management to hospital-at-home. Stel is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

providers.name: WINT
providers.description: WINT (also styled Wint) is an AI-powered water management and leak-detection platform for commercial and industrial facilities. Its IoT flow sensors, automated shut-off valves, and 24/7 staffed monitoring center use signal processing and anomaly detection to catch leaks in real time across main feeds, domestic cold and hot water, HVAC loops, cooling towers, and irrigation systems, reporting 20-25% average water-consumption reduction and up to 90% less water damage and insurance loss. WINT is backed by Insight Partners and carries NSF International, ISO, and USGBC affiliations. During enrichment no public developer API, documentation, well-known discovery surface, OpenAPI, or SDK was found; this profile captures the company's public web properties and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Bloxtel
providers.description: Bloxtel, Inc. builds a decentralized private 5G platform that lets enterprises deploy standalone 5G networks in hours. Its all-in-one 5G Access Point runs Open6GC, Bloxtel's decentralized network core, and pairs with tokenized dSIM electronic-SIM technology and a Web3 Operator dApp for configuring networks, managing dSIM subscriptions, and AI-powered predictive maintenance. Solutions span indoor coverage, SIM-swap protection, neutral hosting, peer nodes, and network analytics, targeting lower latency, reduced threat surface, and lower cost versus traditional carrier deployments. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Bloxtel publishes a marketing and lead-generation site only, with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK yet available.

providers.name: E-Peas
providers.description: e-peas is a Belgian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2014 in Louvain-la-Neuve that designs power management integrated circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting, enabling battery-free and battery-assisted IoT devices to power themselves from ambient energy. Its flagship Ambient Energy Manager (AEM) family harvests from photovoltaic (light), thermal, vibration/piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid multi-source inputs, and the company also develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers for autonomous data acquisition. e-peas positions itself as a pioneer of the "Ambient IoT" concept serving smart buildings, industrial IoT, consumer electronics, and wearables, with an ecosystem of 30+ partners including Panasonic, TDK, Vishay, and Silicon Labs. This is a hardware/silicon company that does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: INGU
providers.description: INGU is a pipeline integrity technology company delivering inline inspection for oil & gas and water/wastewater pipelines through its Pipers multi-sensor free-floating inspection system paired with AI analytics and GIS-based pipeline viewer software. The platform performs leak detection, deposit and wall-condition assessment, and detection of gas pockets, magnetic features, bends, and hot taps across pipelines of any diameter or material. INGU has inspected over 900 pipelines for operators including Chevron, Shell, TotalEnergies, SUEZ, and Vale. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; the company publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Optiwatt
providers.description: Optiwatt is a consumer-centric energy management platform that helps electric-vehicle drivers and homeowners lower their electricity bills by automatically scheduling EV charging and smart-thermostat use for off-peak, low-cost, and low-carbon hours. Its consumer app (getoptiwatt.com) connects to vehicles, chargers, and thermostats via direct OEM integrations such as the Tesla Fleet API and aggregators like Smartcar, while its utility platform (optiwatt.com) orchestrates these distributed energy resources as virtual power plants across demand-response and load-shaping programs for utility partners. Backed by GV. Optiwatt is primarily a consumer of third-party APIs rather than a public API producer; no public developer API or OpenAPI has been found.

providers.name: Pragmatic
providers.description: Pragmatic Semiconductor Limited is a UK semiconductor manufacturer that designs and produces FlexICs - ultra-thin, physically flexible integrated circuits built on thin-film transistor (TFT) technology rather than conventional crystalline silicon. Founded in 2010 by Richard Price and Scott White and headquartered at Cambridge Science Park with manufacturing at Pragmatic Park in Sedgefield, County Durham, the company operates the Pragmatic FlexIC Foundry, a service that takes third-party custom flexible IC designs from tape-out to delivery in roughly six weeks. Product lines include the FlexIC Platform Gen 3 mixed-signal flexible ASIC design flow, Pragmatic NFC Connect and Pragmatic NFC Protect. The company raised a $231M Series D in 2023. Its only network-reachable API surface is the undocumented, authentication-gated backend of its customer portal; it publishes no developer program, no machine-readable contract and no public API reference.

providers.name: Prisma Photonics
providers.description: Prisma Photonics is an infrastructure-monitoring company that turns existing optical fiber into a continuous sensing network using its Hyper-Scan Fiber-Sensing distributed acoustic sensing technology. The platform measures strain, temperature, pressure, and acoustic signatures at every point along hundreds of kilometers of fiber with sub-meter resolution, and applies AI-driven classification to detect and identify events in real time. It is used to protect and monitor power lines, oil and gas pipelines, perimeters, subsea assets, and smart rail and road infrastructure. Backed by Insight Partners, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Prophetic
providers.description: Prophetic is a San Francisco-based neurotechnology startup, incorporated in January 2023, building the world's first wearable device for stabilizing lucid dreams. Its "Halo" headband pairs EEG sensing with targeted transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) to noninvasively stimulate the prefrontal cortex, driven by an in-house AI model, Morpheus-1, that takes brain activity as its prompt and generates shaped ultrasonic waveforms as output. Backed by BoxGroup and a16z's Scout Fund, Prophetic sells its neuromodulation headbands direct-to-consumer. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Prophetic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic integration surface — it is a consumer hardware and wellness company.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: REEV
providers.description: REEV is a medical-technology company developing AI-powered wearable robotics for mobility recovery and neurological gait rehabilitation. Its REEV SENSE platform uses smart shoe- and leg-mounted sensors to analyze gait and visualize biomarkers in a mobile app, and its DREEVEN motorized knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO) delivers robotic walking assistance personalized from REEV SENSE gait data. REEV serves outpatient clinics and rehabilitation centers treating stroke, multiple sclerosis, and paraplegia, and is backed by Techstars, NVIDIA Inception, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: Youredi
providers.description: Youredi is a technology company that provides a platform for managing and integrating IoT devices across various industries. The company offers APIs for device registration, data ingestion, real-time monitoring, and analytics, enabling developers to build scalable solutions for smart environments. While detailed public documentation is limited, the platform appears to focus on secure device communication, data privacy, and flexible integration options for enterprise customers.

providers.name: Aeterlink
providers.description: Aeterlink Corp. is a Tokyo-headquartered deep-tech company, originating from Stanford University research, that develops, manufactures and sells spatial (microwave) wireless power transfer systems under the AirPlug brand. AirPlug delivers power to battery-free IoT sensors and devices at distances of roughly 15-20 meters with bidirectional data communication, and is sold into factory automation, building management and medical implant applications. Founded in August 2020, the company operates offices in Tokyo, Indianapolis and Bangkok, and is active in the international standardization of spatial wireless power transfer. Aeterlink publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; its product materials are distributed by request form.

providers.name: Drover AI
providers.description: Drover AI is a Los Angeles-based micromobility technology company that pioneers the use of computer vision, machine learning, and proprietary sensor fusion in shared light electric vehicles (LEVs) such as e-scooters and e-bikes. Its flagship PathPilot module is a plug-and-play IoT unit retrofit onto existing fleet vehicles that delivers granular infrastructure distinction (sidewalk, bike lane, crosswalk, street), real-time parking validation, and the ability to control vehicle behavior (speed reduction, throttle disable) based on rider location. The Drover Corral dashboard surfaces real-time compliance insights and validation to operators and cities in line with the MDS 2.0 standard, delivered via API and automated Slack alerts. Partners and customers include Spin, Voi, Bolt, Beam, Dott, and Felyx. Drover AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published; integration is handled directly with operators.

providers.name: Flowserve
providers.description: Flowserve moves, controls and protects the flow of materials in the world's most critical industries through pumps, seals, valves, and flow control systems. No public developer APIs have been identified; the company offers digital services such as RedRaven IIoT monitoring through customer engagements rather than an open developer portal.

providers.name: Nanit
providers.description: Nanit is a consumer smart baby-monitoring company whose camera-based system tracks infant sleep patterns, monitors breathing motion through wearable Breathing Wear, and sends real-time safety notifications to parents. Its products pair 1080p HD video with computer-vision analytics, alongside a companion mobile app, sound machines, and sleep-guidance content, sold direct-to-consumer as hardware plus app subscriptions. As of this enrichment pass Nanit publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or webhook surface for third-party integration.

providers.name: Preteckt
providers.description: Preteckt provides AI-powered predictive maintenance for transit buses, coach buses, and trucking fleets. Its platform ingests vehicle sensor telemetry and applies machine-learning algorithms to detect maintenance issues before they cause breakdowns, reducing diagnostic time by nearly 50 percent and preventing roughly 20 percent of failures. Preteckt processes more than one million sensor data points per day per vehicle across 20+ maintenance-focused algorithms. The company is part of Diesel Laptops. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Preteckt publishes no public developer, API, documentation, or sign-up surface.

providers.name: swap
providers.description: Swap provides city‑based infrastructure of battery swapping stations for e‑motorcycle riders, enabling rapid battery exchange in 9 seconds. This service reduces range anxiety, supports sustainable urban mobility, and offers a platform for operators to manage stations, monitor usage, and integrate with smart city initiatives, fostering a greener transportation ecosystem across multiple cities.

providers.name: Timeseer.ai
providers.description: Timeseer.ai provides an industrial data validation platform that uses AI to ensure sensor data integrity across IIoT devices. By detecting drift, gaps, and anomalies in real time, it helps businesses avoid decisions based on faulty data, improves operational reliability, and reduces downtime. The solution integrates with existing IT/OT systems, offers out‑of‑the‑box checks, and supports seamless API access for developers to embed validation into workflows.

providers.name: Casa
providers.description: Casa provides a smart home security platform that integrates door locks, cameras, and alarm systems into a unified mobile experience. The company focuses on user‑friendly design, robust encryption, and seamless integration with third‑party IoT devices, offering both subscription and one‑time purchase options for consumers and property managers. Founded in 2020, Casa has grown to serve millions of households across North America and Europe, emphasizing privacy, reliability, and continuous software updates.

providers.name: Motorq
providers.description: Motorq is a connected vehicle intelligence platform that taps native OEM connectivity to deliver AI-powered insights across the automotive ecosystem. It aggregates and normalizes vehicle telematics data from 25+ automotive brands and third-party sources without plug-in hardware or dongles, so fleets, fleet management companies, dealerships, lenders, insuretechs, and mobility companies can drive maintenance, safety, utilization, and EV use cases. Motorq offers access through a cloud fleet management portal, bi-directional APIs and data streams (Get Location, Create Geofence, and more), and a Snowflake data lake integration. Its Motorq Fuse AI layer surfaces prioritized recommendations ranked by severity and cost impact. API access is gated to enterprise and OEM partners; there is no public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI definition. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Oriient
providers.description: Oriient provides software-only, hardware-free indoor positioning ("indoor GPS") and navigation delivered as a SaaS SDK. Its geomagnetic technology reaches roughly 1-meter (3-foot) accuracy indoors without Wi-Fi, beacons, or installed infrastructure, powering product finding, order picking, visitor navigation, asset tracking, and in-store analytics for retail, grocery, and smart-building customers across thousands of locations. Oriient New Media Ltd is based in Tel Aviv and is a Techstars portfolio company. Oriient ships first-party mobile SDKs (including a React-Native Product Location AI package on npm) rather than a public REST API; integration is gated behind a customer dashboard and sales.

providers.name: Philips
providers.description: A Dutch multinational health technology company focused on diagnostic imaging, patient monitoring, image-guided therapy, ultrasound, sleep and respiratory care, and connected care solutions. Philips transitioned from a diversified electronics conglomerate to a dedicated healthcare technology leader and operates the HealthSuite Digital Platform (HSDP) as its cloud-based platform for connected health applications. HSDP exposes Identity & Access Management, Provisioning, IoT/Connect, Foundation, Cognitive, Clinical Data, and Notification building blocks to enable consumer health and professional healthcare applications, but access is gated behind a customer portal at www.hsdp.io with developer documentation distributed to authenticated customers and partners rather than the open public web. Philips also operates vertical Connected Care offerings (Patient Monitoring, eICU/Capsule, Sleep & Respiratory Care/SimplyGo, IntelliSpace) layered on HSDP. The legacy Philips Hue lighting API is no longer a Philips offering - Hue has been spun off into Signify and is published at developers.meethue.com.

providers.name: AutoTrac
providers.description: AutoTrac is a Brazilian fleet management and vehicle tracking technology company with over 30 years of experience. As the national market leader, AutoTrac provides satellite and cellular fleet tracking solutions, real-time telemetry, driver journey management, and management intelligence platforms for logistics, agriculture, maritime, and insurance sectors. The company operates its own terrestrial satellite communication station and data center for nationwide coverage.

providers.name: CeQur Simplicity
providers.description: CeQur Simplicity provides a wearable mealtime insulin patch designed to simplify insulin delivery for people with diabetes. The patch offers discreet, painless dosing, reduces the need for multiple injections, and aims to improve glucose control and adherence. The company’s website offers product details, getting started guides, coverage information, FAQs, and resources for both patients and healthcare professionals.

providers.name: Feel Therapeutics
providers.description: Feel Therapeutics, an IQVIA business, is a Digital Precision Medicine company on a mission to reinvent how mental health is diagnosed, managed and cared for by bringing objective data, continuous passive measurement and novel digital biomarkers into mental healthcare. Rather than relying on episodic, subjective self-reported questionnaires, Feel develops digital biomarkers from wearable and passive sensor data to enable continuous, objective monitoring. Its solutions span the Feel Digital Precision Medicine Platform (DPMP), Feel DTx precision digital therapeutics, drug-plus / beyond-the-pill programs, and a wearable monitoring device. The company partners with pharma and biotech to advance clinical development, real-world evidence (RWE), and commercialization strategies, and has run 20+ research studies with 3000+ participants.

providers.name: Huawei FusionSolar
providers.description: Huawei FusionSolar provides intelligent solar energy solutions, including photovoltaic inverters, energy storage systems, and management platforms for residential, commercial, and utility-scale solar projects. The platform offers monitoring, design tools, and a developer portal for integrating solar data and services.

providers.name: ainode-tech
providers.description: Ainode Tech is a Portuguese company specializing in AI‑enhanced wearables. It provides audited, privacy‑focused wearable devices, offering detailed methodology, reviews, and a curated shop. The site includes extensive documentation on its auditing process, a blog, podcast, and clear privacy and terms pages, positioning itself as a trusted authority for consumers seeking secure AI wearables.

providers.name: eWeLink (ITEAD / Sonoff)
providers.description: eWeLink, developed by ITEAD and known for the Sonoff line, provides a cloud‑based platform that connects smart home devices to mobile apps, voice assistants, and third‑party services. Users can control lights, switches, sensors, cameras, and more through the eWeLink app, web portal, or integrations with Alexa, Google Home, Home Assistant, and other ecosystems. The service offers device management, scene automation, firmware updates, and remote access, serving millions of users worldwide across 170+ countries.

providers.name: Frontlinewildfire
providers.description: Frontline Wildfire Defense is a wildfire protection company that designs, manufactures, and installs exterior sprinkler defense systems for homes, businesses, wineries, summer camps, and new-home communities. The system combines roof- and ground-mounted sprinklers, a pump, and water/foam concentrate with a mobile app (iOS and Android) that lets property owners remotely activate the system, monitor nearby wildfires on a live fire map, and receive evacuation alerts. The company also publishes wildfire risk maps, home-hardening and defensible-space guidance, and works through a network of partner installers. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a consumer/hardware company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Inofab
providers.description: Inofab Health (a Clario company) is a digital respiratory health company headquartered in Ankara, Turkey, building connected spirometry and inhaler devices with cloud software for the home-based and clinical management of chronic respiratory conditions including asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis. Its product line spans the SpiroHome Personal portable ultrasonic spirometer, the SpiroClinic Pro and SpiroClinic Compact clinical-grade spirometers with EHR integration, the SpiroCloud web dashboard that collects and analyzes data from all connected SpiroHome and SpiroClinic devices, and the SpiroHaler smart inhaler attachments for medication adherence. Inofab was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: KiddoWear
providers.description: KiddoWear (now operating as Kiddo Health) is a pediatric healthcare technology company that offers a connected care platform for capturing and sharing health data for children with physical and behavioral health challenges. The platform combines biometric tracking of 12+ biomarkers (respiration, heart rate, stress scores, and sleep), family journaling of behavior and health status between visits, educational family resources, care navigation that integrates with medical records and clinical workflows, and a provider dashboard that surfaces insights and real-time health trends. Kiddo Health serves behavioral health conditions such as ADHD and autism spectrum disorder and metabolic conditions such as childhood obesity and diabetes, bridging gaps between families, providers, and care teams across health plans, health systems, and employers. A Techstars-backed portfolio company added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Lumos Helmet
providers.description: Lumos (Lumos Helmet) is a consumer hardware company that designs and manufactures smart bike helmets and connected bike lights with integrated safety features such as turn signals, brake lights, and high-visibility LED lighting. Its product line spans commuter, e-bike, and kids' helmets plus standalone smart bike lights, controlled through companion iOS and Android mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Lumos sells direct-to-consumer through an online store; it does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed no programmatic API surface and captured the company's identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Omnitracs
providers.description: Omnitracs is a commercial fleet management, telematics, and transportation-management provider, now part of Solera Inc. (acquired 2021, operating under Solera Fleet Solutions). Its Omnitracs One platform and the Omnitracs Roadnet routing platform serve roughly 15,000 fleet customers with ELD / Hours-of-Service compliance, telematics and GPS positioning, driver workflow and messaging, routing and dispatch, and video safety. Omnitracs exposes real integration APIs and web services (Roadnet Web Services, the Services Portal Entity Management web services, and the SOAP/XML Event Subscription Service that streams positions, messages, HOS, and critical events), but access is partner- and customer-account gated - there is no open, self-service public developer portal. API credentials (a username/password with API access) and the integration developer wiki are provisioned to contracted customers and integration partners. Endpoints documented here for gated surfaces are honestly modeled from public integration notes, not from an open reference.

providers.name: Open Bionics
providers.description: Open Bionics is a Bristol, UK-based medical technology company that designs and manufactures advanced multi-grip bionic arms for children and adults with upper-limb differences. Its Hero product family (Hero ARM, Hero PRO, Hero RGD, Hero FLEX and Hero GAUNTLET) pairs 3D-printed, lightweight myoelectric prosthetic hands with an ecosystem of MyoPods wireless electrodes and the Sidekick companion app, delivered through a network of specialist prosthetists and clinics in the US and UK. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Renpho
providers.description: Renpho, founded in 2016 in California, USA, creates state‑of‑the‑art lifestyle and wellness solutions, including smart scales, massage devices, and health‑tracking apps. Their mission is to make premium wellness technology accessible to all, empowering individuals to monitor and improve their health through connected devices and intuitive software.

providers.name: Roost
providers.description: Roost is a Sunnyvale, California home-telematics company that helps property and casualty insurance carriers modernize homeowners and commercial insurance with smart, in-home sensors and monitoring. Its Protection360 commercial loss-prevention service and Security360 white-label home-security bundle detect water leaks, extreme temperatures, and smoke-alarm events, delivering real-time alerts and risk data to insurers, property owners, and third parties. Roost partners with dozens of top P&C carriers, but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; integrations are arranged directly with its engineering team.

providers.name: STAND+
providers.description: STAND+ is a Techstars-backed footwear company making biomechanically engineered "energy-recovery" shoes for people who spend long hours standing or walking - healthcare workers, frontline and workforce professionals, athletes, and everyday movers. Its proprietary midsole is designed to dissipate and disperse impact energy outward rather than returning it into the joints, which the company markets for fatigue and pain reduction. The product lineup includes the AntiGrav1, AntiGrav2, and AG3 recovery shoes, the Gales Pro and Gales Frontline workforce and healthcare lines, and standalone recovery insoles.
