STAND+ is APMA (American Podiatric Medical Association) certified and HSA/FSA eligible through a Truemed partnership. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand (standshoes.com) with no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Wellxai
providers.description: Wellx (Wellxai) is a Dubai-based health insurtech company that transforms health insurance from reactive to proactive through AI-driven behavior change. Its consumer mobile app pairs behavioral science and gamification with wearable integrations (Fitbit, Apple Watch, Whoop) so members earn xCoins rewards by hitting health goals, step and sleep challenges, and wellness programs, then redeem them with marketplace partners. Wellx also sells to corporates and SMEs and partners with brokers and insurers, positioning healthier behavior as the driver of better-value health insurance. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company exposes consumer iOS/Android apps backed by a private API but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Connectivity Standards Alliance
providers.description: The Connectivity Standards Alliance (CSA) is a global industry consortium that develops and promotes open standards for the Internet of Things (IoT). It oversees the Matter, Zigbee, and Aliro specifications, providing certification programs, testing tools, and resources for manufacturers and developers to ensure interoperable, secure IoT products. CSA engages members worldwide through events, developer resources, and a community portal.

providers.name: Ekahaa Solutions
providers.description: Ekahaa Solutions provides a no‑code data abstraction platform called Abstracta™ that enables effortless data ingestion, quality control, and API generation with GraphQL flexibility. It targets IoT‑based business use cases, offering event‑driven data propagation, secure data access with RSA key pairs, and rapid deployment on Kubernetes. The platform helps organizations accelerate data abstraction initiatives, reduce integration complexity, and improve operational efficiency across cloud environments.

providers.name: Globalstar
providers.description: Globalstar provides satellite communications solutions, offering voice and data services for a range of industries including IoT, emergency response, and enterprise mobility. Their platform delivers always‑on connectivity through a global network of low‑earth‑orbit satellites, enabling tracking, monitoring, and two‑way communication for devices and personnel in remote locations.

providers.name: Kardome Technology
providers.description: Kardome develops Voice AI technology that lets voice-integrated products hear and understand speech with human-level accuracy in complex, real-world acoustic environments. Its two core technologies are Spatial Hearing AI, which understands the acoustic scene to localize sound sources and attribute speech to the correct speaker, and Cognition AI, which adds contextual awareness so devices understand what people mean in the moment. Kardome targets automotive in-car voice UI and smart-home voice interaction in noisy environments. The company is a Techstars portfolio company, tracked in the API Evangelist network; it licenses embedded voice technology to device makers rather than publishing a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Kepler Communications
providers.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.

providers.name: Shelly
providers.description: Shelly is a global IoT company that designs and manufactures smart home devices, including Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth switches, plugs, sensors, energy meters, and controllers. Their products enable users to automate lighting, climate, security, and energy management through mobile apps and integrations with platforms like Home Assistant and major voice assistants.

providers.name: Aiper
providers.description: Aiper is a consumer robotics company that designs and sells cordless robotic pool cleaners, solar-powered pool skimmers and smart yard-care hardware (the Scuba, Surfer/EcoSurfer, Pilot and IrriSense lines), sold in more than 7,000 stores across 50+ countries with a US base in The Woodlands, Texas. Its devices are paired to the Aiper mobile app, which talks to a regional cloud control plane at apiamerica/apieurope/apiasia.aiper.com plus an AWS IoT MQTT layer. That cloud surface is a private first-party app backend: Aiper publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable contract, and every anonymous request to those hosts is answered with an authentication error. The only clients that speak it are unofficial, community reverse-engineered Home Assistant and Homebridge integrations.

providers.name: C3.ai (C3 IoT)
providers.description: C3.ai (C3 IoT) provides an enterprise AI platform delivering AI-driven applications across industries such as manufacturing, energy, defense, and healthcare. The company offers a suite of products including C3 AI Studio, C3 Code, and generative AI tools, enabling customers to build, deploy, and operate AI solutions at scale. Its platform integrates data, models, and business logic, supporting use cases like demand planning, process optimization, and predictive maintenance.

providers.name: Iceotope
providers.description: Iceotope Technologies is a Sheffield, UK precision liquid cooling company founded in 2005 as a research-driven "green computing" venture, now supplying chassis-level liquid cooling for AI, HPC, data center and edge infrastructure. Its "direct to everything" single-phase immersion approach removes heat from every component rather than the processor alone, and ships as two product lines: KUL BOX for near-edge AI and HPC deployments, and KUL AI liquid-cooled server chassis for high-density rack environments. The company licenses its thermal IP (228 patents granted, allowed and pending) and works through OEM/ODM partnerships with vendors including HPE, Intel and nVent. Iceotope is a hardware and thermal-engineering business: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Laminar
providers.description: Laminar provides spectral sensor technology and AI-driven analytics for food, beverage, and CPG manufacturers. Their in‑line sensors enable real‑time monitoring of cleaning‑in‑place (CIP) processes, product changeovers, and overall line performance, helping factories reduce downtime, waste, and energy consumption while improving product quality.

providers.name: Spartan Radar
providers.description: Spartan Radar is an automotive radar software and sensing company, now operating as the radar technology brand of Pro-Vision Solutions, LLC following its 2025 acquisition. Its Clarify software applies proprietary digital signal processing and machine-learning perception to existing automotive radar sensors, raising resolution 3-8x on commodity silicon (ARM Cortex, Texas Instruments TDA4VM and AWR, NVIDIA Orin and DRIVE, NXP SAF85xx/SAF86xx) without new hardware, and its Hoplo product is a software-defined collision-avoidance and blind-spot warning system for commercial and heavy vehicles across mining, construction, material handling and logistics. Spartan sells to commercial-vehicle OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers and fleet operators as embedded software and hardware; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: BrainCo
providers.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

providers.name: Cool Planet
providers.description: CoolPlanet is an enterprise energy-management and decarbonisation software company. Its platform, CoolPlanetOS, centralises real-time energy data across multi-site industrial estates, applies AI-driven anomaly detection and efficiency insights, benchmarks performance across facilities, and automates energy and compliance reporting. CoolPlanet pairs the software with consulting and on-site execution services to help manufacturing, pharmaceutical, food and beverage, commercial real estate, mining and shipping enterprises cut energy costs and carbon emissions. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). No public developer API surface is currently published.

providers.name: EcoG
providers.description: EcoG is a Munich-based technology company that builds the software and hardware platform powering electric-vehicle DC fast chargers. Its EcoG OS operating system, Universal Core platform, and controllers let charger manufacturers, charge point operators (CPOs), and EV businesses design, launch, and scale DC charging solutions with reduced complexity, claiming more than 15% market share in Europe with operations across India and North America. For developers, EcoG OS exposes an on-device programmatic surface (an OpenAPI-based application interface, a local web interface, and the LifeC remote management tool) so smart value-added charging applications can be built and run at the device level. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from EcoG's public website; it publishes no public REST API developer portal or specification.

providers.name: Stellapps
providers.description: Stellapps is an end-to-end dairy technology company from Bangalore, India (IIT Madras incubated, founded 2011) that digitizes milk production, milk procurement, and cold-chain management through its SmartMoo full-stack IoT platform. Sensors in milking systems, animal wearables, chilling equipment, and procurement peripherals stream data to the SmartMoo Big Data Cloud for analytics and machine learning serving dairy farmers, cooperatives, and processors, with applications including mooON herd management, smartAMCU and smartCC milk procurement, ConTrak cold-chain monitoring, mooFlow ERP, and mooPay financial services. Stellapps publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; the SmartMoo platform is accessed through hosted applications behind CAS single sign-on.

providers.name: Aclima
providers.description: Aclima is a San Francisco-based environmental intelligence company that maps and analyzes air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions at hyperlocal, block-by-block resolution. Using a network of roving (vehicle-mounted) and stationary sensors, Aclima measures multiple pollutants and climate gases simultaneously at up to 100,000x greater resolution than traditional monitoring, then translates billions of scientific measurements into environmental intelligence for governments, companies, and communities. Its professional analytics software, Aclima Pro, delivers visualization and automated analytics for emissions reduction and public-health programs, while its free air.health app maps address-level air and climate insights for the communities Aclima serves. Co-founded by CEO Davida Herzl, Aclima is backed by DCVC and is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Assa Abloy
providers.description: Assa Abloy is a global leader in access solutions, providing a wide range of electronic and mechanical locking systems, door automation, and identity management products. The company serves billions of users worldwide across sectors such as commercial buildings, residential properties, transportation, and healthcare. Through its extensive portfolio of brands, Assa Abloy delivers innovative security technologies that enhance safety and convenience, supporting digital transformation and smart building initiatives.

providers.name: Boréastechnologies
providers.description: Boréastechnologies, operating as Boréas Technologies, designs and manufactures ultra‑low power piezoelectric drivers and haptic solutions for smartphones, automotive, and IoT devices. Their product line includes CapDrive® drivers, development kits, and software tools, supported by extensive technical documentation, integration guides, and a developer portal.

providers.name: Netatmo
providers.description: Netatmo designs and manufactures smart home devices such as weather stations, security cameras, and smart thermostats. Their products connect to the Netatmo Connect platform, offering APIs for accessing device data, managing settings, and integrating with third‑party services. The company provides a developer portal with documentation, authentication guides, and SDKs for building applications that leverage their smart‑home ecosystem.

providers.name: Payment24
providers.description: Payment24 is a white-label payment platform specializing in fuel and fleet payment solutions for oil companies, banks, and retailers, primarily across Africa. Its technology lets clients design and launch branded payment products under their own name — fuel payments and mobile payments, loyalty and rewards, POS terminals, electronic vouchers, B2B and B2C prepaid and store-account cards, EV charging payments, and wet-stock and fuel-in-tank management — alongside banking-grade issuing, acquiring, card management, and merchant management, plus fleet fuel management and telematics. Payment24 operates as a technology partner rather than a public self-serve API provider, so it publishes no open developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Inspiren
providers.description: Inspiren is a healthcare technology company providing an AI-powered ecosystem for senior living communities that combines hardware and software to improve resident safety, care planning, and staff efficiency. Its platform pairs devices such as the AUGi sensor, Sense, Help Button, Resident Pendant, and Staff Beacon with the Inspiren HQ software platform and mobile app to deliver emergency call, real-time fall prevention and safety monitoring, data-driven care insights, and staff workflow coordination. Inspiren reports outcomes including reductions in falls, faster alert response times, and improved occupancy for the communities it serves. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and Scale Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; Inspiren does not publish a public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Scout
providers.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Skyworks Solutions
providers.description: Skyworks Solutions, Inc. is an American semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California that designs, develops, and markets proprietary semiconductor products for wireless communications, automotive, broadband, connected home, industrial, defense, and consumer electronics applications. Skyworks is a leading provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, with dominant market share in 5G RF front-end modules (35% market share). Products span amplifiers, filters, front-end modules, isolators, switches, and power management ICs serving mobile, automotive, IoT, and infrastructure markets. The company does not publish a public developer API but provides datasheets, evaluation tools, and design resources for hardware engineers.

providers.name: Atlas5D
providers.description: Atlas5D is a healthcare technology company that develops an Ambient Measurement System (AMS) for assessing health and wellness through motion in any environment. Its passive, privacy-preserving sensor platform recognizes specific individuals, characterizes and quantifies their movement, and interprets daily routines to predict trends and assess risk of adverse events such as falls, without wearables, without transmitting video, and without storing images. Atlas5D serves individuals monitoring aging loved ones, assisted-living and other institutional care settings, and healthcare and clinical-trial teams that need clinical-grade, real-world evidence of patient movement wherever people live. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Binsentry
providers.description: BinSentry provides AI‑driven feed management solutions for animal feed and grain operations. Using computer‑vision sensors, it creates 3‑D images of bin contents, delivering real‑time inventory data, alerts, and analytics via a cloud dashboard. The platform helps producers, integrators, and feed mills reduce waste, improve safety, and optimize logistics across thousands of bins worldwide.

providers.name: Carnot Fleet
providers.description: Carnot Fleet (Carnotfleet) is a Seoul-based cold-chain technology company that converts non-refrigerated vehicles into temperature-controlled units in under 30 minutes using modular insulation panels and proprietary solid-state thermoelectric heat pumps, spanning frozen, chilled, and ambient ranges with humidity control. Its Adaptive Thermal Control System (ATCS) is an AI-based autonomous control platform delivering cloud-connected temperature monitoring at 10-second intervals. Carnot Fleet surfaces its capabilities through the CF Mobile Application, the CF Portal, and CF APIs that let customers integrate the ATCS into existing logistics solutions to detect, analyze, prevent, and discover cold-chain data points and reduce post-harvest to pre-retail loss across the supply chain.

providers.name: Humatics
providers.description: Humatics Corporation is a Waltham, Massachusetts microlocation company founded in 2015 by MIT professor David Mindell and led by CEO James Kinsey. It builds radio-frequency positioning systems — ultra-wideband beacons, RF-pulse ranging, radar and inertial sensors fused in software — that locate people, vehicles and robots at centimeter- to millimeter-scale precision. Two product lines are on sale today: MILO, a sub-millimeter positioning system for industrial automation and in-motion robotics, advertised as compatible with Yaskawa, Mitsubishi Electric, FANUC, Universal Robots and KUKA; and Mobility, a rail and transit portfolio covering the FOCUS track-geometry monitoring kit and the Humatics Rail Navigation System (HRNS), used on New York City MTA subway signalling projects. Humatics publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable description of any product API. Two rounds of probing humatics.com returned HTTP 404 for every /.well-known/ path, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /graphql; *.humatics.com is a DNS wildcard onto one retired address, so api., docs., developer., portal. and status. resolve but time out on connect. The only machine-readable HTTP interface on any Humatics host is the WordPress REST API of the marketing site itself at humatics.com/wp-json/ — 375 routes across 19 stock core and commercial-plugin namespaces, exposing pages and posts rather than positioning, and so recorded as evidence rather than catalogued as a Humatics API. The GitHub organization github.com/Humatics is real and public, but 31 of its 33 repositories are forks of third-party embedded and robotics open source (Fast-RTPS, Fast-CDR, FreeRTOS, Orange Pi BSP, Yocto meta-layers, EIPScanner, donkeycar); the two non-forks are internal tools. There is no first-party SDK, client library or specification, and no package named humatics exists on npm or PyPI. Marketing material for the earlier KinetIQ OS / Spatial Intelligence Platform referenced an "extensible API", but no public interface for it was ever documented, and the news host that carried those announcements (now.humatics.com) no longer answers.

providers.name: Plumerai
providers.description: Plumerai builds AI software for intelligent cameras that pairs tiny on-device edge AI models with cloud Vision Language Models (VLMs). Its Video Intelligence products cover detection of people, vehicles, animals and packages, Familiar Face Identification, cross-camera Re-Identification, noise-robust motion detection, VLM-based video search, and custom AI notifications. The Plumerai Inference Engine is a deep-learning model compiler and runtime optimized for CPU inference on Arm Cortex-M / Cortex-A, RISC-V and x86_64. Plumerai integrates via SDKs (C++, C, Python, Rust, Java) rather than a hosted REST API, with the same unified API running from microcontrollers to servers. Plumerai also maintains the open-source Larq ecosystem for training and running Binarized Neural Networks.

providers.name: Sensefinity
providers.description: Sensefinity is a supply-chain IoT company ("The IoT Transformation Company") delivering real-time tracking, monitoring, and analytics for global cargo and logistics operations. Its platform combines GPS/NB-IoT tracking devices for maritime containers, pallets, and vehicles with temperature and condition (cold-chain) sensors, indoor location tracking, a cloud analytics and machine learning layer, and digital product passport / blockchain integrations. The operational platform is delivered as a hosted web application (uiadmin.sensefinity.com) and mobile asset-management apps, serving enterprise customers across food, pharma, automotive, and manufacturing supply chains. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published as of this profile; a private API host (api.sensefinity.com) backs the platform.

providers.name: Zonar Systems
providers.description: Zonar provides fleet management technology that improves safety, efficiency, and compliance for transportation companies. Their platform includes telematics, driver tools, predictive maintenance, fuel analytics, and a marketplace of third‑party apps. Zonar serves industries such as construction, utilities, and vocational fleets, offering solutions like asset tracking, dash‑cam video, and electronic logging devices. The company emphasizes safety, regulatory compliance, and operational insight for fleets of all sizes.

providers.name: Aprilgetaprilcom
providers.description: Aprilgetaprilcom, operating as April, provides embedded tax solutions for modern financial platforms. Their AI‑powered tax engine enables platforms to offer tax filing, planning, and estimation tools as white‑label services. The company focuses on delivering a seamless, mobile‑first tax experience integrated into fintech, wealth management, and SMB applications, with compliance certifications and a developer‑focused API suite.

providers.name: Bancada
providers.description: Design and manufacture of custom products: devices, applications and AI that connect to your business. We turn ideas from sketch to functional hardware and software, delivering IoT hardware, firmware, web and mobile apps, and MCP servers. Our team works together in the same workshop, ensuring rapid decision‑making and seamless integration of embedded software and hardware. Based in Barcelona, we serve industrial IoT, prototyping, and bespoke product development.

providers.name: Dominion Dynamics
providers.description: Dominion Dynamics Inc. is a Canadian defence-technology company (Kanata/Ottawa, Ontario) building the autonomy stack for the Arctic and other extreme, infrastructure-constrained operating environments. It develops integrated autonomy, edge sensing, communications, and command-and-control systems for defence, security, and critical infrastructure. Its AuraNet platform is a peer-to-peer sensor mesh that fuses EO/IR/SAR imagery, SIGINT/EW/RF signals, telemetry, and structured reporting into a unified local intelligence stream that interoperates with existing allied C2 architectures, and its Aurion product is an open-source government procurement intelligence platform built on Canadian federal open data. Founded by Anduril alum Eliot Pence, the company raised a $139M CAD Series A (2026) led by Georgian. This profile currently has no public developer/API surface; the entry captures the company identity, security.txt, and llms.txt the company publishes.

providers.name: Dotnova
providers.description: Desenvolvemos soluções de software de ponta que impulsionam a evolução e a eficiência do seu negócio. Dotnova provides cutting‑edge software solutions to drive evolution and efficiency for businesses.

providers.name: Hyper Nexus
providers.description: Hyper Nexus (北京超级联接科技有限公司) provides industrial LTE and 5G RedCap modems, mmWave radar health monitoring, and AI messenger solutions. Their products include MF833V, Dongle 400, F40, HN‑X1 radar and Hala messenger, serving over 1.4M devices in 60+ countries with global certifications and custom firmware.

providers.name: LF Edge
providers.description: LF Edge is an umbrella organization under the Linux Foundation establishing an open, interoperable framework for edge computing independent of hardware, silicon, cloud, or operating system. It hosts projects like Akraino, EdgeX Foundry, and Open Horizon.

providers.name: Tozuda
providers.description: Tozuda is a Philadelphia-based safety technology company that makes mechanical, non-electronic head impact indicators for helmets. The patented indicator changes from clear to red when a helmet sustains force exceeding a set G-force threshold, making hidden helmet damage visible to workers, athletes, and safety inspectors across ANSI, DOT, EN, CSA, CPSC, and SNELL helmet types. Tozuda is a Techstars portfolio company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Understory
providers.description: Understory is an insurtech company headquartered in Madison, Wisconsin (founded 2012) that combines its own network of ground-truth Dot weather sensors with a proprietary weather risk model to underwrite parametric insurance against severe weather, including hail coverage for automotive dealership open lots and agricultural weather risk. Its UnderstoryOS platform covers broker management, pricing and quoting, and automated weather-triggered claims. Understory publishes no public API or developer portal; the platform is offered to insurance partners rather than as a self-service developer product.

providers.name: Biobeat
providers.description: Biobeat Technologies is an Israeli med-tech company whose remote patient monitoring (RPM) health-AI platform pairs a disposable short-term chest-monitor and a reusable long-term wrist-monitor - both using a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor - to continuously track up to 13 vital signs, including FDA-cleared cuffless blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation, temperature, stroke volume, cardiac output, and one-lead ECG (chest-monitor). Readings stream to Biobeat's HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant, cloud-based patient management platform, where clinicians view real-time data, trends, and configurable alerts. Biobeat offers programmatic data access and EMR/EHR integration as a paid add-on for hospitals, health systems, and research partners; there is no publicly documented self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Breaker
providers.description: Breaker Industries provides advanced energy management solutions for industrial facilities, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and optimization of power usage across complex operations. Their platform integrates IoT sensors, AI-driven analytics, and a robust API suite that allows customers to retrieve device data, control equipment, and automate workflows. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Breaker aims to reduce energy costs and carbon footprints while improving operational efficiency for manufacturers, data centers, and large-scale infrastructure.

providers.name: Feetme
providers.description: FeetMe is a Paris-based medical device company, founded in 2013, that develops smart connected insoles and digital health software for real-time gait analysis and mobility care. Its CE-marked, ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certified wearables embed plantar pressure sensors and a 6-axis inertial measurement unit to capture more than twenty gait and balance metrics per step, streaming them over Bluetooth Low Energy to the FeetMe Mobility dashboard used by clinicians for neurological, orthopedic and rehabilitation assessment. Product lines include FeetMe Evaluation, FeetMe Rehabilitation, FeetMe Monitor and FeetMe Stimulate. The company is backed by Partech. FeetMe does not currently expose a public developer API or OpenAPI-described web API; a partner SDK for raw-data integration is referenced in product materials but is not publicly documented.

providers.name: HomeBoost
providers.description: HomeBoost is a startup focused on home energy optimization, offering a platform that helps homeowners monitor and improve energy efficiency. Backed by True Ventures, the company provides resources such as a blog with articles on energy audits, DIY upgrades, and smart thermostat guidance. Their website homeboost.com presents product information, pricing, and support resources.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Cepton Technologies
providers.description: Cepton Technologies develops advanced lidar sensors and perception software for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and safety-critical applications. Their products include Vista Ultra, Nova Ultra, and Helius platforms, delivering high-resolution, long-range detection for a variety of industries. The company focuses on safe, reliable, and scalable sensing solutions to enable autonomous transportation and intelligent machines.

providers.name: Green Fusion
providers.description: Green Fusion GmbH is a Berlin-based climate-energy software company that provides an intelligent 360-degree energy management platform for the residential real estate sector (Wohnungswirtschaft). Its software digitizes and optimizes building heating systems: "Der Energiespar-Pilot" delivers digital boiler-room management and optimized operation of conventional heat sources (gas, oil, district heating, CHP/BHKW), while its AI platform for sector coupling (Sektorkopplung) integrates heat pumps, PV systems, storage, and grid connectivity for intelligent monitoring and control. The platform is TUV-certified under GEG section 71a. Green Fusion is backed by HV Capital and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a climate-energy provider; it operates a customer control platform (control.green-fusion.de) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Naviday Health
providers.description: Naviday Health is a Boston-based women's health technology company and Techstars portfolio company building clinical decision support that connects the continuous health data women generate every day from consumer wearables and patient-generated sources to the practitioners who need it most. Its LUCI Care platform surfaces actionable insights for clinicians between appointments, and the company partners with device manufacturers on wearable integration services. Naviday Health is HIPAA compliant and has been recognized by the Mayo Clinic Platform, StartUp Health, and MassChallenge. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Pebble
providers.description: Pebble is a Silicon Valley electric-vehicle and consumer-hardware company that designs and manufactures the Pebble Flow, an all-electric travel trailer (RV) with an integrated battery, solar, and motor-assist drivetrain. The product line pairs the trailer with the Pebble mobile app for remote control and monitoring, offering features such as autonomous "Magic Hitch" coupling, remote-control positioning, automatic leveling and setup, and up to seven days of off-grid capability. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Pebble sells direct-to-consumer under the tagline "Where Home Meets the Road." As of this enrichment pass Pebble publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; its only software touchpoint is the consumer-facing Pebble Control Center app.

providers.name: Securly
providers.description: Securly is a K-12 student safety company whose platform spans web filtering, device management (MDM), classroom management, and student wellness/self-harm and threat monitoring across the web, email, and cloud drives. Securly is deployed by school districts and integrates with the school technology stack - Google Workspace, Microsoft 365/Entra, Apple School Manager, and Student Information Systems via the OneRoster and rostering standards. Securly's public developer surface is limited and access-gated - it primarily CONSUMES rostering and identity APIs from external systems rather than exposing a documented public developer API. The one provider-exposed API is a credential-gated Securly MDM API used by third-party device/asset systems to pull device inventory and assign or unassign students to devices; its endpoints and base URL are provisioned per tenant and are not publicly documented as a reference.

providers.name: Adasky
providers.description: ADASKY (Adasky Ltd.) is an Israeli automotive sensor company founded in January 2016 and headquartered in Yokneam, Israel, that develops and manufactures automotive-grade long-wave infrared (LWIR) thermal imaging cameras and the perception software that runs on them. Its flagship product, Viper, is a compact solid-state shutterless thermal camera with 50mK sensitivity, object detection to about 300 metres and living-being classification beyond 200 metres, sold into ADAS and autonomous-vehicle programs for pedestrian, cyclist and wildlife detection, free-space detection and automatic emergency braking in darkness, glare and fog. A second line, SharpVision, serves intelligent transportation, V2X and smart-city infrastructure. ADASKY publishes no developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification; its software ships embedded in the camera under commercial OEM engagement.

providers.name: B2X
providers.description: B2X is a Munich-founded hardware lifecycle orchestration company that manages the complete service journey of electronic devices for global brands and operators — from warehousing, staging and onsite deployment through customer support, maintenance and repair, returns management, refurbishment and recycling. Its proprietary B2XONE platform combines ONE Connect (self-service customer portals with track & trace and appointment booking), ONE Service (operations management for repair, warehouse, inventory and logistics) and ONE Analytics (real-time KPIs and predictive insights), delivered through a network of 155+ certified service partners across 25+ countries. B2X serves mobile and consumer electronics, retail automation, B2B/enterprise and mission-critical segments. As of this profile, B2X does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Instrumental
providers.description: Instrumental is a platform for manufacturing intelligence that helps companies detect and prevent product failures during the manufacturing process. The Instrumental API enables programmatic access to retrieve unit and inspection test data and metadata from Instrumental projects.

providers.name: Optoscale
providers.description: Optoscale (OptoScale AS) is a Norwegian aquaculture technology company founded in 2015 in Trondheim that builds AI-powered, camera-based edge-computing monitoring for fish farming. Its Bioscope units capture real-time measurements of fish weight, biomass, sea-lice counts, welfare, behaviour and feeding, producing tens of thousands of validated measurements each day directly on the unit rather than on remote servers. Customers view trends, graphs and high-resolution imagery through the OptoScale web portal, export to Excel/CSV, and integrate the underlying data into their own analytics and farm-management systems via OptoScale's data API. OptoScale was acquired by Insight Partners in 2025.

providers.name: Plotlogic
providers.description: Plotlogic is a mining technology company that builds AI-driven sensing systems for real-time ore and material characterisation. Its flagship product, OreSense, scans rock in open-pit, stockpile, and underground mining operations and delivers decision-ready quantitative mineralogy in under 15 minutes, compared with more than an hour for traditional laboratory assay methods. The hardware is engineered for harsh mining environments and integrates into existing operational workflows so mines can reduce waste, improve grade control, and make faster material-routing decisions. Plotlogic is headquartered in Zillmere, Queensland, Australia, and is backed by the deep-tech venture firm DCVC. Customer access is delivered through an enterprise client platform rather than a public developer API; there is no published developer program, SDK, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Alterego
providers.description: Alterego is a Boston-based startup, spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 2025, building a near-telepathic silent-speech interface: a minimal, non-invasive wearable that detects the faint neuromuscular signals produced when a person internally verbalizes words, letting them interact with AI and computers without typing, tapping, or speaking aloud. Its "Silent Sense" technology responds only to intentional internal speech, keeping private thoughts private while enabling hands-free, screen-free messaging, queries, and information access. The company is pre-launch, backed by investors including Canaan, Granite Ventures, Mayfield, Rembrandt Venture Partners, and Cisco Investments. As of this profile Alterego publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Congatec
providers.description: Congatec designs and manufactures embedded computer-on-modules (COM) and system-in-package solutions for industrial, automotive, and IoT applications. Their product portfolio includes COM-HPC, COM Express, SMARC, and Qseven modules, along with aReady services, design‑in training, and support resources. Congatec serves sectors such as automation, medical technology, and transportation, offering customizable modules and carrier board designs to meet performance, low‑power, and server‑class requirements.

providers.name: DNOW
providers.description: DNOW Inc. (NYSE: DNOW), formerly NOW Inc. and operating as DistributionNOW, is a Houston-headquartered Fortune 1000 distributor of pipe, valves, fittings (PVF), pumps and packaged, engineered process and production equipment serving the upstream, midstream, downstream energy, and industrial sectors. Spun off from National Oilwell Varco in 2014 and built on a heritage that spans more than 160 years, DNOW combines a global network of distribution branches and engineering facilities with the DigitalNOW platform — shop.dnow.com B2B eCommerce, cXML/OCI ERP punchout integrations, the eSpec product configurator, the AccessNOW automated inventory control system, and a library of customer-facing mobile applications. DNOW does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, or a self-serve API program; customer integrations are delivered through configured cXML/OCI punchout sessions tied to enterprise ERP systems. In June 2025 DNOW announced a definitive merger agreement to acquire MRC Global in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $1.5 billion.

providers.name: SwitchBot
providers.description: SwitchBot provides smart home automation products, including robotic switches, curtains, bots, and sensors, enabling users to control devices via Bluetooth, Wi‑Fi, and cloud APIs. Their platform offers a developer portal with RESTful APIs for device management, status monitoring, and integration with third‑party services, supporting OAuth2 and API keys for secure access.

providers.name: Volteum
providers.description: Volteum provides fleet electrification and EV fleet management software that helps companies plan, execute, and operate the transition of their vehicle fleets to electric. The platform covers electrification planning, charging optimisation, and live fleet management, connecting directly to vehicles through OEM APIs across 30+ brands with no hardware installation to track mileage, fault codes, charging sessions, maintenance intervals, and costs across electric, diesel, petrol, and hybrid fleets. Volteum is a Techstars portfolio company and publishes no public developer portal; its telematics and fleet-system API integrations are offered to customers directly.

providers.name: Karnott
providers.description: Karnott is a French agricultural technology company based in Lille that builds connected tracking devices and a digital management platform for farms, equipment cooperatives (CUMA), agricultural contractors (ETA), and wine growers. Its beacon automatically records equipment usage and field interventions without manual data entry, enabling real-time fleet and equipment monitoring, fuel-cost tracking, parcel mapping, and precise billing and regulatory documentation. Karnott is a portfolio company of Partech. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found on the provider's public surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Neolink
providers.description: Neolink is an open-source bridge for Reolink cameras that provides an RTSP stream gateway and REST API for managing Reolink IP cameras, enabling integration with NVR software, home automation, and other camera management tools.

providers.name: Yale Home (smart locks)
providers.description: Yale Home (smart locks) designs, manufactures, and sells connected smart lock solutions for residential and commercial use. Their product line includes the Yale Assure Lock series, offering keyless entry via Bluetooth, Wi‑Fi, Z‑Wave, Apple Home Key, and Matter integration. The company provides a consumer‑focused e‑commerce storefront at shopyalehome.com and integrates with major smart‑home ecosystems such as Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Samsung SmartThings.

providers.name: Aiden Auto
providers.description: AiDEN Auto (Aiden Automotive Inc.) is a connected-vehicle software company founded in 2021 by former Volvo Cars connected-services and infotainment engineers, with offices in San Ramon, California and Gothenburg, Sweden. Its software-only platform runs natively on Android Automotive OS (AAOS) infotainment head units and lets automakers, fleets and third-party service providers deliver in-cab mobility services — tolling, parking, fueling and charging, payments, insurance, roadside assistance, maintenance and regulatory compliance such as Poland's SENT cross-border freight reporting — without a phone, a downloaded app, or a bespoke per-OEM integration. AiDEN brokers real-time vehicle signals (fuel level, tire pressure, battery state, engine data, location) to partner backends under an application-level, GDPR/CCPA-aligned consent model, and partners configure signal access and triggers through the AiDEN Portal rather than proprietary OEM APIs. The company is a COVESA member, has raised roughly $11M (a $6.1M oversubscribed seed announced February 2025), holds three patents covering in-vehicle consent, payments and data sharing, and works with Volvo Trucks, HERE Technologies and IF Insurance among others.

providers.name: FANUC
providers.description: FANUC Corporation is a Japanese multinational headquartered in Oshino, Yamanashi at the base of Mount Fuji, and is one of the world's largest suppliers of factory automation, industrial robots, and CNC (computer numerical control) systems. Founded in 1972 after spinning out of Fujitsu's numerical control division (originated 1955) under Seiuemon Inaba, FANUC pioneered commercial NC and CNC technology and by the early 1980s held roughly half of the global CNC market. The company operates three primary business segments: FA (CNC systems, servo motors, lasers, and PMC controls for machine tools), Robot (industrial arms from the LR Mate and M-series through the heavy-payload M-2000iA, plus the CRX collaborative robot family), and ROBOMACHINE (ROBODRILL machining centers, ROBOCUT wire EDM, and ROBOSHOT all-electric injection molding machines). FANUC's primary developer surface is FOCAS (FANUC Open CNC API Specification), a licensed C/C++ library (fwlib32.dll) used by machine builders and MES/OEE vendors to read CNC state over Ethernet, plus KAREL and Teach Pendant (TP) programming on the robot controllers and a published ROS 2 driver for the CRX collaborative arms. FANUC does not operate a public REST developer portal or publish OpenAPI specifications; integrations are partner-driven through MTConnect adapters, OPC UA servers, FIELD system edge apps, and the FANUC America customer/training portals.

providers.name: Open mHealth
providers.description: Open mHealth is a nonprofit, community-driven initiative that develops open standards and open-source software for making patient-generated health data interoperable across mobile apps, wearables, clinical systems, and electronic health records. Its core contribution is a library of clinically validated JSON Schema data point schemas — covering physical activity, sleep, heart rate, blood pressure, body weight, blood glucose, and other vital signs — with the sleep, physical-activity, and metadata schemas now superseded by IEEE 1752.1, the IEEE standard for Mobile Health Data co-shepherded by the Open mHealth community. Around the schemas Open mHealth ships a stack of Apache-2.0 reference implementations: Shimmer (a Java/Spring server that pulls health data from Fitbit, Google Fit, iHealth, Misfit, RunKeeper, and Withings APIs and normalizes it into Open mHealth or IEEE 1752.1 data points), omh-dsu-ri (a Data Storage Unit reference implementation exposing an OAuth 2.0-secured Data Point REST API on top of MongoDB and PostgreSQL), Granola (an Objective-C library that serializes Apple HealthKit samples into Open mHealth JSON), a web visualizations library built on D3 and Plottable.js, the OMH-on-FHIR mapping that aligns Open mHealth data points to HL7 FHIR resources, and a sample-data-generator. Open mHealth operates as the steward of the standard, the schema and unit registry at registry.openmhealth.org, and a developer community of thousands of developers and health organizations including Cornell Tech, Kaiser Permanente, Stanford School of Medicine, UC Davis, and UCSF. The project has no commercial API, no paid tier, and no hosted SaaS — all artifacts are open source under Apache 2.0 and the standard itself is openly published.

providers.name: Sensata Technologies
providers.description: Sensata Technologies is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Sensata Technologies API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: CropX
providers.description: CropX is an Israeli ag-IoT company that combines in-field soil and weather hardware with a cloud Farm Management Software (FMS) platform. The hardware portfolio includes SV-series soil sensors (moisture, temperature, conductivity, salinity at depth), ET-series evapotranspiration sensors, WS-series weather stations, RG rain gauges, the Apex root-zone sensor, an in-development nitrate sensor, and TD-series cellular telemetry gateways. The FMS covers farm / field / crop data, device management, irrigation scheduling, disease monitoring, nutrition, effluent, and reporting. CropX does not publish a public developer portal; integrations with third-party sensors and machinery are arranged through their team.

providers.name: ioBroker (self-hosted)
providers.description: ioBroker is an open-source integration platform for the Internet of Things, allowing users to connect and automate a wide variety of smart home devices, services, and protocols. It provides a modular, plugin‑based architecture where adapters enable communication with devices such as lights, thermostats, sensors, and cloud services. The platform can be self‑hosted on a server, Raspberry Pi, or Docker, offering a flexible, community‑driven solution for home automation enthusiasts and developers.

providers.name: Kinetic
providers.description: Kinetic provides workers' compensation insurance and injury management solutions powered by wearable technology. Their platform combines real-time injury detection, return-to-work coordination, and claims management to help policyholders, brokers, and self-insured businesses reduce costs and improve safety. By integrating reflex wearable devices, Kinetic delivers data-driven insights that enable proactive health monitoring and streamlined compliance for frontline industries.

providers.name: Parklio
providers.description: Seamlessly integrate your existing systems or products with Parklio API so you can scale your operations and monitor parking space usage in real time. It provides access to your data in a way that works best for you, whether through integration, automation, or full customization. The API is RESTful with JSON responses, and Android and iOS SDKs are available on request.

providers.name: Pillar Technologies
providers.description: Pillar Technologies provides construction jobsite risk management through environmental monitoring and data analytics. Its wireless, rugged "Pod" sensors measure eight environmental metrics on the jobsite (temperature, humidity, carbon monoxide, VOCs, particulates, noise, light, and pressure) with cellular connectivity and a one-year battery life, feeding a real-time software platform with customizable dashboards, floorplan integration, and drill-down reporting by site, floor, or sensor. A configurable alert system notifies teams via text, email, or phone. Pillar serves data centers, hospitality and multi-family housing, and science and healthcare construction projects to improve safety and protect schedules and budgets. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Subaru of America
providers.description: Subaru of America, Inc. is the United States subsidiary of Subaru Corporation (Japan), headquartered in Camden, New Jersey. SOA sells, services, and supports the Subaru lineup through more than 600 U.S. dealers and operates the MySubaru / STARLINK connected-vehicle platform that powers the MySubaru mobile app, owner portal, remote vehicle commands, safety and security services, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, and dealer integration. None of these surfaces are exposed as a public developer API; all known interfaces are private, OEM-internal, or partner-only.

providers.name: Hydrow
providers.description: Hydrow (legally True Rowing, Inc., Boston, Massachusetts) is a connected-fitness hardware company that makes the Hydrow indoor rowing machine and the LYQUID strength-training platform, sold with a subscription to a library of live and on-demand athlete-led workouts filmed on real water. Members interact with Hydrow through its rower touchscreens and the Hydrow iOS/Android companion apps, which sync workout summaries outward to Strava and Apple Health. Hydrow operates a real production backend for those apps, but publishes no public developer program, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no first-party SDK in any package registry; its developer-facing subdomains do not resolve to a service. Its public machine-readable surface is limited to an Atlassian Statuspage.

providers.name: OSIsoft
providers.description: OSIsoft was the enterprise software company behind the PI System, the operational data infrastructure used across manufacturing, energy, utilities, oil and gas, and other industrial sectors to collect, historize, contextualize, and visualize high-volume real-time sensor and control-system time-series data. Its developer surface centered on the PI Web API (a RESTful interface to the PI Data Archive and Asset Framework), AF SDK, and the PI Square developer community. OSIsoft was acquired by AVEVA in 2021; all osisoft.com and docs.osisoft.com properties now redirect to AVEVA, where the product ships as the AVEVA PI System. This profile is maintained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network, with developer resources pointing at the live AVEVA successor pages.

providers.name: Reekoh
providers.description: Reekoh is an award‑winning Industrial Integration Cloud platform that enables seamless integration of data from any asset, operational or business system, on the edge or in the cloud. Acquired by Autodesk in 2023, Reekoh provides a toolkit for building IoT, PaaS, and data orchestration solutions, helping enterprises accelerate digital transformation.

providers.name: Prime Financial Technologies
providers.description: Prime Financial Technologies provides embedded, bank‑grade lending solutions for software platforms. It enables developers to integrate compliant credit programs, offering quick deployment, customizable loan products, and real‑time risk management. The company focuses on API‑first services, supporting fintech partners with scalable credit infrastructure and detailed developer resources.

providers.name: Skylo
providers.description: Skylo Technologies is a satellite communications company based in Mountain View, California, operating a global Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) that lets standard smartphones and IoT cellular devices connect directly to satellites over 3GPP Release 17 direct-to-device (D2D) standards for SMS, sensor telemetry, and other low-bandwidth messaging. Founded in 2017 and backed by DCM, SoftBank, Intel Capital, Innovation Endeavors, BMW i Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, Next47, Seraphim Space, and NGP Capital, Skylo has commercial service across the US, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Skylo does not publish a public REST/HTTP API; developer integration is device-level (certified modules such as Quectel, Murata, Blues Notecard and Particle) with detailed procedures gated behind a partner Knowledge Base. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company and its developer surface.

providers.name: EcoPlant
providers.description: EcoPlant provides an intelligent air compressor control and monitoring platform for industrial facilities. The Ecoplant 360 solution uses IoT sensors, AI-powered dynamic controls, and predictive analytics to optimize compressed-air systems in real time, preventing downtime, improving reliability, and reducing compressed-air energy costs by up to 50 percent. It installs in under a week with no installation fees and is compatible with most compressor brands and existing plant technology.

providers.name: Eve Systems
providers.description: Eve Systems designs and manufactures smart home devices that integrate with Apple HomeKit, providing users with intuitive control over heating, lighting, and energy consumption. Their product line includes smart thermostats, radiator valves, smart plugs, and sensors, all managed through the Eve app and supporting Matter standards. The company emphasizes energy efficiency, user-friendly design, and seamless automation across a connected home ecosystem.

providers.name: Gabit
providers.description: Gabit is a one-stop health and wellness platform on a mission to add more healthy years to people's lives. Headquartered in Gurugram, India and founded in 2022 by Gaurav Gupta (ex-Zomato cofounder) and Arpana Shahi, Gabit treats health as an interconnected system across four pillars — fitness, nutrition, sleep, and mindfulness. Its consumer ecosystem spans the titanium Gabit Smart Ring, a smart body-composition scale, at-home Blood Work diagnostics, a continuous glucose monitor (CGM), the Sweden-born Näck nutrition supplement line, all-good-no-harm skincare, and coached Fitness & Nutrition Plans — all unified in the Gabit app, which tracks 150+ biomarkers and includes the free PEP AI health coach. India is the primary market, with Ring-only storefronts in the UAE and UK and an informational US/global page.

providers.name: OWLR
providers.description: OWLR (OWLR Technologies) is a London- and Fort Lauderdale-based consumer IoT company that builds universal remote-monitoring apps for home IP cameras, letting users view and manage cameras from many brands through a single mobile application. Its products include the OWLR Multi-Brand Viewer and brand-specific viewers for Foscam and D-Link, plus motion-alert notifications. OWLR emphasizes a privacy-first design in which camera credentials stay on the user's phone and nothing is stored on OWLR's servers. The company reports over two million users and was backed by 500 Global. OWLR is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Acacus Group
providers.description: Acacus Group (Acacus Technologies) is a Dubai-headquartered mobility technology company founded in 2013 that builds artificial-intelligence and machine-learning software for the transportation and airline industries. Its Lynx product family — Lynx, Lynx Pro and Lynx Vision — provides intelligent fleet management, optimized dispatch built on mathematical combinatorics, disruption management, telematics and vehicle diagnostics, and deep-learning video analytics from in-vehicle cameras covering driver fatigue, lane departure, tailgating and passenger counting. Acacus also develops autonomous vehicle technology and Peregrine, an optimization solution for airline crew and airport operations. It won Best Global Startup at GITEX 2016 in Dubai and signed an MOU with Dubai Police for driverless patrol vehicles. Lynx sells as an enterprise SaaS subscription through a demo request; Acacus publishes no public developer program or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Auradine (Velaura AI)
providers.description: Auradine, Inc. is a Silicon Valley semiconductor and infrastructure company founded in 2022, in 2026 rebranded as Velaura AI, Inc. The company designs ultra-low-power compute solutions for data center, edge, and physical AI applications, anchored by its Titan Core silicon design and IP platform that reduces the power required for AI compute while maintaining performance. Its Teraflux product line delivers high-efficiency Bitcoin mining hardware (3nm ASICs, air- and hydro-cooled miners, containers, and fleet management software) deployed by leading Bitcoin data center operators. Auradine raised over $300 million across its funding rounds, including a $153M Series C, and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Auradine/Velaura AI publishes no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Davis Instruments
providers.description: Davis Instruments designs and manufactures personal and professional‑grade weather stations, marine instruments, and air‑quality monitors. The company provides high‑quality weather instruments for accurate data collection, offering reliable weather stations and sensors for hobbyists, researchers, and commercial users. Their product line includes the Vantage Vue, Vantage Pro2, and Vantage Pro2 Plus weather stations, as well as marine barometers and air‑quality monitoring devices.

providers.name: Gozynta
providers.description: Gozynta is a technology company that provides a unified connectivity platform enabling businesses to integrate and manage IoT devices, data streams, and third‑party services through a single API. Their solution focuses on simplifying device onboarding, real‑time data processing, and secure communication across heterogeneous environments, helping enterprises accelerate digital transformation and operational efficiency.

providers.name: SmartDrive Systems
providers.description: SmartDrive provides video‑based safety programs and a transportation intelligence platform that combine video analytics, telematics, compliance applications and predictive analytics. The solutions are offered to commercial trucking, transit, oil and gas, waste and recycling, construction, government, private fleet and distribution customers to improve driver performance, reduce collisions and lower operational costs.

providers.name: Code Metal
providers.description: Code Metal is a Boston-based AI company building a verifiable code translation and optimization platform for mission-critical, edge, and regulated industries including defense, automotive, semiconductor, robotics, and aerospace. The platform ingests high-level research and prototype code (Python, MATLAB, Julia) and produces optimized, edge-ready low-level code across C/C++, Rust, VHDL, Verilog, CUDA, HIP, and ONNX, using a divide-and-conquer pipeline that instruments and tests, translates and verifies functional equivalence, then optimizes and benchmarks against target CPU/GPU/FPGA runtimes. Code Metal was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or specification surface; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Koska
providers.description: KOSKA Corporation (株式会社KOSKA) is a Tokyo-based manufacturing technology company, founded in October 2018, that applies cost accounting and IoT to the Japanese factory floor. Its flagship product GenKan (原価管理自動化サービス) automates cost management for high-mix low-volume manufacturers: RFID and power sensors installed on existing equipment capture work progress and consumption without changing operator behavior, then make processing cost, material cost, and electricity cost visible line by line, feeding real actual-cost figures and KPI setting back to the shop floor and management. A second product, ながら記録 (Nagara Kiroku / "vScribe"), is an AI record-keeping app for manufacturing, construction, and logistics sites — photograph a paper form and AI generates the input form, then operators record hands-free by speaking, with the AI parsing natural speech into structured records, inspections, and reports. KOSKA is led by CEO Kenichiro Sone (Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2021) and advised by Hiroshi Obata, former chair of the Japan Cost Accounting Association. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a sensor-and-SaaS product company, not an API provider.

providers.name: Apar Infotech
providers.description: Apar Infotech Corporation, which operates publicly as Apar Technologies, is a Singapore-headquartered IT services and consulting group serving clients across Asia Pacific, the Middle East and the Americas. The firm delivers technology consulting and application services, data management and business intelligence, collaboration and content management, enterprise applications, managed services, staff augmentation and collaborative development centres, with practice areas spanning artificial intelligence, cloud, CRM, ServiceNow workflow, RPA/BPM hyperautomation, enterprise mobility and IoT. Apar also publishes a small set of its own products — the Otomeyt HR technology and technical-assessment platform, the Innoculate IoT monitoring platform, and the eLite SIS and eLite BAM applications. Apar is part of the Apar Group and is backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Apar publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification or self-service sign-up; its API work is delivered inside client engagements rather than as a public product surface.

providers.name: DataNomix
providers.description: DataNomix provides a data‑powered manufacturing platform that connects shop‑floor equipment, ERP systems, and analytics to enable real‑time production monitoring, quality control, and operational insights. Their solutions include production monitoring dashboards, ERP integration, G‑Code cloud services, and AI‑driven tooling analytics, helping manufacturers improve efficiency, reduce downtime, and make data‑driven decisions across the shop floor.

providers.name: Instabeat
providers.description: Instabeat is a San Francisco based swimming technology company that builds a heart-rate monitoring device integrated directly into swim goggles, giving swimmers real-time, color-coded effort feedback (heart-rate zones), automatic stroke detection, lap counting, pace, distance and rest-interval tracking without a chest strap or wrist watch. Paired with the Instabeat mobile app and myinstabeat.com, it delivers data-driven training insights so swimmers can adjust workouts in the water rather than after the session. The company sells the device through a Shopify storefront and has tested the product with 250+ swimmers across 56 countries. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer or API surface has been identified.

providers.name: INURU
providers.description: INURU (Inuru GmbH) is a Berlin-based printed-electronics company that manufactures ultra-thin, flexible printed OLED lighting for smart packaging, labels, apparel, and medical products. Its core product, the Elf (Embeddable Luminous Film), combines an inkjet-printed OLED, a power source, and a microchip into a paper-thin, waterproof film that can glow in any shape and respond to touch, motion, or sound. Founded in 2016, Inuru operates the automated "Dragon Factory" OLED production line in Wildau and works with brands such as Coca-Cola and Marvel on interactive, sustainable smart-packaging and medication-adherence labels. This is a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network; Inuru is a hardware and smart-packaging manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Lyte
providers.description: Lyte is a Mountain View, California perception company building an end-to-end integrated vision system for robotics and Physical AI. Founded in 2021 by Alexander Shpunt, Arman Hajati and Yuval Gerson — architects of Apple's depth-sensing and Face ID perception stack, and, in Shpunt's case, co-founder and CTO of PrimeSense — the company emerged from stealth in January 2026 with $107M in aggregate funding from Fidelity Management & Research, Atreides Management, Exor Ventures, Key1 Capital, Avigdor Willenz's group and Venture Tech Alliance. Its flagship product, LyteVision, combines 4D sensing (distance plus velocity), RGB imaging and inertial motion awareness with custom silicon and software into a single plug-and-play perception platform for robots, mobility and next-generation automation; it won a CES 2026 Best of Innovation award in Robotics and was named an honoree in Vehicle Tech and Advanced Mobility. Lyte is collaborating with NVIDIA to stream perception into GPUs over Holoscan Sensor Bridge (zero-copy, Jetson Thor, CUDA, NITROS) and into Omniverse and Isaac Sim for real-time digital twins. Lyte ships hardware and an embedded perception stack rather than a developer platform, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract as of this profile.

providers.name: Semios
providers.description: Semios (legally SemiosBio Technologies Inc., Vancouver, British Columbia, founded 2010 by Michael Gilbert) is a precision-agriculture company that operates a large in-canopy IoT sensor network for permanent crops - almonds, apples, cherries, citrus, grapes, pears, pistachios, stone fruit and walnuts. Its sensors report climate, soil moisture, insect trap counts and plant-stress readings on roughly ten-minute intervals, and its platform layers degree-day models, disease and frost risk models and machine learning on top of that feed to drive insect pest management (including variable-rate aerosol mating disruption), disease management, frost management, irrigation and water management, plant-stress monitoring, and alerting and reporting. Growers and agronomists consume it through the Semios Hub web and mobile applications, backed by the hub-api.semios.com service. Semios acquired Agworld, Altrac and Centricity, and in October 2024 the group unified those brands under the Almanac name, with Semios continuing as the sensing and crop-protection brand. Semios does not operate a public developer portal - the Hub API is customer and partner authenticated, and integrations such as the WiseConn irrigation integration are arranged directly.

providers.name: xiaoyi
providers.description: Xiaoyi Technology (小蚁科技), operated by Shanghai Yunyi Zhilian Technology (上海云蚁智联) and best known for its YI-brand cameras, is a Shanghai-based smart-imaging company that emerged from the Xiaomi ecosystem. It builds action cameras, the M1 mirrorless camera, smart home/security cameras, dash cams and in-car rearview systems, VR cameras, and handheld gimbals, and now positions itself around computer vision, edge intelligence, and edge computing solutions for smart mobility, smart home, smart retail, smart parks, and smart communities, selling through JD and Tmall storefronts. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment - the developer subdomain (dev.xiaoyi.com) returns 502, api.xiaoyi.com serves only a placeholder page, and no API documentation, OpenAPI specs, official GitHub organization, or first-party registry packages were located.

providers.name: DayOne
providers.description: DayOne is a hyperscale data center company delivering next-generation digital infrastructure for cloud, AI, and edge computing workloads. Spun out of the GDS International business and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, DayOne develops and operates strategically located, interconnected data center campuses across Asia-Pacific — Singapore, Johor (Malaysia), Batam (Indonesia), Hong Kong, Tokyo, and Bangkok — and is expanding into Europe with a launch market in Finland. The company positions itself as a build-to-suit and hyperscale partner focused on power availability, connectivity, and sustainable operations rather than as a public API or developer-platform provider; there is no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Evreka
providers.description: Evreka is a smart waste and recycling management technology company offering an end-to-end "Sustainability as a Service" platform that digitizes the entire waste management lifecycle. Its software suite spans operations, fleet, asset, MRF, and workforce management, route optimization, citizen engagement, and EPR/PRO management, complemented by IoT hardware such as fill-level sensors, vehicle and container trackers, and RFID readers. Evreka serves dumpster rental, recycling centers, medical, hazardous and liquid waste, construction and demolition, local authorities, and cross-border waste operators. Backed by 500 Global, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Nordsense
providers.description: Nordsense provides smart sensor solutions for waste management, delivering real‑time data insights to municipalities and businesses. Their IoT‑enabled smart bin sensors track fill levels, location, and routing, helping reduce carbon emissions, increase recycling rates, and improve operational transparency. By digitizing waste collection, Nordsense enables data‑driven decisions that optimize routes, lower fuel use, and enhance sustainability outcomes across urban environments.

providers.name: Tuio
providers.description: Tuio provides a cloud‑based platform that enables businesses to integrate real‑time location data and IoT device management into their applications. The service offers APIs for device onboarding, geofencing, event streaming, and analytics, helping clients build location‑aware solutions across logistics, retail, and smart‑city use cases. Tuio emphasizes security, scalability, and developer-friendly documentation, supporting RESTful endpoints and WebSocket streams for live data.

providers.name: Aosongelectronics
providers.description: Aosongelectronics, operating under the brand ASAIR, is a Chinese semiconductor company specializing in MEMS smart sensor solutions. It offers a broad portfolio including temperature & humidity sensors, oxygen sensors, flow meters, pressure gauges, gas sensors, and related instrumentation. The company serves global markets with high‑precision, reliable sensor products for industrial, environmental, and consumer applications, emphasizing stability, low leakage, and long‑term performance.

providers.name: Cron Systems
providers.description: Cron Systems (now operating as Cron AI) builds deep-learning perception software for 3D sensor and LiDAR data. Its flagship platform, senseEDGE, performs real-time 3D object detection, classification, and tracking from point-cloud data at the edge, with multi-sensor fusion and adverse-weather resilience. The technology serves intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, autonomous mobility, smart cities, and security and surveillance — powering use cases such as traffic management, autonomous tolling, crowd and queue management, smart parking, vehicle counting, and airport and aircraft-movement monitoring. Object output is emitted as JSON and Flatbuffers binary over WebSocket, with a web-based configuration and visualizer utility, VPN and PTP time-synchronization support, and a privacy-preserving, GDPR-compliant design. Cron AI was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: E2iptechnologies
providers.description: E2iptechnologies provides smart surface solutions, offering integrated hardware and software platforms for interactive displays, touch interfaces, and IoT-enabled surfaces. Their products span from ideation through fabrication, targeting enterprise, education, and retail markets with customizable, networked surface technologies.

providers.name: IKEA U.S.
providers.description: IKEA U.S. is the United States retail operation of IKEA, run by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA franchisee. The U.S. business operates ~50+ full-service stores, ~40+ Plan & Order Points, and ~80+ pick-up locations across the country, alongside the ikea.com/us e-commerce site and the IKEA mobile app. Inter IKEA Systems B.V. separately owns the IKEA Concept and brand. IKEA U.S. offers home furnishings, kitchens, appliances, lighting, the IKEA Family loyalty program, the IKEA Business Network for B2B customers, home delivery and Click & Collect, design and planning services, the Buy Back & Resell program, and IKEA Home smart products controlled via the IKEA Home smart and IKEA Home smart 1 apps. IKEA U.S. does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading-partner integrations are handled through IKEA's vendor systems and Ingka Group's internal digital platforms.

providers.name: Lyten
providers.description: Lyten is a San Jose, California advanced-materials company founded in 2015 that invented and commercializes Lyten 3D Graphene, a tunable three-dimensional carbon supermaterial produced by converting methane into nanostructured carbon while co-producing hydrogen. Lyten applies that materials platform across four product lines: lithium-sulfur battery cells and battery systems that contain no cobalt, nickel or manganese and target roughly 40% weight savings versus lithium-ion; 3D graphene reinforced 3D printer filament; concrete admixture and structural adhesives; and chemical/environmental sensors, including the Lyten Atmos continuous methane-intelligence platform that pairs solar-powered LTE field sensors with cloud analytics and dashboards for landfill and oil-and-gas emissions monitoring. The company has raised over $600 million from investors including Stellantis, FedEx and Honeywell, operates a 145,000 sq ft pilot manufacturing facility in the Alviso district of North San Jose, acquired Cuberg's San Leandro battery assets in 2024, and in 2025 acquired Northvolt battery manufacturing assets in Poland and Sweden, establishing a European headquarters in Gdansk, Poland. Lyten is a private company; its shares trade on secondary markets such as Forge Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: Nothing
providers.description: Nothing is a London-based consumer technology company designing smartphones (Phone series), wireless earbuds (Ear series), and other consumer hardware under the Nothing and CMF by Nothing brands, backed by EQT Ventures and GV. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass confirmed Nothing publishes a consumer web presence (support centre, community, careers, playground) but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDK, or webhook surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Volterra
