providers.description: Volterra was a Santa Clara-based distributed cloud company founded in 2017 by Ankur Singla, Harshad Nakil, and Ashish Ranjan, offering the VoltMesh (multi-cloud networking and security) and VoltStack (edge application deployment) SaaS platforms on a global application delivery network. Backed by roughly $50M from Khosla Ventures, Mayfield, M12, Samsung NEXT, and Itochu Technology Ventures, Volterra was acquired by F5 in January 2021 for approximately $500M and became the foundation of F5 Distributed Cloud Services. Its API surface (ves.io.schema, console.ves.volterra.io) is catalogued in the F5 Distributed Cloud Services profile, while the Volterra-branded Terraform provider and vesctl CLI remain published and maintained by F5.

providers.name: Carnival
providers.description: Carnival Corporation & plc is the world's largest cruise company operating eight cruise line brands (Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, Cunard, P&O Cruises, Costa Cruises, AIDA Cruises), plus the White Pass and Yukon Route. Carnival operates the OceanMedallion wearable IoT technology and mobile experience platform, the Carnival HUB app, the Princess MedallionClass app, and a portfolio of guest-facing digital experiences across its fleet of over 90 ships.

providers.name: Cassia Networks
providers.description: Cassia Networks, founded in 2014, provides enterprise Bluetooth IoT products and solutions, including long‑range Bluetooth gateways, IoT access controllers, and network management software. Their patented technology enables reliable, scalable, and secure Bluetooth connectivity for industrial, digital health, education, and smart campus applications. Recognized with awards such as Best‑of‑CES 2016 and Bluetooth SIG Imagine Blue 2017, Cassia Networks serves a global customer base and offers comprehensive support, documentation, and developer resources.

providers.name: Compredict
providers.description: Compredict is a German deep‑tech company pioneering AI‑powered virtual sensor technology for the automotive industry. Founded as a spin‑off from TU Darmstadt, it transforms raw vehicle sensor data into trusted physical signals using software‑defined virtual sensors, enabling hardware‑free insights across automotive, manufacturing, defense, robotics, and agriculture sectors.

providers.name: FRITZ! (formerly AVM, FRITZ!Box)
providers.description: FRITZ! (formerly AVM, FRITZ!Box) provides networking hardware and smart home solutions, including routers, repeaters, and home automation devices. The company offers APIs for device management, firmware updates, and integration with smart home platforms, serving both consumers and developers.

providers.name: ISAAC Instruments
providers.description: ISAAC Instruments is a Canadian provider of in-cab technology and fleet management for the trucking industry - electronic logging devices (ELD), telematics, hours-of-service (HOS) compliance, driver workflow, messaging, and fuel/performance analytics, delivered as a fully managed hardware-plus-software platform. ISAAC runs an "Open Platform" with a documented API that lets fleets and 80+ integration partners (TMS/dispatch, maintenance, fuel tax, visibility, safety/compliance) share ISAAC data with their chosen vendors. API access is partner-gated - vendors apply through the ISAAC partner program and the full API Guide and reference live behind the ISAAC InRealTime portal and Client Center rather than on a public developer site. The API surface documented here is modeled from ISAAC's public platform and partner materials; exact endpoints, base URLs, and authentication are provisioned to approved partners.

providers.name: Zwift
providers.description: Zwift is a Long Beach, California online fitness company that operates a multiplayer indoor cycling and running platform combining stationary smart trainers and bikes with a 3D virtual-world game client. Riders and runners use a smart trainer, smart bike (such as the in-house Zwift Ride), treadmill, or pod to drive an avatar through fictional worlds (Watopia, Makuri Islands) and licensed real-world routes, joining structured workouts, group rides, races, training plans, and 24/7 events alongside a global community of more than a million members. The platform pairs with smart trainers and heart-rate monitors over Bluetooth and ANT+, and the Zwift Companion mobile app provides in-game messaging, ride control, and route discovery. Zwift does not operate a general public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, or open-source SDK. Its developer surface is limited to a private, application-only Structured Training API for approved training partners (TrainingPeaks, TrainerRoad, Wahoo SYSTM, JOIN Cycling and similar coaching platforms) that lets external workout builders push custom workouts into a rider's Zwift account, plus one-way activity-export connections to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Garmin Connect, MapMyRide, MapMyRun, Adidas Running, Technogym, Fitbit, Wahoo, Apple Health, and Withings. There is no public REST surface, OAuth client registration, or partner self-service available to general developers — third-party tools (community libraries, ZwiftPower, Sauce for Zwift) interact with Zwift via reverse-engineered private endpoints, not a sanctioned API. Zwift is a paid consumer subscription business; revenue comes from monthly memberships and hardware sales (Zwift Ride, Zwift Cog, Zwift Click, Zwift Play).

providers.name: Cambridge Terahertz
providers.description: Cambridge Terahertz (thzcorp.com) is an MIT-spinout physical security company building compact, AI-powered terahertz imaging sensors that detect concealed weapons -- guns, knives, explosives, and 3D-printed weapons -- as people walk naturally through entrances, without pat-downs or metal detectors. The 2-pound sensors mount like security cameras, serve hospitals, enterprises, and government facilities, and integrate with existing VMS and security systems over standard REST APIs, though the company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation. Backed by Felicis with a $12M seed round and an NSF SBIR Phase II grant.

providers.name: Commsignia
providers.description: Commsignia is a Budapest-based V2X (Vehicle-to-Everything) technology company building connected vehicle and smart infrastructure solutions for the automotive and transportation industries. Its portfolio spans roadside units (RSUs) and onboard units (OBUs), a V2X software stack, and cloud services grouped into product suites: Roadway Intelligence, Emergency Safety, Fleet, Automotive, Smart Infrastructure, and Connected Vehicle. The company turns isolated roadway and vehicle data silos into real-world operational intelligence for safer roads and improved traffic flow. As of this enrichment pass Commsignia publishes no public developer API, REST/OpenAPI reference, SDK, or developer portal; technical integration is handled through direct engagement. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech.

providers.name: deepstreamhub
providers.description: deepstreamHub GmbH provides deepstream.io, an open‑source real‑time server for mobile, web and IoT applications. It enables clients and backend services to sync data, publish events, perform RPCs and monitor presence with a strong focus on security and scalability. The platform supports multiple client libraries (JavaScript, Java, HTTP) and integrates with various databases, caches and message buses, offering flexible configuration without writing extensive code.

providers.name: Globetouch
providers.description: Globetouch is a global mobile and IoT connectivity provider founded in 2010 and headquartered in San Ramon, California, which rebranded to Airlinq in February 2020 — globetouch.com now 301-redirects to www.airlinq.com. Its GConnect / CloudSIM heritage (physical SIM, soft SIM and eSIM provisioning with rule-engine-driven subscription-profile management for mobile operators and IoT enterprises) is carried forward in Mobilinq, the company's IoT connectivity and application management platform, alongside Autolinq for the connected-vehicle ecosystem, Utilinq for electric, gas and water utilities, and Marketlinq, an operator-branded private-5G and IoT marketplace and dashboard. Airlinq markets a "comprehensive API library" for BSS/OSS integration and data and voice plans "enabled via API", but as of August 2026 it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind; the only entry point is a contact-sales form.

providers.name: morewis
providers.description: Morewis (摩尔元数) is a Chinese industrial software company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian, that develops cloud-based Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for the manufacturing sector. Its Morewis Cloud industrial internet platform, MoreDEV low-code development platform (including the WisIDE cloud IDE), and MoreAgent / N³ industrial AI large model let manufacturers build and run smart-factory applications with reduced hand coding. Reference clients include Haier, Hisense, Aisino, Inspur, and 3Trees Group. The company raised a ~100M yuan Series B led by Qiming Venture Partners. No public English-language REST API, OpenAPI, SDK, or GitHub organization was found; the developer surface is a China-hosted low-code industrial application platform.

providers.name: Sasken Communications
providers.description: Sasken Communications provides integrated communication solutions, including network infrastructure, IoT connectivity, and managed services for enterprises. Founded with a focus on innovation, the company leverages advanced technologies to deliver reliable, scalable, and secure communication platforms that enable digital transformation across industries.

providers.name: DSP Concepts
providers.description: DSP Concepts provides embedded audio processing software and the Audio Weaver platform, enabling developers to integrate advanced audio algorithms into automotive, consumer, and professional audio products. Their solutions include AI‑enhanced audio processing, customizable DSP blocks, and tools for rapid development and deployment across a range of industries. The company emphasizes modular, scalable designs and offers extensive documentation, training, and support for engineers building audio‑centric applications.

providers.name: Hinge Health
providers.description: Hinge Health is a San Francisco-based digital musculoskeletal (MSK) care company founded in 2014 by Daniel Perez and Gabriel Mecklenburg, delivering virtual physical therapy, pelvic health, and chronic pain care to enterprise health plans, employers, and their members. The platform combines on-demand exercise therapy with a multidisciplinary care team — physical therapists, health coaches, board-certified physicians, and orthopedic specialists — augmented by 3D motion tracking, computer vision, and an in-house AI Care Assistant. Hinge Health develops Enso, an FDA-cleared, drug-free wearable that delivers proprietary electrical stimulation waveforms for pain relief, and operates HingeConnect, an EMR/claims interoperability layer that ingests records from more than one million external providers across 120,000+ care sites to coordinate care, surface surgical and opioid risk, and feed real-time clinical context into the digital clinic. The company also runs HingeSelect, a national provider network for in-person MSK care, and contracts with all five major US national health plans plus employers including Boeing, Salesforce, and US Foods. Hinge Health raised more than $1 billion from Insight Partners, Tiger Global, Coatue, and Atomico before completing its IPO on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker HNGE on May 22, 2025, pricing at $32/share and opening at $39.25 for an initial market capitalization above $3 billion. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hinge Health, Enso, or HingeConnect — the platform is sold as a managed clinical service to health plans and employers, and the HingeConnect interoperability surface is operated internally rather than exposed to third-party developers.

providers.name: Netgsm
providers.description: Netgsm is a Turkish telecommunications provider offering a wide range of digital communication services, including SMS, voice, virtual numbers, IoT/M2M data lines, cloud PBX, and custom API integrations. Their platform enables businesses to send bulk SMS, manage OTP, integrate WhatsApp, and utilize VoIP solutions, all accessible via documented APIs for developers.

providers.name: Raytheon
providers.description: Raytheon is an American aerospace and defense manufacturer operating as a business of RTX Corporation, the world's largest aerospace and defense company. Raytheon designs, develops, and produces advanced defense systems including precision weapons, air and missile defense systems, sensors, radar, electronic warfare, command-and-control solutions, and cyber capabilities for the U.S. military and allied governments worldwide. Key products include the Patriot missile defense system, StormBreaker smart weapons, RAIVEN electro-optical/infrared sensor suites, and advanced electronic attack systems. Raytheon also develops world-class logistics software through the EAGLE team supporting production management, technical manual development, and product support data. No public developer API or machine-readable specification is available at this time; Raytheon's software solutions are deployed within government program contracts.

providers.name: Savi Technology
providers.description: Savi Technology provides Internet of Things (IoT) and active RFID (aRFID) solutions for real-time supply chain visibility, asset tracking, and cargo security. Combining active RFID tags, environmental condition sensors, and machine intelligence, Savi delivers location, condition, and estimated-time- of-arrival data for cargo and high-value assets across government, military (including U.S. Department of Defense in-transit visibility), and commercial supply chains. The company is headquartered in Wilmington, North Carolina. As of this enrichment pass, Savi Technology exposes no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDKs, or documented web API; its only authenticated surface is the aRFID-VI customer catalog (savirfidcatalog.net).

providers.name: INDOS
providers.description: INDOS (Garment IO) is an AI-powered manufacturing operations platform built for labor-intensive garment and apparel production facilities. Its cloud-based system unifies Manufacturing Execution (MES), Quality Management (QMS), Maintenance Management (MMS), and Warehouse Management (WMS) into a single real-time view of the factory floor. A shop-floor hardware device captures operator and production-line data, and the platform surfaces operator efficiency, AI anomaly detection, performance scorecards, and end-to-end control from cutting through packing. Founded by Ahmed Nounou and Mahmoud Sabae and backed by 500 Global, it serves garment manufacturers across the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia. INDOS does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: openWB (self-hosted)
providers.description: openWB provides a self‑hosted, modular electric vehicle charging solution that combines a 7‑inch touchscreen controller with integrated energy management software. The system enables smart charging for households, businesses and residential property owners (WEGs), allowing users to monitor and control energy consumption, integrate photovoltaic surplus, and upgrade existing wallboxes. openWB’s open‑source approach lets installers customize and extend functionality while maintaining compliance with European charging standards.

providers.name: Sensome
providers.description: Sensome is a clinical-stage medical technology company developing tissue-sensing microchip technology and proprietary integration processes that embed real-time bio-impedance sensing into minimally invasive medical devices. Its lead product, the Clotild Smart Guidewire System (manufactured with Asahi Intecc), is the first tissue-sensing neurovascular guidewire, providing physicians real-time blood clot characterization to guide Acute Ischemic Stroke treatment; additional indications include lung cancer biopsy guidance. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech, Sensome is a medical-device hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer platform at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Wisear
providers.description: Wisear is a Paris-based neurotechnology company building an AI-powered neural interface that lets people control devices through voiceless and touchless commands. Its technology reads biosignals captured by everyday wearables such as wireless earphones, AR/VR headsets and smartglasses, turning subtle facial and neural gestures into hands-free device controls. Wisear targets use cases across consumer audio, industrial augmented reality, walkie-talkie and emergency communications, gaming headsets, the metaverse and accessibility. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Wisear publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal — this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Apex.AI
providers.description: Apex.AI is an embedded and autonomous software company whose tagline is "software that moves," focused on safe, real-time, software-defined systems (SDx) for automotive, robotics, and other safety-critical embedded platforms. Its product line includes Apex.Grace (deterministic embedded execution framework, an automotive-grade evolution of ROS 2), Apex.Ida (high-speed fault-tolerant middleware for sensor, compute, and cloud connectivity), Apex.OS for V&V (data recording and replay for validating autonomous systems), and Apex.Alan (automated tooling and CI/CD workflows for safe software development at scale). Apex.AI also provides technical assessment, architecture, embedded and cloud software development, CI/CD pipeline, and ROS 1 to ROS 2 migration services. The company is a maintainer of substantial ROS 2 and embedded middleware open source. It is backed by Canaan Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Apex.AI publishes no public developer REST API at this time.

providers.name: Audi Connect / myAudi
providers.description: Audi Connect is the connected-vehicle services platform from Audi AG, the Ingolstadt, Germany-based luxury automaker and member of the Volkswagen Group. Delivered to drivers through the embedded MMI infotainment system and the myAudi companion app for iOS and Android, Audi Connect spans remote vehicle control (lock/unlock, remote start, climate pre-conditioning, EV charge management), safety and security (Emergency Call/eCall, Audi Service Request, stolen-vehicle locator, geofencing, speed alerts), and in-car infotainment (real-time traffic, satellite map imagery, parking and fuel information, weather, news, natural voice recognition, Amazon Alexa, Amazon Music, Wi-Fi hotspot, and an in-vehicle app store with Disney+ and passenger gaming on supported models). Services are packaged as Audi connect CARE (included for ten years on new U.S. Audis), Audi connect NAV (navigation and live traffic), and Audi connect PLUS (premium streaming and Wi-Fi). For EVs and PHEVs, Audi Connect adds charging-station search, remote charge monitoring, and cabin pre-conditioning. Audi does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, OAuth program, or partner SDK for myAudi/Audi Connect; programmatic access today is brokered by third-party connected-car aggregators (Smartcar, High Mobility, Enode, Mojio) under Audi's commercial agreements, and community projects reverse-engineer the mobile-app endpoints. Audi has publicly discussed an internal OpenAPI-driven API management strategy (with Nagarro) but the surface remains private to Audi, VW Group brands, and authorized partners.

providers.name: Praan
providers.description: Praan (Praan Climate Technologies) is a deep-tech climate startup working to democratize access to clean, healthy air and to rebuild the atmosphere by capturing air pollution and greenhouse gases with novel filterless technology. Its products include HIVE, an air-purification device for homes and commercial spaces paired with a companion mobile application, and MK II, an air-purification system for industrial environments. Praan is backed by Prosus Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched through the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Praan publishes a consumer hardware and mobile-app surface but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: TP-Link (Omada)
providers.description: TP-Link (Omada) is a global provider of networking hardware and cloud‑based management solutions. The company offers a range of products including routers, Wi‑Fi access points, switches, and the Omada SD‑WAN and Wi‑Fi management platform for businesses. Its public website (tp‑link.com) presents product information, support resources, and corporate details, but does not expose a dedicated developer portal or public API documentation.

providers.name: Biolinq
providers.description: Biolinq Incorporated is a San Diego, California medical device and digital health company founded in 2012 that develops intradermal biowearable sensors. Its lead product, Biolinq Shine, is an autonomous needle-free continuous glucose sensor built on an array of electrochemical microsensors that sit just below the surface of the skin, combined with an accelerometer and an ambient light sensor so a single wearable measures glucose alongside activity and sleep. The sensor carries an on-body LED color indicator for time-in-range and pairs with a companion mobile application for trends and insights. The FDA granted Biolinq Shine De Novo classification for adults with type 2 diabetes not on insulin therapy, with a planned US market launch. Biolinq publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its public web presence is a corporate marketing site.

providers.name: Teradar
providers.description: Teradar is a Boston, Massachusetts semiconductor and sensing company founded in 2020 by Matthew Carey, Gregory Charvat and Nicholas Saiz that is commercializing terahertz-band vision sensors for vehicles, defense and security screening. Its Modular Terahertz Engine (MTE) is an all-solid-state chip architecture built from proprietary transmit (TX), receive (RX) and Teracore processing silicon, delivering 0.13-degree native angular resolution at 300+ meters in day, night, rain, fog and snow, positioned to sit alongside cameras and to displace radar and lidar in SAE L1-L5 driver assistance and autonomy programs. The company emerged from stealth in late 2025 with a $150M Series B led by VXI Capital with Ibex Investors, Capricorn Investment Group, The Engine Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures, and is working with global OEMs and Tier-One suppliers toward a 2028 model-year launch. Teradar is a hardware and silicon company: it publishes a marketing site and product specification sheets, but no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Bwsensing
providers.description: Bwsensing designs and manufactures high‑precision inertial measurement sensors, inclinometers, IMUs, and related solutions for industries such as construction, energy, transportation, and medical devices. Their products enable accurate orientation, motion tracking, and structural health monitoring, supporting smart infrastructure and autonomous systems. The company emphasizes advanced sensor technology, robust data analytics, and integration with IoT platforms to deliver reliable, real‑time insights for critical applications.

providers.name: DRINKOTEC
providers.description: DRINKOTEC is a Swiss beverage technology company headquartered in Nyon, Vaud, that designs, builds and services connected beverage dispensing systems and the software that runs them. Its hardware line covers all-in-one and modern postmix dispensers (NEO, VISION PX), compact premix dispensing (DRAFTER), cocktails and blends (MANHATTAN), self-service walls, contactless payment (BEVPAY), beer and wine counting and control (LEVELUP, BEERMAX), automatic keg switching, cellar cooling monitoring and water fountains. LOOP360, its cloud beverage productivity and analytics platform, connects dispensed beverages to a central system and is marketed as integrating with ERP and CRM platforms. DRINKOTEC sells into breweries, bars, pubs, nightclubs, restaurants, hotels, festivals, sports arenas, cruise ships, offices, schools and healthcare, and markets a RESTful DRINKOTEC API for third-party integration whose reference documentation is not published publicly.

providers.name: Ossia
providers.description: Ossia, Inc. is a Redmond, Washington wireless power technology company founded by physicist Hatem Zeine (incorporated as Omnilectric in 2008, operating as Ossia from 2013) and the inventor of Cota Real Wireless Power — a patented RF smart-antenna system that delivers targeted energy over the air to multiple moving devices at a distance, without pads, plugs, cables or line of sight. A Cota receiver emits a beacon and the Cota transmitter returns a focused 2.4 GHz or 5.8 GHz power signal along the same path, which is how the system tracks and powers devices in motion. Ossia does not manufacture products for sale: it licenses the Cota technology to manufacturers, brands and OEMs, ships Cota developer and reference design kits (receiver chip, sample hardware, software components, test instructions) to authorized licensees, and works through joint ventures and development partners such as Motherson Ossia. The company holds 180+ US and international patents, is FCC certified under Parts 15 and 18, and carries regulatory approval in the US, UK and 45+ other countries. Ossia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind — the developer surface it does have is hardware and firmware delivered under license.

providers.name: Theta EdgeCloud
providers.description: Theta EdgeCloud is a distributed, hybrid AI and video cloud built on the Theta Network blockchain, offering on-demand GPU compute for AI model training, fine-tuning, inference, video transcoding, and live streaming. EdgeCloud aggregates GPU capacity from data-center hyperscaler partners and a global community of Edge Nodes (consumer and enterprise GPUs) into a single dispatchable compute layer addressable via REST, JSON-RPC, and SDK clients. Core services include EdgeCloud AI Services (on-demand model inference APIs for LLMs, image, audio, and multimodal models such as Llama, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and Whisper; agentic RAG chatbots; GPU-backed Jupyter notebooks; dedicated GPU pod deployments; and AI training with GPU clusters), EdgeCloud Video Services (the Theta Video API for upload, transcoding, livestream ingestion, DRM, NFT-gated playback, and webhooks), EdgeStore (decentralized object storage), and the EdgeCloud Client (an installable node that earns TFUEL for contributing GPU and bandwidth). Developers authenticate with x-api-key tokens issued from the EdgeCloud dashboard, manage deployments programmatically through api.thetaedgecloud.com and the Node.js SDK @thetalabs/theta-edgecloud, and access on-demand model endpoints (also distributed through RapidAPI). The Theta blockchain layer is EVM-compatible with an Ethereum RPC adaptor, supports TNT-20 tokens and NFTs, and underwrites EdgeCloud's payment, rewards, and staking economy through the THETA governance token and TFUEL gas token. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

providers.name: Asimily
providers.description: Asimily provides a proactive cyber asset defense platform that offers IoT device visibility, risk modeling, segmentation, and automated remediation. It serves industries such as healthcare, energy, financial services, and manufacturing, helping organizations continuously monitor, prioritize, and mitigate cyber risks across IT, OT, and IoT environments.

providers.name: iTAC Software
providers.description: iTAC Software AG is an independent company of the Duerr Group and a leading provider of Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for discrete manufacturing. Its iTAC.MOM.Suite delivers production control, end-to-end traceability, quality management, and AI-supported analytics that help automotive, electronics, and medical-technology manufacturers implement Industry 4.0 and smart-factory operations. iTAC does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integration is delivered through the MOM platform's IoT and connectivity layers as part of a project engagement.

providers.name: Lynq
providers.description: Lynq Networks develops infrastructure-free, long-range wireless connectivity for enterprise and OEM devices, bridging the gap between short-range Bluetooth and infrastructure-dependent cellular/5G. Its technology lets original equipment manufacturers build large-area device networks without deploying traditional network infrastructure, targeting construction, agriculture, military, and public-safety use cases. Lynq is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nodal Industries
providers.description: Nodal Industries, operating as Nodal Security, is a network security company and 500 Global portfolio startup that makes Numa, a plug-and-play network security appliance providing protective oversight of every connected device on a home or small-office network. Rather than per-device antivirus software, Numa works at the network layer, intercepting malicious traffic before it reaches devices using real-time threat intelligence powered by Suricata, with automatic updates and minimal setup. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or event surface.

providers.name: Tractive
providers.description: Tractive is an Austrian pet-technology company, founded in October 2012 in Pasching, Austria and led by CEO Michael Hurnaus, that builds GPS location and health-monitoring trackers for dogs and cats. Its collar-attached devices (such as the DOG and CAT GPS trackers) pair with a subscription mobile app to deliver real-time worldwide location, virtual fences, activity, sleep and, more recently, resting heart-rate and respiratory-rate health intelligence to more than 1.4 million active subscribers. Tractive was acquired by Italy's Bending Spoons in 2026. Tractive does NOT publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — its backend HTTP API (api.tractive.com) is private to its own apps; the only clients are unofficial, community reverse-engineered libraries. This profile enriches the company's identity for the API Evangelist network; there is no official API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Microsec
providers.description: Microsec provides next‑gen cybersecurity solutions for IoT and OT networks, protecting government and industrial organizations from cyber attacks. Their platform secures devices and infrastructure with enterprise‑grade features, offering threat detection, device authentication, and secure communications across diverse environments.

providers.name: Aerohive
providers.description: Aerohive Networks was a cloud-managed networking company founded in 2006 by Changming Liu and headquartered in Milpitas, California. It pioneered controller-less, cloud-managed Wi-Fi and edge networking, managed through its HiveManager NG (later ExtremeCloud IQ) platform and access points. Aerohive went public on the NYSE under the ticker HIVE and was acquired by Extreme Networks in a deal that closed on 2019-08-09 for approximately $272 million. The company operated an Aerohive Developer Program with a public developer portal (developer.aerohive.com) and REST APIs for the HiveManager NG / ACS platform, plus a GitHub organization of reference applications. Following the acquisition the products were folded into ExtremeCloud IQ, and the legacy Aerohive API and its developer portal were retired (shutdown dated 2026-07-12), with integrators directed to migrate to the Extreme Platform ONE Developer Portal. This profile enriches the historical Aerohive API surface; it is a retired/acquired provider.

providers.name: Bunchtechnology
providers.description: Bunchtechnology (Bunch Tech) provides enterprise IoT solutions for intelligent real‑estate and smart building management. It designs, procures, and deploys multi‑sensor ecosystems that reduce operational costs, improve occupant experiences, and enable data‑driven building automation across energy, air quality, occupancy, leak detection, and more. The company serves large‑scale commercial properties, offering plug‑and‑play device access, cloud integration, and consulting to simplify IoT deployments and accelerate digital transformation.

providers.name: Matter Intelligence
providers.description: Matter Intelligence is a California-based remote sensing and physical-AI company founded in 2024 by former NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory engineers Vishnu Sridhar and Thomas Chrien with former Caltech scientist Nathan Stein. The company builds ultraspectral imaging sensors that capture roughly 2,000 spectral bands from deep ultraviolet through thermal infrared — enough to read the molecular chemistry of a surface rather than only its color — and pairs them with Large Geospatial Models that reason over that data. Its sensors are designed for satellites, aircraft, drones and robots, and its first satellite, EARTH-1, is intended to deliver sub-meter hyperspectral and thermal imaging and to build a global encyclopedia of Earth's material composition. Target applications named on its site include mining and mineral exploration, agriculture, insurance and risk, infrastructure monitoring, emissions and methane detection, and defense ISR. The company emerged from stealth in October 2024 with a $12M seed round led by Lowercarbon Capital, with Toyota Ventures, Pear VC, E2MC and Mark Cuban participating. As of this profile it is pre-launch and pre-product: matter.com is a marketing site with an Early Access request form, and Matter Intelligence publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Sandbar
providers.description: Sandbar is a consumer hardware and AI company behind Stream, a private voice ring and conversational notes app. Worn on the finger, Stream pairs a discreet private microphone, a glass touchpad, and silent haptics with an on-device "Inner Voice" assistant so people can capture notes, reminders, and todos, dictate speech-to-text across any iOS or Mac app, and think aloud without reaching for a phone. Backed by Kindred Ventures and True Ventures, Sandbar is a preorder-stage consumer product; it publishes a marketing site, an About/Us page, and a Careers page, but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Teletrac Navman
providers.description: Teletrac Navman provides GPS fleet tracking and telematics solutions for businesses worldwide. Their platform offers real‑time vehicle location, driver safety monitoring, compliance tools, and analytics to improve fleet efficiency and reduce operational costs. The company serves a broad range of industries, including transportation, construction, and public sector, delivering integrated hardware and software for comprehensive fleet management.

providers.name: Anoria
providers.description: Anoria is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) human-interaction company building a wearable bracelet for the EQ era that measures and tracks emotional states in real time. The device uses the company's proprietary SOMI (state-of-mind inference) model to correlate roughly 150 audio and biometric signals into a "Flow Score" that reflects a user's energy, mood, and focus, then explains why the user feels that way and what they can do about it. Anoria targets founders and creatives who treat their mental state as a performance asset, with the goal of making emotional intelligence trainable. As of mid-2026 the company is an early-stage prototype running an early-access waitlist; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation yet, so this API Evangelist profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: Hyundai Bluelink
providers.description: Hyundai Bluelink is Hyundai Motor America's connected vehicle service for Hyundai owners, providing remote vehicle control, vehicle status and diagnostics, navigation and route services, safety and security features, and EV-specific charging and climate management. Bluelink is delivered to owners through the MyHyundai with Bluelink mobile app (iOS and Android), the in-vehicle infotainment head unit, the owner web portal at owners.hyundaiusa.com, and connected smart-home and voice integrations (Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, smartwatch apps). Feature sets vary by model year and subscription tier — typically Bluelink, Bluelink+, and Bluelink Connected Care / Remote / Guidance bundles — and include remote start with climate, remote door lock/unlock, remote horn and lights, vehicle finder, stolen vehicle recovery and SVI, automatic collision notification, SOS emergency assistance, monthly vehicle health reports, destination search (powered by Google), in-vehicle Wi-Fi hotspot (via AT&T on supported models), and EV-specific remote charge start/stop, charge schedule, charge-level monitoring, and pre-conditioning. Bluelink is a consumer-facing, owner-authenticated service. Hyundai does not publish a public developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API keys for third-party integration with Bluelink vehicle endpoints; access is limited to authenticated owners through Hyundai's first-party apps and to enterprise partners under contract (fleet, insurance telematics, charging networks, smart-home platforms). A community ecosystem of reverse-engineered, unofficial Python and Node.js clients (Hyundai-Kia-Connect/hyundai_kia_connect_api, Home Assistant integrations, Bluelinky) is used by enthusiasts and home automation users, but these are not endorsed, supported, or governed by Hyundai and may break at any time.

providers.name: VeSync
providers.description: VeSync provides smart home devices and a cloud‑based platform that lets users control appliances such as air purifiers, humidifiers, robot vacuums, and lighting through mobile apps and voice assistants. The company offers an API for device status, control, and integration with third‑party services, supporting OAuth‑like authentication and real‑time updates. VeSync’s ecosystem focuses on energy‑efficient, Wi‑Fi‑enabled products aimed at improving indoor air quality and convenience for consumers.

providers.name: Carbontrack
providers.description: Carbontrack (carbonTRACK) is an Australian technology company specializing in smart energy management systems and IoT solutions. Headquartered in Melbourne, it provides a patented intelligent energy management platform that enables users and providers to monitor, control and automate energy consumption, generation and storage, supporting a decentralized energy future.

providers.name: Dalton Mills
providers.description: Dalton Mills is a technology-driven company focused on providing innovative solutions in the manufacturing sector. Founded by a collective of seasoned entrepreneurs, the company leverages advanced data analytics and API integrations to streamline production workflows, enhance supply chain visibility, and drive operational efficiency for its clients. With a commitment to open standards and developer-friendly interfaces, Dalton Mills offers robust APIs that enable seamless connectivity between enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, IoT devices, and third‑party services, fostering a flexible and scalable ecosystem for modern manufacturers.

providers.name: Fossil Group
providers.description: Fossil Group is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of consumer fashion accessories including watches, jewelry, handbags, small leather goods, belts, and sunglasses sold under owned and licensed brands such as Fossil, Skagen, Michele, Relic, Misfit, and licensed lines for Michael Kors, Diesel, Emporio Armani, Tory Burch, and others.

providers.name: Lynk Global
providers.description: Lynk Global, now operating as Elveo, provides direct‑to‑device satellite connectivity, enabling mobile phones, IoT devices and machines to stay connected worldwide without terrestrial infrastructure. The company leverages S‑band spectrum and a network of satellites to deliver reliable, low‑latency service across 60+ countries, supporting enterprises, automotive, consumer and government use cases.

providers.name: Fishbit
providers.description: Fishbit is a smart-aquarium management company whose platform pairs a mobile app (iOS/Android) with connected hardware — the Fishbit Monitor, which tracks water parameters such as pH, temperature, and salinity in real time, and the Fishbit Controller, which wirelessly automates aquarium equipment. Hobbyists and reef keepers use the system to remotely monitor tank conditions and automate lighting, pumps, and dosing. The company sells its monitoring and control hardware through an online store and ran a device-manufacturer partner program (e.g. RapidLED Corona integration). No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a connected-hardware / IoT lead.

providers.name: Aquaexchange
providers.description: Aquaexchange is an IT solution company focused on transforming aquaculture through innovative IoT technology and data‑driven insights. Their platform offers farmers comprehensive, affordable tools to enhance productivity, sustainability, and resource efficiency in fish and shrimp farming. Founded in 2020, Aquaexchange provides services ranging from farm monitoring to data analytics, aiming to promote smarter, sustainable farm management worldwide.

providers.name: Bug Labs
providers.description: Bug Labs is a New York City enterprise software company founded in 2006, first as one of the earliest open-source modular hardware makers and later as an enterprise IoT platform provider serving Fortune 500 customers including Verizon, Comcast, VMware, Ford, Charter and Orange. Its current flagship product, Signalpattern, targets workflow fragmentation by mapping and connecting dispersed enterprise systems, automating cross-system tasks, and letting users interact with APIs directly without writing code. Bug Labs previously operated the well-known public IoT APIs dweet.io, dweetpro.io and freeboard.io; all three are decommissioned and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation or public API today. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital and Court Square Ventures.

providers.name: Soaringtitan
providers.description: Soaringtitan provides a cloud‑based platform for managing and visualizing IoT device fleets, offering real‑time telemetry, device provisioning, and analytics dashboards. The service includes secure API access, webhook notifications, and integration with major cloud providers, enabling enterprises to monitor, control, and derive insights from their connected devices at scale.

providers.name: EchoStar
providers.description: EchoStar Corporation (Nasdaq: SATS) is a global, fully integrated communications and content delivery leader and provider of technology, spectrum, and connectivity. Through its DISH, Boost Mobile, Hughes, and EchoStar Mobile brands, EchoStar delivers satellite communications, wireless services, and IoT connectivity to consumers, enterprises, governments, and aviation customers worldwide.

providers.name: Kubota
providers.description: Kubota Corporation is a Japanese multinational manufacturing agricultural, construction, and industrial machinery, including compact tractors, excavators, mowers, utility vehicles, engines, and water and environmental infrastructure systems sold in over 120 countries. Kubota does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; equipment telematics (KubotaNOW) and dealer integrations are handled through partner channels rather than open APIs.

providers.name: Limbo
providers.description: Limbo is a direct-to-consumer digital weight-loss and metabolic-health program operated by Vitals in View, Inc., with subsidiaries in the UK (company no. 15047668) and Ireland (company no. 725671). Members wear a body-worn "energy sensor" that reads metabolic signals, and a companion app turns those readings into personalized, nudge-based guidance intended to change eating habits without calorie counting. The company is Seedcamp-backed, raised a seed round in September 2022, and is mid-rebrand from Limbo (limborevolution.com) to Viv (viv.co), with the marketing site now served from content.viv.co. Limbo publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed security posture only.

providers.name: houmo
providers.description: HOUMO.AI (后摩智能) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 that develops compute-in-memory (CIM / storage-and-computation integrated) edge AI chips for running large language models and other AI workloads on endpoint devices. Its products include the MOMAGIC (H30) series processors, LIQING M.2 modules, and Limou (LM 5050 / LM 5070 / LM 30) AI acceleration cards, paired with the Houmo Avenue software toolchain (PyTorch / TensorFlow / ONNX, CUDA-style front end) for model quantization, compilation, and deployment. The company targets edge inference, autonomous driving, embodied robotics, and intelligent mobile devices, and runs a developer community with documentation and downloads. This profile is a hardware / AI-chip vendor with a developer toolchain rather than a public web API provider; no REST/OpenAPI, OAuth, or hosted API surface was found.

providers.name: iRobot
providers.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

providers.name: Lively
providers.description: Lively provides a platform that connects wearable device manufacturers with consumers, offering tools for device management, data analytics, and user engagement. Backed by GGV Capital, the company focuses on simplifying the integration of wearables into everyday life, enabling developers to build richer experiences through robust APIs and SDKs. Their services include device provisioning, firmware updates, health data aggregation, and personalized insights, aiming to accelerate innovation in the wearable technology market.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: Argus
providers.description: Argus builds AI-powered solutions for real‑world systems, delivering intelligent analytics, automation, and decision‑making tools for enterprises. Their platform integrates machine‑learning models into IoT and industrial workflows, helping customers optimize operations and unlock new value from data.

providers.name: DataShapesAI
providers.description: DataShapes AI provides edge-native electromagnetic spectrum monitoring and AI-driven signal classification solutions for defense and security. Their platform enables real-time detection, classification, and response to RF threats directly at the tactical edge, reducing latency and eliminating the need to transmit raw data to the cloud. Built by warfighters for warfighters, DataShapes AI combines advanced RF hardware with machine learning to create custom signal libraries in seconds and deliver actionable alerts in mission.

providers.name: Jawbone
providers.description: Jawbone was a consumer electronics company known for its wearable fitness trackers and Bluetooth headsets. Founded in 1999, the company focused on integrating health and activity monitoring into everyday accessories, offering products like the Jawbone UP series and the Jambox speaker. Although it ceased operations in 2017, its legacy includes pioneering the use of motion sensors and cloud-based data analytics in personal health devices, influencing the modern wearable market.

providers.name: Omate
providers.description: Omate designs and manufactures Wearable-as-a-Service (WaaS) safety solutions built around cellular-connected smartwatches for people who need protection — seniors, children, and lone workers. Its devices (such as the O6L Pro line, marketed under the Omahome brand) combine GPS location tracking, SOS calling, fall detection, and two-way voice into a managed hardware-plus-service offering sold direct to consumers and through partners. Omate is a hardware and connected-device company; as of this profile it exposes no public developer program, API, or SDK. This entry was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with an identity and domain-security pass.

providers.name: TE Connectivity
providers.description: TE Connectivity is a global manufacturer of connectors and sensors headquartered in Galway, Ireland with operational headquarters in Berwyn, Pennsylvania. TE provides electrical connectivity and sensor solutions for transportation, industrial, and communications markets, with strong automotive Tier 1 supply relationships.

providers.name: 4DBIM
providers.description: 4DBIM is the product brand of Beijing Yunjianxin Technology Co., Ltd. (北京云建信科技有限公司), a Beijing construction-technology company founded in 2015 that commercializes Tsinghua University 4D-BIM and BIM-FM research as a full-lifecycle Building Information Modeling platform for infrastructure. Its 4DBIM Cloud data centre combines a lightweight BIM+GIS graphics engine, multi-source model fusion and IoT ingestion on a microservice architecture, packaged as Power4D (construction management), Wonder4D (operations and maintenance), Skill4D (3D work instructions) and Smart4D (smart precast beam yards), plus a BIM consulting practice. It targets municipal and "national lifeline" infrastructure — metro, bridge, highway, tunnel and utility corridors — and has raised about USD 13.7M through a Series B. The 4DBIM Cloud page markets an "API开放平台" (API open platform), but 4DBIM publishes no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract, and www.4dbim.ren is an HTTP-only marketing site.

providers.name: Ancsonic
providers.description: Ancsonic (安声科技) is a Beijing‑based technology company specializing in intelligent acoustic solutions for smart earphones, automotive, appliance and industrial applications. It offers R&D, core algorithms, manufacturing services and ODM solutions, serving global customers with advanced sound processing and acoustic design.

providers.name: Humanising Autonomy
providers.description: Humanising Autonomy is a London-based behavioural AI company that builds ethical computer-vision software to understand and predict human behaviour, providing context between people and machines. Its "Behaviour AI" platform combines novel deep learning, behavioural psychology and statistical AI to analyse existing camera and video footage across automotive & ADAS, fleet telematics, city infrastructure & planning, and health & safety use cases -- improving road safety and reducing liability. The company connects to a customer's existing cameras, platform or video footage rather than exposing a public developer API. Backed by Anthemis. NOTE: the primary website (humanisingautonomy.com) is currently unreachable / parked (HTTP 404) as of 2026-07-19, indicating the company may be inactive; this profile is reconstructed from archived (Wayback) sources -- no public API, SDK registry, or developer portal was ever published.

providers.name: Skyfri
providers.description: Skyfri is a cleantech software and hardware company headquartered in Oslo, Norway that builds an operating platform for owners and operators of solar and battery energy assets. Founded in 2021, Skyfri combines an edge-native monitoring and control device (the SSI hardware, which speaks Modbus and SCADA over isolated RS-485 ports to inverters, meters, and sensors) with a cloud platform that automates operations, maintenance, and asset performance management. The software delivers real-time data processing, operational management, weather forecasting, dynamic benchmarking, plant insights, and fault detection to monitor generation and address underperformance and equipment failure across a global portfolio of solar and battery assets. The company has offices in Denver, London, Oslo, Singapore, and Bangalore and is backed by Speedinvest. Skyfri exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; its platform is delivered as a customer application at app.skyfri.com.

providers.name: 500net
providers.description: 500net Technology Co., Ltd. (五百戶科技股份有限公司) is a Taipei-based systems integrator, founded in 2004, that combines telecommunications integration, electromechanical engineering, hardware design and custom software development into smart-building, smart-factory, smart-parking and AI+IoT platforms for enterprise clients. Its published solution set covers BA central-monitoring systems, smart property-management and parking operations, the 500net-EMS energy-management platform, carbon-footprint / ESG inventory reporting, digital twins, AMR robotics and AI/AOI inspection, integrated across heterogeneous controllers over RS-485/Modbus, wired, wireless and 4G/5G links. Work is delivered as project-based system integration for named enterprise customers; the company publishes a corporate site and an investor section but no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: EQUIPTAL
providers.description: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD operates Moedatech (معداتك), Saudi Arabia's first digital procurement and rental marketplace for heavy construction equipment, connecting contractors with verified suppliers of excavators, cranes, and trucks through RFQs, real-time bidding, and audit-ready digital contracts. Founded in Riyadh in 2020 by Ali Merie and Mansour Hmaid, the company pairs the marketplace with a telematics/fleet layer (built on Traccar GPS tracking) so equipment owners can monitor real-time asset performance. The product ships as iOS and Android apps plus a web app; there is no publicly documented developer API at this time. The company is backed by 500 Global and Plug and Play Middle East. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from the company's public web, brand (moedatech.net), and GitHub presence.

providers.name: KDDI
providers.description: KDDI Corporation is a Japanese multinational telecommunications operator headquartered in Tokyo, providing mobile, fixed-line, broadband, and enterprise ICT services. KDDI markets its consumer mobile services under the au brand, alongside UQ mobile and povo, and serves enterprise customers globally through KDDI Global and KDDI America. The company operates the KDDI Open API for Developers portal exposing inquiry-gated product APIs including the au PAY Mini App platform, an XR/MEC low-latency application API, a PPM consent management API, and an au mobile Identification Support Service for KYC/identity verification. KDDI also runs the au OPEN DEVICE DEVELOPER SITE for cellular module device certification, and a KDDI Cloud Platform Service knowledge site with developer API references for cloud infrastructure. In 2025 KDDI became an equity partner in Aduna, the GSMA/Ericsson-backed network API venture aggregating CAMARA-aligned carrier APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location) across global operators. Public OpenAPI specifications are not openly published; API access is provided through contact/inquiry workflows after partner onboarding.

providers.name: Friend
providers.description: Friend is an AI companion pendant — a sub-two-inch wearable with a microphone that pairs with a phone app and communicates back to the user via text messages rather than speech. Originally announced at $99, the product shipped (after delays) in 2025 at $129 in North America. Friend is a consumer hardware company with no public developer API, SDK, or partner program; only the consumer site, an app, and the Wikipedia / press coverage exist as references.

providers.name: I Flow
providers.description: iFlow Inc. is an energy and water solutions provider headquartered in Santa Ana, California, offering products and services for the sustainable use of vital resources including water metering and leak detection, wastewater management, gas measurement and control, thermal energy/BTU metering, and data connectivity solutions. No public developer APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: Source.dev
providers.description: Source.dev builds AI-native software tooling that helps device manufacturers develop, build, and update the operating systems that run intelligent devices such as smartphones and electric vehicles. Its platform virtualizes source access (SourceFS) to cut Android checkout-and-build times from hours to minutes, replays build steps across languages and systems for faster CI, and uses LLM-driven merging (Harmony AI / Continuous Merges) to automatically resolve conflicts when applying security patches and OS upgrades to large, long-lived codebases like AOSP. The company is a sales/demo-led platform for device makers and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface.

providers.name: Swiftlane
providers.description: Swiftlane is a San Francisco-based physical security company providing cloud-based access control and video intercom systems for multifamily residential and commercial buildings. Its touchless, mobile-first platform combines face recognition, mobile and key-card credentials, visitor PIN access, vehicle readers, smart locks, and a centralized cloud management dashboard with access logs, user management, and remote unlock. Swiftlane publishes a customer product site, a large blog, and an Intercom-hosted help center, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or webhooks; integrations are delivered through partners such as Okta, Azure, Google Workspace, and Eagle Eye.

providers.name: Vayu Robotics
providers.description: Vayu Robotics is a Palo Alto, California robotics company building AI foundation models and sensing for autonomous mobile robots. Its stack spans Vayu Drive, an end-to-end learned, sim-first foundation model for mobility; Vayu Sense, a plenoptic sensor with embodied AI for high-resolution depth perception; a Vayu Sense Development Kit bundled with NVIDIA Orin; and Vayu One, a low-cost autonomous delivery robot for last- and middle-mile delivery. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company was acquired by Serve Robotics in September 2025. Enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Vitesse
providers.description: Vitesse is a universal physical-AI platform for industrial machines, founded by the team behind Tesla's "Model 3 automation hell" fix alongside leaders from SpaceX, Siemens, and Safran. It connects any machine - Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, and legacy PLCs - through 135 native OT connectors, generates control logic from a natural-language description of a process (up to 15x faster than traditional PLC programming), and runs the full stack at the edge on purpose-built industrial controllers with no cloud required. The platform layers hardware, live data dashboards and SCADA views, interoperability, physical AI, and zero-trust OT/IT cybersecurity (NIS2 and NIST aligned) into one stack, with real-time browser-based monitoring across 800,000+ machine hours. The company traded as Full Speed Automation and renamed to Vitesse Automation after acquiring Niagara Tech; the legacy fullspeedautomation.com domain no longer resolves over TLS. Vitesse exposes a marketing website and a login-gated product application at app.vitesse.dev; as of August 2026 it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL specification, SDK, webhooks, developer portal, or pricing page, and serves no /.well-known discovery documents.

providers.name: Aixinsemiconductortechnology
providers.description: Axera Semiconductor Co., Ltd. (Aixin Semiconductor Technology) is a global leader in AI inference SoC solutions, delivering high‑performance perception and computing platforms for on‑device computing, edge AI inference, and smart vehicles. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in February 2026, the company focuses on advanced edge and terminal‑side AI technologies, serving industries such as smart vehicles, vision, and edge AI chips.

providers.name: AltoTech Global
providers.description: AltoTech Global is a Bangkok-based energy-management technology company building an AI and IoT (AIoT) platform that optimizes energy consumption and reduces carbon emissions across smart buildings. Its Alto CERO air-side and water-side products autonomously tune HVAC, VRF, and chiller-plant systems based on real-time occupancy and conditions, while Alto Digital Twin, Alto Multi-Property, and AltoACE deliver spatial building intelligence, centralized multi-site energy tracking, and AI-assisted facility engineering. Backed by 500 Global, AltoTech serves offices, malls, hotels, banks, and government facilities across Southeast Asia to help accelerate the net-zero economy.

providers.name: FogHorn Systems (Johnson Controls)
providers.description: FogHorn Systems was a Sunnyvale, California developer of edge AI and machine learning software for the industrial and commercial Internet of Things (IIoT). Its Lightning Edge AI platform and Lightning EdgeML brought real-time streaming analytics and ML inference to constrained on-premises edge hardware for predictive maintenance, machine optimization, and operational intelligence use cases. Johnson Controls acquired FogHorn in January 2022 and folded its team and technology into the OpenBlue suite of smart, autonomous building solutions, with the former Sunnyvale headquarters operating as a Johnson Controls "AI Hub." FogHorn no longer operates as a standalone brand and publishes no independent public developer surface — no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization resolve as of this enrichment pass; the former foghorn.io/foghorn.ai domains are parked. This profile is retained as a network company record with no public API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Infiot
providers.description: Infiot was a secure access service edge (SASE) and intelligent edge networking startup that combined SD-WAN, zero trust network access (ZTNA), security service edge, and cloud-delivered edge intelligence into a single-vendor, AI-driven service for connecting branch, remote, and IoT sites. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Netskope in August 2022 and its technology was folded into Netskope's Borderless SD-WAN and Converged Access product line. Infiot no longer operates an independent brand, developer portal, API reference, or public API host; the former infiot.com domain now 301-redirects to Netskope's Converged Access product page, so there is no standalone API surface to enrich. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio lead with its acquisition status recorded.

providers.name: North
providers.description: North (formerly Thalmic Labs) was a wearable-computing hardware company founded in 2012 in Kitchener, Ontario by University of Waterloo graduates Stephen Lake, Matthew Bailey, and Aaron Grant. It first shipped the Myo gesture-control armband, which read electrical muscle activity to wirelessly control computers and other devices, and later pivoted to Focals, consumer smart glasses with a heads-up display. A Y Combinator Winter 2013 company that raised over $140M, North was acquired by Google in January 2020 and wound down; its products and consumer-facing website (bynorth.com) were discontinued. This profile is retained as a network record. North published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Parstream
providers.description: ParStream was a big-data analytics database company founded in 2011 in Cologne, Germany by Michael Hummel, Joerg Bienert and Norbert Heuber. Its columnar, GPU-accelerated OLAP database was built for Internet-of-Things environments, filtering and analyzing billions of records in sub-second time at the edge of the network, with query access via SQL and a JSON query format plus a C++ API for user-defined query nodes. Cisco acquired ParStream on October 26, 2015 and folded the team into its Data and Analytics Group; the standalone product was declared obsolete and retired in 2018. The former parstream.com domain now redirects to a Cisco end-of-life product page, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or discovery surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: PayRange
providers.description: PayRange is a fintech company providing cashless commerce and self-service retail technology for unattended machines. Its platform enables mobile payments, age and identity verification, and access control across laundromats, vending, car washes, campgrounds, hospitality, micro-markets, coffee, and transit ticketing. Hardware includes the BluKey family, BluCheck, and PayStation, paired with a consumer mobile app and an operator Business Management Suite. Backed by GV and Matrix Partners. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment; integrations appear to run through direct partner and licensing channels.

providers.name: Qnovia
providers.description: Qnovia, Inc. is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical and drug-device company developing inhaled therapeutics built on its proprietary RespiRx aseptically pre-filled, portable vibrating-mesh nebulizer platform. Its lead asset, the RespiRx Nicotine Inhaler (QN-01), is a prescription smoking-cessation therapy that cleared FDA IND review and has dosed patients in a U.S. Phase 1 study; a cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) program is advancing toward a second IND. The device is Bluetooth Low Energy connected and pairs with Neblit AI, a cloud-connected companion app and machine-learning platform that tracks dose events and delivers behavioral interventions, which the company positions as a digital therapeutic layer over the pharmacotherapy. Founded in 2018 as Respira Technologies and rebranded to Qnovia in 2022, the company is led by founder and CEO Mario Danek, operates R&D and manufacturing in Newport Beach/Irvine, California and an R&D facility in Richmond, Virginia, and has raised roughly $50 million to date. Qnovia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable contract; its corporate site is a client-rendered single-page application whose only HTTP API is a private backend serving its own contact, careers and investor-portal forms.

providers.name: AgroMatch
providers.description: AgroMatch is a Chilean agricultural technology (AgTech) platform, founded in 2018 and backed by 500 Global, that connects farmers, agricultural contractors, and machinery owners in a single collaborative marketplace. Often described as the "Airbnb of agricultural machinery," it lets machinery owners lease idle equipment (tractors, implements, portable bins) during low-use periods to farmers in regions whose seasons do not coincide, and lets farmers contract or offer agricultural services such as harvesting, soil preparation, and crop applications. The platform also supports buying and selling new and used machinery, operative leasing, and supplier networking, using artificial intelligence and IoT to match demand for machinery with available supply. AgroMatch reports more than 400 B2B customers across Chile and Perú with operations extending to the US, Colombia, and Mexico. The company operates as a web and mobile application at app.agromatch.cl; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: AliciaBots
providers.description: AliciaBots is a maritime robotics company, backed by Techstars, that builds autonomous robot teams for cleaning and inspecting ship hulls. Its flagship Roverclean robot operates independently to remove marine growth and monitor hull condition in real time without interrupting a vessel's voyage, using self-learning adaptive systems, precision cleaning, and remote monitoring and control to improve fuel efficiency and help operators meet IMO regulatory standards. AliciaBots does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks the company as a network lead.

providers.name: Atom Semiconductor
providers.description: Atom Semiconductor (Atom Semiconductor Technologies Limited) is a fabless mixed-signal chip design company founded in Hong Kong in October 2020, with offices in Shenzhen and Shanghai. It designs high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for consumer and industrial IoT systems across three product lines: digital sensor chips (temperature/humidity, pressure, optical), analog-to-digital converters (24-bit Sigma-Delta, high-precision SAR, and high-speed GSPS ADCs), and microprocessors. Its first product, the AS1412 24-bit Sigma-Delta ADC, shipped for customer trials in late 2021. The company raised roughly 100M yuan in a pre-A round led by Qiming Venture Partners (with Venus Medtech and Alibaba Entrepreneurs Fund) and was named to the Forbes Asia 100 To Watch 2022. It is a hardware chip designer and does not publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: GeoGrid
providers.description: Geogrid Co., Ltd. is a South Korean smart-building water technology company behind BLOS ("Building Oasis"), an integrated building-level water purification and monitoring system. BLOS delivers drinkable water from every tap using chemical-free ionization to eliminate rust, scale, and biofilm, and pairs it with real-time monitoring of water quality, usage, carbon emissions, and consumption plus predictive analytics for pipe condition, contamination risk, and filter replacement. Geogrid targets schools, hotels and resorts, public institutions, and healthcare facilities, and offers a BLOS Care membership service. The company is based at Seoul Startup Hub Seongsu, holds 21 registered patents, and has been recognized with venture certification, ESG awards, and selection as a Korean representative for WSA 2026. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Homebridge
providers.description: Homebridge is an open-source platform that enables you to integrate non‑Apple devices with Apple HomeKit, allowing users to control a wide range of smart home accessories through Siri, the Home app, or automations. It acts as a lightweight Node.js server that bridges various plugins to expose devices as HomeKit accessories, supporting extensive customization and community‑driven extensions.

providers.name: Kraftful
providers.description: Kraftful is a startup focused on providing a platform for managing smart home devices and IoT integrations. The company offers APIs that enable developers to connect, control, and monitor a variety of connected products, aiming to simplify the creation of unified smart home experiences. Backed by leadout-capital, Kraftful targets both consumer and enterprise markets, delivering tools for device onboarding, state synchronization, and automation workflows.

providers.name: Nofence
providers.description: Nofence is a Norwegian agritech company (founded 2011, headquartered in Batnfjordsøra, Norway) that produces the world's first commercial virtual fencing system for livestock. Solar-powered GPS collars worn by cattle, sheep and goats keep animals inside virtual pastures that farmers draw on a map, with the collar teaching animals boundaries through audio cues before a mild electric pulse. The system is operated entirely from a mobile app (iOS and Android) and a web portal, communicating over GPS and the cellular network with no base stations or buried wire. Farmers get real-time animal location, boundary/escape push notifications, herd replay, grazing-history and multi-species management. Nofence is a consumer/farmer-facing product: as of this profile it publishes a mobile app and web portal but no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface. It is a portfolio company of Speedinvest, added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.

providers.name: OpenEyes Insurance
providers.description: OpenEyes Insurance (OpenEyes Insurance Agency, Inc.) is an Austin, Texas-based insurtech startup, with an additional New York office, that provides commercial auto insurance for truck and bus fleet operators bundled with proprietary risk-prevention technology. Its offering pairs fleet coverage with real-time driver monitoring, AI dashcams, safety analytics, customized driver training, and 24/7 claims management, serving both insurance agents (For Agents) and fleet operators directly (For Fleets). Founded by Yoav Oron (CEO), Dr. Omry Sendik (CTO), and Dan Charash (Chairman), OpenEyes emerged from stealth in February 2023 with a $23M Series A led by Insight Partners with Pitango First. The company operates a customer-facing fleet dashboard but does not publish a public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Otolith
providers.description: Otolith Labs, Inc. (trading as Otolith) is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company headquartered at 200 Massachusetts Ave NW in Washington, D.C., founded in 2015 by Sam Owen and developing a non-invasive wearable headband — the OtoBand — that applies calibrated mechanical vibration to the vestibular system, a technique the company calls non-invasive Vestibular Resonance Therapy (nVRT) or vestibular masking, to reduce the symptoms of chronic vertigo and vestibular migraine without surgery, medication, or patient-specific calibration. The device holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation, has been evaluated in clinical work spanning 600+ subjects, and is being studied for cybersickness in virtual reality. Otolith Labs is backed by Morningside Ventures, Mark Cuban Companies and a group of ENT physician investors. It is a physical medical device manufacturer: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and its only web surface is a WordPress marketing, investor and clinical-trial site.

providers.name: Augmate
providers.description: Augmate provides a mission‑driven IoT and wearable device management platform that connects employees, customers, devices and data. Their solutions enable enterprises to deploy and manage head‑mounted displays, smart glasses, and other wearables at scale across industries such as smart medicine, energy, agriculture, retail, and automotive. Augmate’s platform offers device provisioning, app distribution, data analytics, and integration via robust APIs, supporting blockchain‑enabled, protocol‑agnostic, tokenized architectures for secure IoT deployments.

providers.name: Autonomic
providers.description: Autonomic is a connected-vehicle cloud company founded in 2016, acquired by Ford Motor Company in 2018 and fully integrated into Ford in 2023. Its flagship product, the Transportation Mobility Cloud (TMC), is one of the largest connected-vehicle cloud platforms in production, providing an API-driven platform for developers to build applications that interact with vehicles while abstracting the complexity of different vehicle models and connectivity devices. The public developer surface (the TMC Developer Portal) is gated behind partner authentication, so most technical artifacts are not publicly harvestable. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Craft Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Axera Tech
providers.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Bsquare
providers.description: Bsquare is an IoT and edge-software company known for Windows IoT device licensing, OS consulting (Windows, Linux, Android), device management, and its DataV IoT analytics and SquareOne data platform. Bsquare was acquired by Kontron; the bsquare.com domain now 301-redirects to www.kontron-americas.com, and the Bsquare brand operates as part of Kontron's connected-device software portfolio serving healthcare, avionics, energy, manufacturing, logistics, transportation, and hospitality. No independent public developer API or documentation surface is currently published; this profile carries the honest enrichment of the domain's live security and DNS posture.

providers.name: ByteRoad, Sociedade Unipessoal Lda
providers.description: ByteRoad, Sociedade Unipessoal Lda is a technology company focused on providing innovative solutions for road safety and transportation management. It offers a platform that integrates data analytics, IoT devices, and mobile applications to help authorities monitor road conditions, manage traffic, and improve driver safety. The company aims to reduce accidents and enhance efficiency through real-time insights and automated reporting tools, serving both public and private sector clients across Europe.

providers.name: emergen
providers.description: emergen (智昌科技集团股份有限公司, Zhichang Technology Group) is a Chinese industrial intelligence company founded by Dr. Gan Zhongxue, an expert in intelligent manufacturing. Built around its proprietary "ternary control" technology and cluster (swarm) robotics, the company positions itself as "AI + Control," delivering integrated "industrial agent" solutions that install a control "brain" into individual machines, production lines, and whole factories. Its portfolio spans robot controllers, ubiquitous controllers, industrial and collaborative robots, life-science robots, GVision 2D/3D machine vision, the GSC-AI100 sense-compute-control AI controller, a swarm-intelligence network controller, a micro-control cloud platform, and the "Jiangxin" family of industrial large models (design, production, service, and management). emergen serves automotive, electronics, equipment manufacturing, steel, metallurgy, textile, furniture, and shipbuilding sectors, plus Robotics-as-a-Service. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass no public developer/API surface was found.

providers.name: petkit
providers.description: PetKit is a consumer smart pet-technology company that designs and sells connected pet-care hardware — automated feeders, smart water fountains, self-cleaning litter boxes, cameras, and health-monitoring accessories — paired with the PetKit mobile app that controls the devices over the cloud. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass, PetKit publishes no dedicated first-party developer portal or public API; petkit.com is operated as a Shopify storefront, so the only machine discoverable surface on the domain is Shopify's Customer Account OAuth/OIDC discovery documents. Third-party (community, reverse-engineered) integrations exist for the mobile-app backend but there is no officially documented API.

providers.name: Lexmark International
providers.description: Lexmark International is a global imaging and IoT solutions leader that helps customers worldwide realize the full potential of their information through printers, multifunction devices, and managed print services. As of 2024, Lexmark was acquired by Xerox Holdings Corporation. Public developer APIs are not currently advertised through an open developer portal.
